It does not establish work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special-document, restricted-area, security, or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Namibian citizen: outside foreign-visitor visa requirement
policies.summary: The Immigration Control Act's ordinary entry rule expressly excepts a person proved to be a Namibian citizen from the foreign-visa requirement.
conditions: This classification only records the statutory exception to the foreign-visitor visa requirement. It does not decide documentary proof, a dual national travelling on another passport, departure controls, security screening or individual admission matters.
The Act permits the Minister to make or withdraw category exemptions and does not displace other immigration-control powers.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free holiday visitors
policies.summary: The current MHAISS Visa Fact Sheet expressly places this all-passport cohort on its holiday visa-exemption list under the 1 April 2025 reciprocity framework.
conditions: The fact sheet describes this as holiday travel and lists all passport types; this policy only normalizes the catalog's ordinary passports. It establishes neither work, residence, business-only, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee nor other special-document treatment.

A visitor permit issued at entry may not exceed 90 days in a calendar year. The FAQ requires a valid passport (normally six months; two clean pages for the general tourist list), accommodation or invitation evidence, funds, itinerary/onward evidence, insurance and any child documents; admission remains discretionary.
The online Visa-on-Arrival portal may offer a voluntary application to an otherwise exempt traveller. It is not a required ETA or visa and does not displace this direct exemption.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa on arrival
policies.summary: MHAISS's current named schedule says this cohort may obtain a visa on arrival, while allowing an optional pre-departure eVisa. Because a border-issuance route is directly available, it is normalized as visa_on_arrival rather than evisa.
conditions: This is the MHAISS named non-exempt cohort. It can obtain an arrival visa or, optionally, an eVisa before travel; the latter optional alternative does not convert the direct arrival route into evisa for this taxonomy.

The visitor route is for holiday/tourist travel. The FAQ sets a visitor-entry permit ceiling of 90 days in each calendar year, allows an extension application before expiry, and requires the ordinary visitor documents, funds, accommodation/invitation, onward itinerary and insurance. A VOA applicant needs a passport valid at least six months and three clean pages.

VOA is only at designated ports. The FAQ lists Hosea Kutako airport, Ariamsvlei, Impalila, Katima Mulilo, Mohembo, Ngoma, Noordoewer, Oshikango, Oranjemund, Trans-Kalahari, Walvis Bay Harbour and Walvis Bay airport; Version 4 additionally lists Lüderitz Harbour. Recheck the operating port because current MHAISS documents disagree on that port.

The September notice said the pre-existing manual VOA fee was N$1,600 and approved an additional N$400, with implementation of the increase to be announced. Fees, security/admissibility and border-officer decisions remain variable. Work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are excluded.

application.label: Namibia online Visa-on-Arrival application
application.processingTime: The current FAQ says an online Visa-on-Arrival application takes 48 hours; an application may also be completed on arrival at a listed port.
steps: Use the MHAISS e-services route before departure if choosing the optional online Visa-on-Arrival process, or complete the arrival application at a designated port.
Present the required passport, supporting visitor documents and any approved/printed document requested by immigration.
Obtain the visa and visitor-entry permission from the immigration officer; approval or application does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Approved September 2025 additional ordinary passports: visa on arrival
policies.summary: MHAISS's approved 23 September 2025 notice expressly adds this catalog cohort to Visa-on-Arrival eligibility at designated ports. Its online e-services reference is an application for VOA, not proof of an electronically issued advance visa.
conditions: The official additional-country notice says these nationals are now eligible to obtain visas on arrival at designated ports and directs them to the e-services portal for an optional VOA application. It therefore does not establish an ETA or a mandatory pre-travel eVisa.

The FAQ visitor requirements, 90-days-in-a-calendar-year visitor-permit cap, extension-before-expiry procedure, six-month passport validity and three clean VOA passport pages apply. Carry accommodation/invitation, funds, itinerary/onward evidence, insurance and child documentation as applicable.

VOA is only at designated ports; the FAQ and Version 4 differ about whether Lüderitz Harbour is in the current set, so travellers must check the operating port. Fees were announced as subject to a later implementation notice. This excludes work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes.

application.label: Namibia online Visa-on-Arrival application
application.processingTime: The FAQ describes a 48-hour online Visa-on-Arrival application, while the notice also preserves issuance on arrival at designated ports.
steps: Choose the MHAISS online VOA application before travel or apply manually on arrival at a designated port.
Bring the required passport, supporting visitor evidence and any printed approval requested at the border.
Receive the actual visa and visitor-entry permission from immigration; entry is subject to officer assessment.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: mandatory pre-travel eVisa
policies.summary: The current MHAISS fact sheet supplies an explicit default: a passport absent from every exemption and VOA list cannot use VOA and must obtain an eVisa before travel. This is an exhaustive official complement, not inference from silence.
conditions: This residual cohort is defined only by the fact sheet's exhaustive rule: it is not on any listed exemption or VOA list, cannot apply for VOA, and must obtain an eVisa before travel. It does not support a consular-visa, VOA, ETA or visa-free alternative.

The FAQ says online visa processing is five business days and an approved eVisa must be printed for the immigration officer. The visitor permit at entry may not exceed 90 days in a calendar year; extensions are requested before expiry.

Use only gazetted entry ports and carry the general visitor passport, accommodation/invitation, funds, itinerary/onward, insurance and child documents. Work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and special-document routes are outside this ordinary visitor policy; all admission remains discretionary.

application.label: Namibia MHAISS e-services visa application
application.processingTime: The current FAQ says an online visa takes five business days; allow extra time because MHAISS may require documents or further assessment.
steps: Obtain the required eVisa through MHAISS before travelling; this cohort cannot wait to apply for a visa on arrival.
Submit the passport and supporting visitor documentation and retain the approval for travel.
Print the approved eVisa and present it with the required documents at an authorised port; entry remains subject to immigration assessment.

policies.title: Nepal: Indian ordinary passports with no visa required
policies.summary: TIA Immigration expressly says Indian citizens do not need a visa to enter Nepal.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality result only. TIA Immigration says Indian citizens may enter using a valid passport without a visa.
The source also describes voter-card and minor-document alternatives for Indian citizens without a passport; those document-specific routes are outside this ordinary-passport policy.
Does not decide residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, or case-specific entry rules.

policies.title: Nepal: ordinary passports eligible for tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Nepal's current tourist-visa guidance and TIA's exhaustive exception list support visa on arrival for all listed foreign ordinary passports except India and the twelve prior-visa nationalities.
conditions: For ordinary short-visit/tourist treatment, TIA facilitates visa on arrival; the listed twelve nationalities in the separate prior-visa policy are expressly ineligible for arrival issuance, and Indian citizens are visa-free.

DoI's online tourist form may be completed before arrival or at airport kiosks, then the traveller pays at the counter and the immigration officer issues the visa. This is arrival processing, not a nationality-wide eVisa classification.
Tourist visa-on-arrival options are 15, 30 or 90 days; tourist stay, including extensions, is subject to Nepal's stated visa-year limits and immigration determination.

SAARC nationals Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Pakistan and Sri Lanka receive a gratis visa for up to 30 days on their first visit in a visa year; this is a fee-free visa on arrival, not no-visa admission. Afghanistan remains a named arrival-visa exclusion.

China, child, NRN-card, diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, study, transit, crew, special-document and case-specific rules are not flattened into this ordinary-passport nationality result.

policies.title: Nepal: SAARC ordinary passports with fee-free tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Nepal grants these non-Indian, non-Afghan SAARC citizens a gratis visa for up to 30 days on the first visit of a visa year.
conditions: This is a fee-free tourist visa, not no-visa entry, and is limited to up to 30 days on the first visit in a given visa year.
Afghanistan is a SAARC member but is expressly ineligible for visa on arrival and is therefore excluded from this group; Indian citizens are separately visa-free.
All ordinary-passport arrival conditions and exclusions of the overlapping universal visa-on-arrival policy continue to apply.

policies.title: Nepal: ordinary passports not eligible for visa on arrival
policies.summary: TIA Immigration expressly excludes these nationalities from visa on arrival; obtain an appropriate visitor visa before travel.
conditions: TIA Immigration expressly names these nationalities as not eligible for visa on arrival. They require an appropriate visa arranged before travel through Nepal's pre-departure visa channels.

This policy does not call an online form eVisa: DoI's ordinary tourist online form is also used for counter-issued visa-on-arrival processing, and the reviewed sources do not establish an exclusive nationality-wide electronic issuance route for this group.
Does not decide diplomatic, official, service, special-document, refugee, residence, work, study, crew, transit or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: Nicaragua: named Category A ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule explicitly marks these ordinary passports Category A (exempt from visa). It is a visa-free baseline, not an ETA, eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The AIP says Category A nationals need a valid passport and admission by the migration officer at the arrival port; individual admission remains controlled.
The Tourist Card is a separate paid personal tourist document. It is not an ETA, eVisa or visa on arrival and does not change the Category A visa classification.
No duration, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health, fee-exemption or special-document rule is inferred beyond the cited sources.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: named Category B ordinary passports require consular visa
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule expressly marks these ordinary passports Category B: consular/no-consultation. The baseline is visa_required because the schedule requires a consular visa stamped before arrival, not an eVisa or ETA.
conditions: The AIP states that Category B nationals must present a passport and carry a stamped consular visa before the migration officer admits them at the arrival port.

The migration digest says a Category B visa may be issued at a migration post only under ratified instruments and migration policies. It does not identify a nationality-wide border-issued route for this cohort, so no visa_on_arrival route is inferred.
No online application, duration, fee, entries, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health or admission outcome is inferred.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: Indian ordinary passports eligible for a border-issued visa
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule uniquely marks Indian ordinary passports Category B ‘consular or border-issued’. Nicaragua’s migration law likewise describes Category B as consular-without-consultation or border visa. The border-issued route is normalized as visa_on_arrival, not eVisa or ETA.
conditions: The same ordinary-passport row also permits a consular route; this policy records the expressly available border-issued route as the nationality baseline.
The Special Tourist Card is a separate paid personal tourist document, is not an arrival visa, and is not valid for nationals subject to visa restrictions.
No online application, duration, fee, entries, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health or admission outcome is inferred.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: named Category C ordinary passports require advance consulted visa
policies.summary: The current official CA-4 AIP schedule expressly marks these ordinary passports Category C (consulted visa). It is an advance-authorization and consular route, normalized as visa_required rather than eVisa, ETA or visa on arrival.
conditions: The AIP requires the traveller or sponsor to request a Directorate-General of Migration and Foreigners endorsement through the relevant consulate before entry.

The migration digest assigns consulted visas for restricted-country nationals to the Directorate General of Migration and Foreigners; consular offices transmit applications and notification follows its decision.
The cited law gives consulted visas a 30-day validity and allows extension up to 90 days, except five-day transit visas; the actual visitor purpose, grant and admission remain case-specific.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, territorial and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: CA-4 national ordinary-passport entry
policies.summary: The official Assembly record describes the CA-4 agreement as suppressing visas and permitting each national to move among Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua. This establishes the ordinary-passport visa-free baseline for the other three CA-4 nationalities.
conditions: The source describes regional free movement; this candidate records only the ordinary-passport visa outcome, not identity-card or other document alternatives.
No tourist-card exception, duration, fee, extension, onward-travel, funds, accommodation, health or port rule is inferred for this nationality cohort.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Nicaragua: citizen entry
policies.summary: Nicaragua’s current migration digest expressly says that no Nicaraguan needs an entry visa to enter Nicaragua; this is recorded as citizenship rather than visitor visa-free access.
conditions: This is a citizenship/right-of-entry rule, not a visitor route and not an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival, Tourist Card or advance visa.
The source also addresses national document and age-specific departure rules; those are outside this ordinary-passport entry classification.

policies.title: ECOWAS ordinary passports: visa-free entry to Niger under AES declaration
policies.summary: The AES Heads of State declared that ECOWAS nationals need no visa to enter the AES space, which includes Niger. ECOWAS later reported that its members and the three AES States agreed continuing free movement pending a new agreement.
conditions: Applies only to nationals of the named ECOWAS State passport issuers holding ordinary passports for the normal visitor baseline.
AES States retain power, under national law, to refuse entry to ECOWAS nationals falling within inadmissible-immigrant categories.

The current MFA rule treats airport transit without leaving airport limits separately, and only permits a point-of-entry visa exceptionally on Interior Minister authorization for a person departing a country without a Niger mission; neither is a nationality-wide visitor route.

This policy does not decide residence administration, employment, commercial vehicle, diplomatic, official/service, refugee, laissez-passer, special-document, health, security or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: ECOWAS ordinary passports: Nigeria short-visit visa exemption
policies.summary: The current NIS landing-card portal labels ECOWAS passports Visa Free / Exemption, while the operative ECOWAS Protocol removes visa requirements for Community citizens visiting a Member State through an official entry point for up to 90 days. This policy maps the catalog's foreign ECOWAS ordinary passports.
conditions: The Protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, limits the baseline visit to 90 days, and permits Nigeria to refuse admission to an inadmissible immigrant. It does not eliminate all border, health, security or documentary checks.

Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger formally withdrew from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025. ECOWAS's current transition notice expressly continues their visa-free movement, residence and establishment rights until further notice; their status must be rechecked if that notice changes.

This maps only ordinary passports for short visitor movement. It does not normalize ECOWAS travel certificates, residence or establishment rights, employment, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or other special-document routes.
The Landing and Exit Card is an immigration declaration workflow, not an ETA or a visa. Completing it does not change this exemption.

policies.title: First-list ordinary passports: 14-day Oman visa exemption
policies.summary: The named first-list nationalities may enter Oman without an entry visa for a short stay of up to 14 days, subject to the published visitor conditions.
conditions: The traveller must hold a passport valid for at least six months, a return ticket, confirmed hotel reservation, health insurance, and sufficient funds for the stay.
The stay is limited to 14 days and cannot be extended or converted to a residence visa.

CN is limited to the Ministry’s China entry, which expressly includes Hong Kong and Macau; HK and MO represent only those named special-administrative-region entries, not a PRC travel document or another special document.
The published accompanying spouse and children facility is not a passport-nationality-wide rule for an unaccompanied traveller, and is not modelled as separate passport access.

This policy does not establish work, residence, sponsored visit, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, or other special-document treatment. Entry remains subject to border admission.

policies.title: Second-list ordinary passports: conditional 14-day Oman visa exemption
policies.summary: The named second-list nationalities may use Oman’s 14-day visa exemption only when the stated third-country-visa/residence or GCC-resident-profession condition is met.
conditions: The traveller must meet the same passport-validity, return-ticket, confirmed-hotel, health-insurance, and sufficient-funds conditions as the general 14-day exemption.

The national must either be a resident of, or hold a valid entry visa for, the United States, Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Japan, or a Schengen country; alternatively, the national may be a GCC resident in a qualifying resident-visa profession.
The stay is limited to 14 days and cannot be extended or transferred to a residence visa.
This is not unconditional visa-free access. It does not establish a nationality-wide eVisa, visa-on-arrival, employment, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, or special-document route.

policies.title: GCC citizens: Oman visa-free entry
policies.summary: Citizens of the named Gulf Cooperation Council states do not require visas to enter Oman.
conditions: This policy follows the Foreign Ministry’s GCC-citizen rule and does not state a maximum visitor stay, an employment entitlement, or treatment of GCC residents who are not GCC citizens.
GCC residents of another nationality are instead subject to the separate conditional exemption’s qualifying-profession rule.
Diplomatic, official, service, special, emergency, travel-document, residence, work, purpose, and individual-admission requirements are not established by this ordinary-passport classification.

policies.title: Maldives and Nepal ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: DGIP's current visa-abolition schedule identifies Maldives and Nepal as the only two all-national ordinary-passport visitor exemptions.
conditions: The current DGIP schedule gives Maldives nationals three months and Nepal nationals one month without a visa; an extension is required after the stated period.

This records ordinary visitor passports only. It does not establish work, residence, overseas-Pakistani origin, diplomatic/official/special document, transit, security, or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Qatar ordinary passports: direct visa on arrival
policies.summary: DGIP grants all Qatari passport holders, including ordinary passports, visa on arrival without the ETA requirement that applies to the other listed tourist-VOA nationalities.
conditions: The current DGIP page says the route is available at any port of entry, free of charge, for 30 days and extendable another 30 days, with single or multiple entries.
Requires a passport valid for at least six months, a confirmed return ticket, and cash equivalent to USD 1,500 or a valid credit card.
It does not establish work, residence, Indian-origin religious tourism, group-tour, diplomatic/official/special-document, security or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: tourist Visa Prior to Arrival / ETA
policies.summary: For these named tourist nationalities, Pakistan labels the visa as visa on arrival but requires electronic travel authorization 48-72 hours before travel. This candidate normalizes that required advance authorization as ETA rather than a true walk-up VOA.
conditions: The DGIP list names 50 tourist-VOA nationalities; Nepal and Maldives use the easier visa-free route and Qatar has the direct no-ETA VOA route recorded separately.
Submit the ETA/VPA intent 48-72 hours before travel. The arrival-issued tourist visa is up to three months under the category page.
A 2025 MFA release says the mobile-app VPA category serves eligible nationals of 120 countries but does not name them. It cannot safely expand or replace DGIP's named 50-country table.

Requires the category's passport, photograph, and sponsor invitation or hotel-booking evidence. It does not establish business-only VOA, Indian-origin religious tourism, designated-tour-operator groups, residence, work, special documents, security or individual admission.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: tourist eVisa
policies.summary: DGIP's live 175-country eVisa schedule establishes the online tourist-visa route for these passports; easier visa-free, named VPA/ETA, and direct-VOA routes above take precedence.
conditions: The official page says applicants from 175 countries can apply for eVisa and that the route is augmented with ETA; use the official online visa system before travel.
The newer MFA mobile-app release reports an unnamed 120-country VPA cohort. Because it supplies no country list, it does not safely prove an easier VPA route for any particular eVisa-only passport.

For tourist/visit travel, DGIP requires the ordinary passport, photograph, and a sponsor invitation or hotel booking. The listed standard tourist visa is up to three months with double entry and can be extended subject to the stated limits.

The policy does not establish business-only routes, overseas-Pakistani origin or family arrangements, work, residence, transit, group tourism, diplomatic/official/special documents, prohibited areas, security or individual-admissibility rights.

policies.title: List-A-only ordinary passports: advance tourist visa
policies.summary: Pakistan's current List-A schedule authorizes missions to grant these ordinary-passport holders a standard tourist visa, while they are not in the current 175-country eVisa schedule or a more favorable ordinary visitor route.
conditions: DGIP authorizes missions to grant List-A foreigners a visit/tourist visa with three months' validity and stay and double entry; use the online visa process as directed by MFA.

This policy records the ordinary tourist advance-visa baseline only. It does not establish a business, work, residence, transit, group-tour, diplomatic/official/special-document, security or individual-admissibility outcome.

policies.title: Palauan nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Immigration Division directs Palauan citizens to use a Palauan passport to enter and leave Palau; foreign-national visitor visa rules do not determine their entry.
conditions: Palau permits dual citizenship, but this classification does not determine a dual national's entry when presenting another passport or any departure, residence, security, or individual-admissibility decision.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Federated States of Micronesia, Marshall Islands, and United States ordinary passports: visa exemption
policies.summary: Palau expressly exempts citizens of the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the United States from a visa to visit, work, or reside, subject to Palauan law.
conditions: The authority states that this exemption is effective from 2 November 2022 and allows visit, work, or residence only in accordance with Palauan law. It is not a passport-wide grant of work authorisation independent of those laws.
The traveller needs a passport valid at least six months, must state the purpose of visit, and is not required to hold an onward ticket under this specific route.
This does not establish treatment of U.S. military personnel, diplomatic missions, dependants, special travel documents, or non-citizen residents; those are separate status-specific rules.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Schengen-contracting-state ordinary passports: 90-day visa waiver
policies.summary: Citizens of the named Schengen Agreement contracting states may enter Palau without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
conditions: This is the mutual Palau-European Union waiver as described by the Immigration Division. It applies to citizens of the named Schengen-contracting states; Cyprus is not added without an express current source classification.
The page does not make this tourist waiver an employment, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, or other special-document entitlement.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: 30-day visa waiver
policies.summary: Palau's Immigration Division states that the Palau-Russia mutual waiver permits Russian citizens to stay without a visa for 30 days.
conditions: This classification is limited to the stated 30-day visa waiver and does not establish work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or special-document treatment.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Taiwan ordinary passports: conditional visa waiver
policies.summary: Taiwan nationals may use Palau's bilateral visa-free arrangement when they meet the stated passport, purpose, return-ticket, and onward-destination requirements.
conditions: The waiver accepts ordinary, official, or diplomatic passports with at least six months' validity; this policy models only an ordinary passport.
The traveller must not intend to work, study, or reside in Palau, and must hold a return-flight ticket and a valid visa for the onward destination.
No stay duration is stated in this bilateral-waiver passage. Other visitor, security, admission, and special-document requirements remain separate.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Bangladesh and Myanmar ordinary passports: visitor visa before travel
policies.summary: Palau Immigration expressly says Bangladesh and Myanmar nationals must apply for a visa before reaching Palau, rather than use the ordinary visitor visa-on-arrival process.
conditions: Applicants should contact a Palau diplomatic mission, representative authority, or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs from their country of residence. The authority does not establish an eVisa or visa-on-arrival option for these ordinary passports.

Both nationalities also appear in the current flagged-country pre-clearance process. Complete applications must be submitted at least five days before travel, and incomplete submissions may lead to denied boarding or refusal of entry.

Any approval remains subject to document validity, stated purpose, accommodation, funds, onward travel, security, and the Director's assessment. Work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, or special-document routes are separate.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Flagged ordinary passports: mandatory pre-clearance before visitor visa on arrival
policies.summary: The named nationalities must obtain written Palau pre-clearance before travel; their ordinary short-visitor visa is otherwise the Immigration Division's visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: This ETA normalization represents the notice's mandatory advance pre-clearance, not an electronic visa: carriers must not board a flagged traveller without written confirmation of clearance. The visitor visa itself remains issued on arrival under the general rule.

Submit the completed pre-clearance application, Palau Entry Form submission, passport bio-page, non-refundable return ticket, accommodation proof, and sufficient-funds proof to immtravelapproval@bcbp.pw at least five days before travel.
Under the notice, entry is only for the duration on the return ticket and no more than 30 days; no extension is granted unless approved through a formal visa or permit process.
This does not classify separate invitation-based, diplomatic, medical-emergency, government-invited-delegation, work, residence, transit, crew, official, or special-document cases.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Cyprus ordinary passports: reciprocal EU–Palau visa waiver
policies.summary: The reciprocal EU–Palau agreement covers citizens of Cyprus even though Palau's live Schengen-contracting-state list omits Cyprus.
conditions: The agreement covers valid ordinary passports and short stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
Paid activity is excluded, and ordinary border-entry conditions and refusal powers remain applicable.
The treaty is controlling legal evidence for Cyprus; the Immigration page's separately worded Schengen list does not repeal or narrow it.

policies.title: Other ordinary foreign passports: 30-day tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: Palau's Immigration Division says a tourist visa may be issued on arrival to short-term genuine visitors; this explicitly bounded complement excludes every stated visa-waiver, pre-clearance, and advance-visa cohort.
conditions: The visitor must genuinely intend tourism, leisure, or a social visit and must not perform work. The initial tourist visa is 30 days and may be extended twice for 30 days each by applying at least seven days before expiry.

The traveller needs a passport valid at least six months, an onward or return ticket unless exempt, sufficient funds, and any other travel evidence or circumstances acceptable to the Director. Visa issuance and border admission remain discretionary.

Business, work, student, missionary, foreign-government/international-organization, resident, investor, dependent, diplomatic, crew, transit, emergency, refugee, stateless, official, service, and other special-document arrangements are separate and not established by this ordinary tourist classification.
Diplomats recognized by the Ministry of State and their families, and holders of a Presidential or Director exemption letter, have separate visa and onward-ticket exceptions.
All arriving passengers must have a valid passport or travel document, submit the Palau Entry Form no more than 72 hours before departure, and present its QR code at check-in and arrival.

policies.title: Paraguay: named ordinary passports visa-free for tourist entry
policies.summary: The National Migration Directorate's current country table directly marks these nationalities 'NO REQUIERE VISA' in its tourist-entry column. This is a visa exemption, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The authority’s table is used only for nationalities it explicitly names and only for its tourist-entry column. No residual status is inferred from a missing row, generic application form, agreement label or a third-country document.
Where stated in the table, the tourist stay is up to 30, 60 or 90 days; the source does not provide a single shared duration for this entire cohort, so no uniform duration is assigned.

The separate entry-requirements page retains valid travel-document, migration-registration, admission and other border conditions. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are outside this ordinary short-visitor baseline.

Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the United States are deliberately not included: the migration table says visa-free while the Foreign Ministry’s current arrival page names them for visa on arrival. Taiwan has the same cross-source disagreement. Mongolia is also excluded because the Foreign Ministry’s country-requirements page states that unlisted countries require a visa, but it does not list Mongolia.

policies.title: Paraguay: named ordinary passports visa on arrival
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry expressly says these nationalities can obtain a visa on arrival at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport without prior processing, on presentation of a qualifying passport and payment of the fee. This is visa_on_arrival, not an eVisa or ETA.
conditions: The named route is at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport and requires a passport valid for at least six months and payment of the applicable fee.

The National Migration Directorate separately marks these same nationalities as requiring a visa in its tourist-entry column; the Foreign Ministry's direct arrival-issuance page supplies the more specific route classification.

The exceptional arrival process for other visa-required nationalities requires a justified case, an inviter and advance Ministry review; it is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival entitlement and is excluded.
Work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

policies.title: Paraguay: named ordinary passports require an advance visitor visa
policies.summary: The National Migration Directorate's current tourist-entry table directly marks these nationalities 'REQUIERE VISA', except that the Foreign Ministry's current country-requirements page supplies the explicit unlisted-country visa rule for China. The Foreign Ministry describes the regular consular application and treats arrival issuance for other visa-required nationalities as exceptional and pre-approved; this is normalized as visa_required, not eVisa or a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The regular route is an online application reviewed by the relevant Paraguayan consular office, followed by the Ministry's communicated consular appointment. An online form does not establish an eVisa.

The National Migration Directorate's combined 'China/Taiwan' row cannot safely be used for the People's Republic of China code. The Foreign Ministry instead expressly lists Taiwan as visa-free and says an unlisted country requires a visa, establishing the China code's advance-visa baseline.

For a visa-required nationality other than the named no-prior-processing arrival cohort, the arrival-visa page characterizes arrival issuance as exceptional, justified and subject to Ministry process and approval. It does not replace this nationality-only advance-visa baseline.
Venezuelan nationals are specifically subject again to a visa requirement from 10 January 2026 under the Foreign Ministry notice, corroborating the current migration table.

No duration, number of entries, fee, extension, accommodation, funds, health, onward-travel or admission outcome is inferred where the authority does not state it. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and third-country-document routes are excluded.

application.label: Paraguay Foreign Ministry non-resident tourist/technical visa application
application.processingTime: The Foreign Ministry recommends applying at least 30 days before planned travel; no uniform approval time is promised.
steps: Complete the Foreign Ministry's digital visa application and upload the requested supporting documents.
Wait for the responsible Paraguayan consular office to review the application and communicate any additional documents or an interview appointment.
Obtain the visa through the regular consular process before travel; admission remains for migration authorities at the border.

policies.title: Paraguayan citizens: national return
policies.summary: The National Migration Directorate expressly accepts Paraguayan national travel documents, including an expired national travel document, for entry. The same-country ordinary-passport pair is citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa classification.
conditions: This records only the national entry function. It does not decide document issuance, dual nationality, exit requirements, customs, health, criminal process, security checks or other border formalities.

policies.title: Philippines: Philippine ordinary-passport holders
policies.summary: A valid Philippine passport is citizenship proof for Philippine arrival processing, rather than a foreign visitor-visa route.
conditions: This is a same-country citizenship normalization only; it does not determine dual nationality, passport issuance, exit controls, residence, work, transit, security, or any foreign passport held by the person.
The cited BI order also covers retained or reacquired Philippine citizens travelling with a foreign passport and specified proof; that conditional route is not inferred from a foreign passport code.

policies.title: Philippines: EO 408 30-day ordinary-passport visa-free entry
policies.summary: The current DFA eVisa policy gives these ordinary-passport nationalities visa-free temporary entry for business or tourism for up to 30 days.
conditions: For business or tourism temporary visits only, initially not exceeding 30 days.
Traveller must hold a passport valid at least six months beyond the contemplated stay and a return or onward ticket.
Brazil and Israel have the separately stated 59-day arrangement; Brunei and Cambodia are separated due to a live official-service duration conflict.
eTravel is an arrival/departure declaration that replaced cards; it is not normalized as an ETA or visa.

Does not establish admission for work, residence, study, media, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, Balikbayan/former-Filipino privilege, security clearance, deportation/blacklist, or discretionary border decisions.

policies.title: Philippines: Brazil and Israel 59-day visa-free ordinary-passport entry
policies.summary: The DFA eVisa policy states that Brazil and Israel use existing bilateral arrangements for visa-free admission of up to 59 days.
conditions: Temporary visitor entry only; the policy attributes the 59-day period to existing agreements.

Passport validity, return/onward ticket, eTravel, admissibility, purpose, extension, work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special-document, security, and blacklist rules remain applicable.
This policy does not model other document classes or special admission arrangements.

policies.title: Philippines: Brunei and Cambodia visa-free ordinary passports (duration conflict)
policies.summary: The official DFA policy page and the eVisa country-policy service both establish visa-free admission for Brunei and Cambodia ordinary passports, but publish conflicting maximum stays of 30 and 21 days.
conditions: Visa-free status is supported; do not rely on either 21- or 30-day duration without confirming the current rule with the competent Philippine border authority or a Philippine mission.
The primary eVisa policy page lists these nationalities under the 30-day EO 408 scheme. The live country-policy service, used by the same portal’s citizenship checker, says 21 days.
eTravel is a declaration, not an ETA or visa. Work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, Balikbayan, admissibility, and security remain outside the policy.

policies.title: Philippines: Indian ordinary passports visa-free for 14 days
policies.summary: Since 8 June 2025, Indian nationals have a nationality-wide 14-day visa-free temporary-visitor route; a separate 30-day route is conditional on a specified third-country visa or residence permit.
conditions: For tourism or business only, non-extendible and non-convertible, for up to 14 days.
Requires a passport valid at least six months beyond the stay, confirmed accommodation, financial-capacity proof, and return/onward ticket; the applicant must have no BI derogatory record.
The longer 30-day route is conditional on a valid American, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singaporean, or United Kingdom visa or residence permit, so it is not the code-only baseline.
Available at Philippine ports of entry; transit, long-term visits, non-tourism activities, work, residence, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, and admission discretion remain separate.
eTravel is an arrival/departure declaration, not an ETA or visa.

policies.title: Philippines: Chinese ordinary passports 14-day visa-free entry
policies.summary: The current DFA policy establishes a 14-day, non-extendible and non-convertible visa-free route for Chinese nationals for tourism and business.
conditions: For tourism or business only, up to 14 days; it is non-extendible and non-convertible.
Available only through Ninoy Aquino International Airport or Mactan-Cebu International Airport. Transit passengers need an advance Philippine transit visa before entry.
Requires a passport valid at least six months beyond the intended stay, confirmed hotel accommodation/booking, return/onward ticket, and no BI derogatory record.
The Bureau of Immigration implementation order takes effect on 16 January 2026 and remains valid for one year, through 15 January 2027 unless otherwise stated.

Complete eTravel registration is an entry requirement in the Bureau of Immigration order. It is a declaration, not an ETA or visa; work, residence, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, admission, and security rules remain separate.

policies.title: Philippines: Chinese Taipei ordinary passports visa-free for 14 days
policies.summary: FSC 2026-035 grants Chinese Taipei ordinary-passport holders a temporary 14-day visa-free visitor route through 30 June 2027.
conditions: The maximum stay is 14 days; it is non-extendible and non-convertible. A stay longer than 14 days requires an advance visa.

Available at Philippine ports of entry. The traveller must have a passport valid at least six months beyond the stay, proof of accommodation and financial capacity, a return or onward ticket, and no BI derogatory record.

The FSC expressly excludes diplomatic and official/service Chinese Taipei passports. This ordinary-passport policy does not determine MECO ETA, sticker visa, residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, or discretionary admission treatment.
eTravel is an arrival/departure declaration, not an ETA or visa.

policies.title: Philippines: Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR ordinary passports visa-free for 14 days
policies.summary: The current DFA eVisa policy gives Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport holders a 14-day visa-free temporary-visitor route.
conditions: Maximum initial stay is 14 days; the Macao-SAR route expressly requires a return or onward ticket.

This mapping is confined to Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passports. It does not cover British National (Overseas), Hong Kong British, Macao-Portuguese, other Chinese documents, or holders of residence documents.
eTravel is a declaration, not an ETA or visa. Work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, Balikbayan, security, and admission discretion remain separate.

policies.title: Philippines: other ordinary passports require an advance 9(a) visa
policies.summary: These foreign ordinary passports are outside the nationality-wide visa-free cohorts. The current DFA policy expressly classes other countries as visa-required nationals, requiring the appropriate advance visitor visa.
conditions: The ordinary visitor route is an advance Temporary Visitor 9(a) visa. The eVisa policy lists visitor categories and requirements, but does not publicly establish a nationality-wide electronic-issuance entitlement for every residual passport; this policy therefore remains visa_required, not evisa.

The official eVisa portal’s ability to issue an eVisa after its process is not treated as proof that every residual nationality has that electronic route. An online form or country checker alone is not an eVisa classification.

Passport validity, purpose, return/onward travel, accommodation, finances, clearance, fees, entries, duration, port, security, and admission are case-specific; eVisa issuance also does not guarantee admission.

Pre-arranged VUAP, cruise waiver, conditional third-country documents, Balikbayan/former-Filipino family arrangements, transit, crew, diplomatic/official/special documents, work, study, residence, and eTravel are not nationality-wide alternatives to this baseline.

application.label: Philippine eVisa portal
steps: Confirm no visa-free or document-specific exemption applies, then choose the appropriate visitor category and follow the responsible Philippine Foreign Service Post’s process.
Provide the passport and the purpose-, itinerary-, financial-, accommodation-, and other documents the authority requests; the official policy says original documents can be required.
Obtain the required advance visa before travel and complete eTravel as the separate arrival/departure declaration; issuance does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Qatari nationals: outside foreign visitor scope
policies.summary: The foreign visitor visa framework does not establish entry treatment for Qatari passport holders.
conditions: This does not determine dual-national, resident, departure, identity-document or individual admission treatment.

policies.title: GCC citizens: no visa required
policies.summary: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia and UAE nationals may visit Qatar without a visa on the current Hayya/Qatar Tourism guidance.
conditions: The guidance says GCC nationals need a passport or GCC ID. This policy is nationality-based and does not establish the separate GCC-resident or accompanying-person Hayya routes for other passports.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: arrival-issued visitor waiver or visa
policies.summary: The current Qatar Tourism passport wizard places these nationalities in arrival-entry paths. Although Qatar Tourism now calls the former free visa-on-arrival route “visa-free”, MOI describes on-arrival visas and passport stickers; this operational category is normalized as visa_on_arrival.
conditions: Passport-level routes vary: some are free arrival waivers, while IR, MU, ME, TW, PK, TH and UA are displayed with paid and/or Discover Qatar hotel-reservation arrival routes. Hayya A1/A2/A3 may be an advance alternative where the wizard says so; optional online processing does not replace an available arrival status.

Current MOI guidance requires a passport valid at least three months, onward/return ticket and compulsory health insurance for on-arrival visitors; particular routes also require a hotel booking, Discover Qatar booking, cash/card or fees. Check the live selector for the exact passport route and duration.

The older MOI 90-day schedule publishes six-month passport validity, onward ticket and a passport sticker; its duration lists do not exactly match the current Qatar Tourism selector. Treat the individual live selector and border decision as controlling.

A residence in GCC, or residence/valid visa in Schengen, UK, US, Australia, New Zealand or Canada, can create distinct document-conditioned A2/A3 routes. It is not a nationality-wide rule. Transit, Qatar-Oman joint visas, employment, residence, diplomatic/official, temporary travel documents and special cases are separate.

policies.title: Other passport codes listed by the visa wizard: advance Hayya eVisa
policies.summary: For these ordinary-passport codes, the current Qatar Tourism selector directs an A1 Entry Visa through Hayya rather than an arrival route. It is normalized as evisa.
conditions: Apply for the A1 Entry Visa through Hayya before travel; the selector states that a hotel reservation is required during application and visa fee is payable after approval.

The eVisa route is for tourism and remains subject to passport, accommodation, insurance, funds, health, security and admission requirements. It does not create work, residence, transit, diplomatic/official or special-document rights.

application.label: Hayya Tourist E-Visas
steps: Select the appropriate A1 visitor route in Hayya before travel.
Provide the required hotel reservation and other requested travel documentation, then complete payment after approval as instructed.
Carry the approved electronic visa and supporting documents; admission remains subject to Qatar border control.

policies.title: Previously unmapped ordinary passports: Hayya Tourist Visa (A1)
policies.summary: The current Hayya country eligibility records expose the Tourist Visa (A1) for these ordinary-passport nationalities. It is an advance electronic tourist visa issued in the Hayya app or by email.
conditions: Apply for Tourist Visa (A1) through Hayya before travel. It is single-entry, non-refundable and non-transferable; the current country records state a QAR 100 fee payable upon final approval, subject to any stated exemption.

The Hayya steps require the selected visa, a passport and personal photograph, personal-information validation, accommodation confirmation, and payment; the issued eVisa is received in Hayya or by email.

The route is for tourism or leisure and remains subject to its passport, accommodation, insurance, funds, health, security, purpose and final-admission requirements. It does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, temporary-document or special-case treatment.
For XK, Hayya's current country list calls its UN record Kosovo and separately labels XK as Eswatini. This policy maps only the explicitly named Kosovo record to the project's XK passport code.

application.label: Apply for Qatar Hayya Tourist Visa (A1)
steps: Select Tourist Visa (A1) in Hayya before travel.
Upload the passport, photograph and requested accommodation information, then validate the application and complete payment.
Receive the approved electronic visa through Hayya or email and carry the required supporting documents for border admission.

policies.title: Foreign CEMAC ordinary passports: Republic of the Congo short-visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: CEMAC’s current Commission material confirms effective visa-free movement for its Member-State citizens. The five foreign CEMAC passports are mapped to visa-free admission to the Republic of the Congo. The published common convention describes a three-month tourist rule and document conditions, while the Republic of the Congo’s foreigner law otherwise preserves particular immigration agreements and does not establish a named residual route.
conditions: Applies to nationals holding ordinary passports of the five other current CEMAC Member States: Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea.

The published CEMAC common convention describes tourist free movement for up to three months and requires the community traveller to produce a valid or recently expired national identity card or passport and an international health booklet. The current Commission interview confirms visa-free movement but does not independently restate the duration; verify the convention’s continuing implementation before relying on that limit.

It does not establish a right to work, long-term residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, crew, refugee or other special-document treatment. Entry remains subject to the applicable border, health, public-order, security and admissibility controls.
No current source reviewed establishes that an eVisa project, an online service, or case-specific arrival facilitation is an alternative nationality-wide route for this policy.

policies.title: Rwanda: universal ordinary-passport visa on arrival
policies.summary: DGI states that citizens of every country may receive a visa on arrival without applying before travel.
conditions: Applies to foreign ordinary-passport holders visiting Rwanda where nationality is the only modelled basis.

DGI states citizens of all countries may obtain a visa on arrival without prior application; its online and diplomatic pre-departure application routes are optional alternatives, not a nationality-wide eVisa requirement.
A genuine, acceptable travel document valid for at least six months, vaccination requirements, sufficient funds and final immigration-admissibility assessment remain required.
DGI describes fee-free arrival visas or passes for some regional, organisation-member and named-nationality cohorts; a fee waiver does not establish no-visa admission.
Does not decide citizenship, residence-based access, work, study, long-stay, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document or case-specific entry rules.

policies.title: Rwanda: named ordinary passports with fee-waived 90-day arrival visas
policies.summary: DGI grants these named nationalities a 90-day visa free of charge upon arrival; the entry instrument remains a visa.
conditions: DGI names these nationalities for a 90-day visa free of charge upon arrival.
The source still describes a visa granted upon arrival. This is a fee-waived visa-on-arrival policy, not visa-free/no-visa admission.
The universal ordinary-passport visa-on-arrival conditions, admission checks and excluded purposes or documents continue to apply.

policies.title: Schedule 4 named ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: Saint Lucia’s current Revised Laws Schedule 4 directly exempts the named country nationals, including the non-Haitian CARICOM cohort. Singapore is exempt only for stays under 15 days.
conditions: Applies to the expressly named passport issuers and the named non-Haitian CARICOM foreign-member cohort only.
Singapore is visa-free only for stays of less than 15 days.
Haiti is expressly excluded by Schedule 4’s temporary visa-requirement carve-out.
The statutory waiver does not establish citizenship, residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Covered EU ordinary passports: reciprocal short-stay visa-free access
policies.summary: The official Government notice states that the EU–Saint Lucia agreement gives EU citizens the identical reciprocal short-stay visa-free rights. The named 26 covered EU States supplement Schedule 4.
conditions: Valid ordinary passports only; stay may not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.
Paid activity is excluded and ordinary border, health, security and admissibility controls continue to apply.
Ireland and the United Kingdom are outside this agreement; their treatment is separately stated in Schedule 4.

policies.title: Brazilian ordinary passports: reciprocal short-stay visa-free access
policies.summary: Brazil’s Foreign Ministry treaty record identifies the reciprocal ordinary-passport short-stay waiver with Saint Lucia as in force from 14 January 2024. It is easier than the older Schedule 2 arrival-visa entry.
conditions: The bilateral instrument is limited to holders of ordinary passports and is recorded by Brazil’s Foreign Ministry as in force from 14 January 2024.
The reviewed treaty record does not state a duration, purpose, paid-activity, admission, document or route rule; the agreement and Saint Lucian immigration controls still govern those details.

Schedule 2 still lists Brazil for a visa that may be issued on arrival. The later in-force reciprocal waiver is used as the easier route; the unreconciled domestic schedule is a material recheck risk.
This is not a citizenship, residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual-admissibility rule.

policies.title: Schedule 2 named ordinary passports: visa may be issued on arrival
policies.summary: The current Revised Laws expressly place these named nationalities in Schedule 2, under which the visa may be obtained on arrival.
conditions: The statute says the visa may be issued on arrival; entry is not guaranteed and immigration, document, health, security and admissibility requirements remain applicable.
Brazil is excluded because the in-force bilateral ordinary-passport waiver is the easier route. Georgia is excluded because its published waiver material lacks an entry-into-force date.
This policy does not establish eVisa, ETA, work, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: Schedule 3 named ordinary passports: visa required before arrival
policies.summary: The current Revised Laws expressly require these named nationalities to obtain a visa before arrival.
conditions: An advance visa is required under Schedule 3; it is not an eVisa or an unconditional visa-on-arrival route.
The current external-affairs service describes an application workflow and a case-specific airport possibility, not a nationality-wide electronic or arrival alternative to this Schedule 3 rule.
This policy excludes citizenship, residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document and individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Samoa: free Visitor’s Permit on arrival for foreign ordinary passports
policies.summary: Samoa Immigration says foreign nationals without Samoan citizenship or temporary residence receive a free Visitor’s Permit when they arrive, subject to entry requirements.
conditions: Ordinary-passport short-visit classification only. Samoa Immigration states a destination-wide rule for foreign nationals who do not hold Samoan citizenship or a valid Temporary Resident Permit.

The Visitor’s Permit is issued upon arrival and is therefore normalized as visa on arrival, even though it is free and a Samoa Tourism Authority page describes short visits as not requiring an entry permit in advance.

Current Samoa Immigration guidance states 90 days. The Samoa Tourism Authority page still states less than 60 days; travellers should verify the permitted duration with Samoa Immigration because the official pages conflict.

Entry requires a return or onward ticket, a passport valid for at least six months after intended departure, permission for the onward destination, accommodation details and evidence of sufficient funds.
Grant remains subject to health, character, deportation-record, warning-list and immigration-clearance requirements and is not automatic admission.
Does not decide residence, employment, study, longer visits, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document, American Samoa territorial-national, emergency or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: CPLP, EU, United States and Canada ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: Article 25(1)(e) of the published foreign-citizens regime exempts citizens of current CPLP and EU members, the United States and Canada from a visa. This policy maps only the ordinary-passport component of those citizenship categories.
conditions: Law No. 5/2015 names the citizenship groups but does not state an ordinary-passport document subtype, a visitor purpose, or a per-nationality stay period. The current Foreign Ministry brief says waivers are generally 15 days and sometimes 30 or 90 days, but supplies no country-to-duration crosswalk; no duration is asserted here.

A valid recognized travel document, border examination, financial means, accommodation, return/onward evidence, health requirements, security checks and individual admission remain separate. The law and brief do not establish work, residence, study, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency, stateless or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Current Foreign Ministry named visa-waiver partners: visa-free entry
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry's current mobility brief expressly names these additional nationalities within São Tomé and Príncipe's visa-waiver agreements. It is recorded separately because the brief does not publish each underlying agreement or its ordinary-passport detail.
conditions: The current Foreign Ministry brief calls these visa-waiver agreements and says exemptions are generally 15 days, with 30 or 90 days for some states; it does not provide an agreement-by-agreement duration, passport-type, purpose or effective-date crosswalk.

This policy therefore records the named current visa-waiver outcome only for the catalog's ordinary passports, with medium confidence. It does not establish a universal waiver, eVisa, visa on arrival, work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency, stateless or other special-document route. Border admission remains discretionary.

policies.title: Saudi nationals: outside foreign visitor scope
policies.summary: Saudi citizens do not receive a foreign visitor-entry classification when travelling on an ordinary Saudi passport.
conditions: This does not determine a dual national’s treatment when presenting another passport, nor any case-specific exit, security or border requirement.

policies.title: Current nationality-wide ordinary-passport visa-on-arrival cohort
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget places these passport nationalities in groups that offer both eVisa and visa on arrival. Under the easiest-access taxonomy, the direct arrival route is visa_on_arrival.
conditions: The live widget offers either an eVisa or a visa on arrival. For arrival issuance, it directs the traveller to a self-service KIOSK or passport-control office at the Saudi entry point.

The widget states that both eVisa and visa on arrival may be single- or multiple-entry. Multiple entry is valid for one year and allows no more than 90 consecutive days; single entry is valid for three months and allows no more than 90 consecutive days.

Visitors must have a passport valid at least six months beyond entry, except that US citizens may enter while the passport remains valid. Travellers under 18 may need to travel with a parent, grandparent, or adult sibling.

Tourism and Umrah are within the visitor materials; work, study, residence, Hajj, transit, crew, diplomatic, special-document and other purpose routes are outside this ordinary-passport visitor classification. Umrah permits may be required through Nusuk.
Approval or arrival issuance does not guarantee admission; border, security, document and local-law requirements remain applicable.

The older eVisa terms and portal lists are not fully concordant with the live widget. The live route API is used for route precedence; Brazil remains unresolved because it appears on an older public list but is noneligible in the current widget.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passport: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget explicitly says Russian passport holders need no visa or prior application, confirming that the December 2025 agreement is operational.
conditions: The widget says a valid Russian passport permits entry on arrival without a visa or prior application, with no visa, exemption or medical-insurance fee.
The limit is up to 90 days in a calendar year, in one continuous stay or across visits, for tourism, leisure, business visits and Umrah.

Work, study, residence, Hajj, transit, crew, special-document and case-specific entry treatment are outside this ordinary-passport short-visitor classification. Umrah permits may be required through Nusuk.

The older eVisa terms still list Russia as eVisa-eligible; the current live country group and route content expressly identify visa exemption and are preferred. Admission remains subject to border and security requirements.

policies.title: GCC nationals: visa-free entry
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget says GCC nationals do not need a visa and may travel using an ID or passport.
conditions: This policy covers ordinary passport holders from the five other GCC member states; the Saudi citizen pair is classified separately as citizenship.

The widget permits travel using an ID or passport. This record concerns ordinary passports and does not resolve residence, work, study, Hajj, transit, crew, special-document or case-specific treatment.
Admission remains subject to border, security, document and local-law requirements.

policies.title: Group D nationalities: advance embassy or consulate visa
policies.summary: The live Saudi Tourism Authority visa-regulations widget places these nationalities in Group D and presents only the Embassy/Consulate/Tasheer visitor-visa route, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The widget requires an embassy, consulate, or Tasheer visa application, including the stated residence proof, return ticket, employment proof, financial-solvency evidence, flight itinerary, identification and Saudi residence address.
Entry count, duration and approval are determined by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the widget describes a multiple-entry visitor visa as valid for one year and stays up to 90 days.

This record does not establish eVisa, visa-on-arrival, transit, work, study, residence, Hajj, crew, diplomatic, special-document or case-specific treatment. Border and security checks remain applicable.

policies.title: Swiss SEM short-stay visa exemption for listed national passports
policies.summary: SEM List 1 marks each listed nationality as not requiring a visa for a stay of up to 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary/national passport scope only; the SEM table's document and V1 annotations remain controlling.
Short stays only: the table column is for stays of up to 90 days; longer stays are separately marked visa-required.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, refugee, crew, transit, residence, work, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Swiss SEM Nauru short-stay visa requirement
policies.summary: SEM List 1 marks Nauru as visa-required for stays of up to 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary/national passport scope only, subject to the SEM table's travel-document annotations.
Short stays only: this is the up-to-90-day column, not transit or a long-stay residence decision.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, residence, family, humanitarian, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Norwegian statutory Annex 5 visa-free-state list
policies.summary: Annex 5 expressly lists the named states as visa-free for entry to Norway.
conditions: Applies only to nationals on the current statutory visa-free-state list, whose stated reference date is 14 August 2025.
The Immigration Act limits the total Schengen stay for visa-exempt entrants to three months in six months.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, asylum, work, document, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Norwegian statutory Nauru visa requirement
policies.summary: Nauru is absent from the complete statutory visa-free-state list, while the Immigration Act imposes a visa requirement unless regulations except it.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality result derived from the current complete Annex 5 list and the Act's default visa rule.
The Act separately exempts holders of qualifying Schengen residence permits and recognizes valid Schengen visas.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, asylum, work, document, family, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Liechtenstein's SEM-referred short-stay visa treatment for listed national passports
policies.summary: Liechtenstein's competent authority directs visa-requirement checks to Swiss SEM and states that the two countries generally share entry regulations.
conditions: The Liechtenstein authority expressly directs visa-requirement enquiries to SEM; SEM List 1 marks these national passports visa-free up to 90 days.
Liechtenstein states its rules are generally/largely the same and reserves bilateral or multilateral deviations; this policy is therefore not unconditional.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, work, family, document, territorial, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Liechtenstein's SEM-referred Nauru short-stay visa treatment
policies.summary: Liechtenstein's competent authority directs visa-requirement checks to Swiss SEM, whose List 1 marks Nauru visa-required up to 90 days.
conditions: The Liechtenstein authority expressly directs visa-requirement enquiries to SEM; SEM List 1 marks Nauru visa-required up to 90 days.
Liechtenstein states its rules are generally/largely the same and reserves bilateral or multilateral deviations; this policy is therefore not unconditional.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, work, family, document, territorial, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: EU visa-list Regulation: Nauru exemption remains conditional on a future agreement
policies.summary: The current Regulation lists Nauru in Annex II with a footnote that makes an exemption conditional on entry into force of an agreement still to be concluded with the EU.
conditions: Ordinary-passport short-stay result only, for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
The result follows the current Nauru Annex II footnote; it is not a conclusion about a future agreement or its possible effective date.
Article 6 permits Member State exceptions for specified categories, including diplomatic, service, special, crew, school, refugee, and paid-activity cases; those are out of scope.
Does not determine transit, residence, family-free-movement, territorial, document, asylum, humanitarian, or case-specific entry treatment.

policies.title: Category A ordinary passports: Senegal visa exemption
policies.summary: Senegal's current detailed consular schedule places these ordinary passports in Category A or its reciprocal visa-exemption arrangements. ECOWAS and temporary AES movement rules directly support the Community portion, while the schedule names the five additional ordinary-passport reciprocal exemptions.
conditions: For Community citizens, the ECOWAS Protocol requires a valid travel document and international health certificate, permits a short visit of up to 90 days through an official entry point, and preserves Senegal's right to refuse an inadmissible immigrant.

BF, ML and NE are the AES States. The current detailed Category A schedule expressly continues their visa exemption until further notice; the remaining mapped Community passports are covered by the Category A schedule.

The current consular schedule separately names CF, CG, MA, MU and TN as ordinary reciprocal visa-exemption countries. It requires a valid passport, repatriation guarantee/return or onward ticket, and health certificate as applicable.
The 2026 Foreign Ministry health notice says the vaccination card is not mandatory for entrants not arriving from epidemic/endemic-country situations; changing public-health controls may still apply.

This excludes residence, employment, study, transit, refugee status, diplomatic, service, official and mission-based document treatment. Official passports and ordinary passports on official mission have distinct conditional exemptions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Senegal advance consular visa
policies.summary: Senegal's current detailed consular schedule states that Category B requires a visa without mandatory Interior consultation, Category C requires prior Interior authorisation, and every passport absent from the lists follows Category C. This is an explicit complete advance-visa default, not inference from application availability.
conditions: Category B still requires a visa but has optional Interior consultation. Category C requires an authorisation of entry issued after application to the Ministry of the Interior; passports absent from all lists are expressly subject to the same Category C conditions.

The consular authority says the visa is issued by Senegalese diplomatic or consular authorities. This supports visa_required rather than evisa, visa_on_arrival or ETA; no current official source reviewed establishes a nationality-wide electronic or airport-issuance visitor alternative for this residual cohort.

Required materials vary by category but include passport validity of at least six months, visa form, photos, return/onward or repatriation evidence, accommodation and health documentation. Category C applicants are advised to apply two months in advance.

The current Foreign Ministry overview, retained from the 2015 regime, lists a materially broader visa-free cohort (including many European and other passports) than the detailed Category A/B/C page. The latter is used because it contains the post-2025 AES treatment and explicit Category C default; the conflict is a material review risk.

Work, residence, study, transit, refugee, diplomatic, official, service and official-mission exceptions are excluded. Issuance and entry remain subject to individual security, health and immigration assessment.

policies.title: Seychellois nationals: outside foreign visitor-entry scope
policies.summary: The visitor permit and foreign-visitor Travel Authorisation framework does not establish entry requirements for Seychellois nationals travelling on a Seychelles passport.
conditions: This classification does not establish the departure-form, carrier, document, dual-nationality, permit-holder, or admission treatment of a particular Seychellois national.
The Electronic Border System separately describes an Embarkation Information Form for Seychellois citizens and permit holders leaving Seychelles; it is not a visitor ETA classification.

policies.title: All foreign ordinary passports: no visa, mandatory pre-travel ETA and visitor permit on arrival
policies.summary: Seychelles does not require an entry visa regardless of nationality and issues the Visitor's Permit on arrival, but every foreign ordinary visitor must first obtain a Travel Authorisation/ETA before departure. The mandatory pre-travel authorization is normalized as eta.
conditions: Seychelles' Immigration guidance expressly distinguishes a no-visa system from the mandatory pre-departure Electronic Travel Authorisation. For this repository's access taxonomy, the live mandatory ETA is the operative entry status and supersedes an otherwise visa_free label; it does not turn the Visitor's Permit into a visa on arrival or an eVisa.

The Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival, initially for up to three months and free for that first period. It may be extended in successive periods of up to three months to a maximum of twelve months if the visitor continues to meet the conditions; each extension costs SCR 5,000.

A visitor must not be a prohibited immigrant or already hold a permit entitling residence; must have a valid return/onward ticket, confirmed accommodation and sufficient funds. Immigration's general entry guidance states a minimum of US$150 or equivalent per day.

The visitor route covers holiday, pleasure, business, and visits to friends/family. It does not permit paid or unpaid full-time or part-time work by a non-Seychellois; a Gainful Occupation Permit is separate. Residence, student, dependant, international-trade-zone, crew, maritime, diplomatic, transit, refugee, alien-document, laissez-passer, and other special-document cases are not established by this ordinary visitor policy.

A valid passport or other Seychelles-recognised travel document is required and must remain valid through the intended stay and return to the country of origin/residence. A yellow-fever certificate is required only for a traveller resident in, recently visiting, or transiting more than 12 hours through a listed endemic-risk country.

Use the Seychelles e-Border app or seychelles.govtas.com before departure.
