policies.summary: Although the country list calls these nationalities exempt from a visitor visa, DIPS expressly issues the tourist visa to them upon arrival.
conditions: This is an arrival-issued tourist visa, not true no-visa admission: DIPS says exempt-country travellers can obtain the tourist visa upon arrival.
Tourism, leisure and social visits only; the stated stay is up to 120 days, with no extension or status change, and no commercial, employment or business activity.
The traveller must meet DIPS grant criteria including character, health, security, funds, genuine departure intent, onward/return transport and parental/guardian consent where applicable.
Non-citizens need a valid passport or travel document with more than six months validity, a return airline ticket, and confirmed accommodation or a local address.
Does not decide visitor visa (30-day), transit (airside up to 24 hours), residence, work, study, close-family, descent, diplomatic, official, special-document, or case-specific rules.

policies.title: Vanuatu: listed non-exempt ordinary passports requiring tourist visa approval before travel
policies.summary: DIPS states that non-exempt-country nationals must apply in advance and obtain approval before travelling.
conditions: DIPS says these non-exempt nationalities must apply for and obtain tourist-visa approval before travel; the application is subject to the stated tourist grant criteria.

The eVisa-branded online application portal is an application route. The reviewed DIPS pages do not establish a nationality-wide electronic visa issued in lieu of the required pre-approval, so this is not classified as eVisa.
Tourist visas allow up to 120 days without extension or status change and prohibit commercial, employment and business activity.
Transit, visitor (30-day), residence, work, study, diplomatic, official, special-document, and individual admissibility rules remain separate.

application.label: Vanuatu Immigration online visa application portal
steps: Select the tourist visa application route for a non-exempt nationality.
Submit the completed application and supporting passport, travel, funds, health, character and departure-intent documents.
Obtain approval before travelling to Vanuatu.

policies.title: Vanuatu: citizenship treatment
policies.summary: The destination's own code is represented as citizenship, not a foreign-entry visa result.
conditions: Represents a Ni-Vanuatu citizen using a Vanuatu passport or qualifying identity/travel document.
Does not decide dual nationality, foreign residence, diplomatic, official, emergency or other special-document cases.

policies.title: Venezuela: named ordinary passports exempt from tourist visa for air entry
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry’s current list expressly exempts these named nationalities from a tourist visa for entry to Venezuela by air. The status is visa_free only within that published air-entry tourist scope; it is not an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival, universal mode-of-entry rule or residual classification.
conditions: The official list expressly limits this tourist-visa exemption to entry by air. It does not establish an equivalent land- or sea-entry route.
Only the named country rows are mapped. France, Netherlands and United Kingdom parenthetical territories are not expanded beyond the catalog’s directly corresponding FR, NL and GB ordinary passports.
The source does not state a general duration, entries, fee, extension, airport, carrier, health, funds, return/onward-travel or final-admission rule for this air-entry exemption; none is inferred.

The separate Digital Chancellery process electronically issues tourist visas to foreign natural persons and is mapped in this batch for the unlisted catalog passports; it does not broaden this policy's expressly air-only visa-free scope.

Mercosur, bilateral identity-document facilities, diplomatic/official/service passports, special travel documents, work, study, residence, transit, citizenship and third-country-document arrangements are excluded.

policies.title: Vietnamese citizenship is outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: A Vietnamese ordinary passport belongs to a Vietnamese citizen and is not classified through the foreigner eVisa or foreign visitor-exemption framework.
conditions: Does not decide a dual national’s document choice, overseas-Vietnamese visa-exemption certificate, residence, departure, security, or individual admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Twelve nationalities: Resolution 44 unilateral visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Resolution 44 policy exempts these nationals from visas for a 45-day stay, regardless of passport type or entry purpose.
conditions: Applies to Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Finland, regardless of passport type and entry purpose.

Requires full compliance with Vietnam’s legal entry conditions. The current MOFA table states unilateral-exemption entrants need a passport valid at least six months and at least 30 days outside Viet Nam since their last departure.
British National (Overseas) passport holders are expressly excluded by the MOFA table; this ordinary UK-passport policy does not cover BNO or other special British documents.
Work, residence, overseas-Vietnamese, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, and individual security/admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Twelve nationalities: Resolution 229 visa exemption
policies.summary: The current Resolution 229 policy exempts these nationals from visas for up to 45 days from entry, regardless of passport type, subject to legal entry conditions.
conditions: Applies to Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Switzerland, regardless of passport type.

Maximum stay is 45 days from entry and remains subject to Vietnam’s legal entry conditions. The current MOFA table states unilateral-exemption entrants need a passport valid at least six months and at least 30 days outside Viet Nam since their last departure.
This current 2025-2028 resolution supersedes the expired 2025 Poland/Czechia/Switzerland package-tour pilot for the same ordinary passports; do not retain the expired tour-only condition.
Work, residence, overseas-Vietnamese, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, and individual security/admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Belarus ordinary passports: reciprocal visa exemption
policies.summary: Belarus ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for up to 30 days per stay, capped at 90 days in a calendar year.
conditions: The current MOFA table records 30 days for all passport types and caps ordinary-passport stay at 90 days in a calendar year.
The ordinary-passport agreement is distinct from diplomatic/official rules; purpose, work, residence, security, and admission limitations remain governed by Vietnamese law.

policies.title: Brunei ordinary passports: 14-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Brunei ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 14 days.
conditions: The current MOFA table distinguishes 14 days for ordinary Brunei passports from 30 days for diplomatic and official passports.
Does not establish work, residence, diplomatic/official, transit, crew, special-document, security, or individual-admission rights.

policies.title: Ten ordinary passports: bilateral short-stay visa exemptions
policies.summary: These current bilateral instruments give ordinary-passport holders short-stay visa exemption, with duration and purpose conditions varying by nationality.
conditions: Cambodia, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Singapore, and Thailand have 30-day ordinary-passport routes; Kazakhstan is 30 days per entry, capped at 90 days in each 180-day period.

The current MOFA instrument schedule records: Cambodia effective 5 December 2008 (amended 1 January 2010); Indonesia 4 December 2003; Kazakhstan 25 May 2024; Laos 1 July 2004; Malaysia 25 November 2001; Myanmar 26 October 2013 (amended 1 January 2020); Mongolia 6 March 2024; Singapore 1 December 2003; and Thailand 9 July 2000. It identifies Kyrgyzstan as a successor arrangement with the former Soviet agreement, without printing an effective date.

Cambodia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, and Singapore require at least six months' passport validity. Mongolia, Myanmar, and Singapore exclude income-earning activity; Myanmar also excludes other commercial activity. Malaysia is limited to the listed short-visit purposes; Laos and Indonesia have separate extension/residence rules.

The MOFA table separately records ordinary-passport periods for these bilateral arrangements. Do not generalize diplomatic, official, service, special, crew, ASEAN-official-event, residence, or border-pass rows to ordinary visitor passports.

policies.title: Philippines ordinary passports: 21-day visa exemption
policies.summary: Philippines ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 21 days when they hold a passport valid at least six months and an onward or return ticket.
conditions: The current MOFA table records an ordinary-passport exemption of up to 21 days, requiring a passport valid at least six months and a return or onward ticket.
The table separately identifies diplomatic, official, ASEAN-official-event, work, residence, special-document, security, and individual-admission provisions; they are not generalized here.

policies.title: Chile and Panama ordinary passports: 90-day non-remunerated-activity exemptions
policies.summary: Chile and Panama ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 90 days when entry is not for income-earning activity.
conditions: The MOFA table records 90-day ordinary-passport exemption for Chile and Panama; the underlying ordinary-passport rules require passports valid at least six months and prohibit entry for income-earning activity.
Do not generalize the diplomatic/official/special, crew, residence, employment, or individual security/admission provisions.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: all-nationalities eVisa
policies.summary: Every other catalog foreign ordinary-passport code can use Vietnam’s nationality-wide electronic-visa route; it is normalized as evisa.
conditions: Available to foreigners outside Viet Nam holding a valid passport or international travel document. The Article 8 visa-class and Article 16 invitation/guarantee rules, including their personal, delegation, diplomatic, residence, and purpose distinctions, remain separate procedures rather than nationality-wide ordinary-passport exclusions.

Valid for at most 90 days, for single or multiple entry. The Ministry of Public Security states that application, issuance, receipt, printing, and fee payment are electronic; an issued eVisa can be printed without collecting a visa at a mission or border gate.

Use only Government-designated international air, land, or sea border gates. The Government Portal confirms the official site publishes the eVisa border-gate list; the pre-arrival declaration is not an ETA or visa-exemption substitute.

Entry and stay remain conditioned on a valid travel document, the stated entry purpose, no suspension/prohibition from entry, and border-control admission. Accommodation providers must make temporary-residence declarations; work, residence, diplomatic/official, crew, border-pass, transit and overseas-Vietnamese certificate routes are distinct.

application.label: Viet Nam E-Visa
steps: Apply personally from outside Viet Nam, accurately complete the eVisa form, and select approved entry/exit border gates.
Pay the non-refundable eVisa fee and receive the result electronically before travel.
Enter and exit only at the designated border gates and comply with temporary-residence declaration and border-control requirements.

policies.title: Listed foreign ordinary passports: approved advance Visit Visa route
policies.summary: The current IPNA nationality eligibility dataset lists Visit Visa for every catalog passport code in this policy; the published route requires pre-travel approval and an embassy or consulate visa sticker, so it is normalized as visa_required rather than a true eVisa or a general visa on arrival.
conditions: The exact policy scope is the 196 catalog codes in the live eligibility dataset that display Visit Visa; Israel and Kosovo are deliberately excluded because neither appears in that dataset.

This is an online-portal application and approval workflow, but the published Visit Visa terms say the final visa sticker is issued by a Yemeni embassy or consulate abroad after Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority approval; do not normalize it as eVisa.

For the published Visit Visa, an applicant needs a request from a Yemeni or foreign resident host able to accommodate and support the visitor and undertaking departure; round-trip tickets are required.

The portal requires the host request, a passport data page valid at least six months, an official health certificate showing no infectious disease, a departure undertaking, and documents for the stated purpose (kinship, treatment, study, or request).

The published Visit Visa terms do not state an initial permitted stay. They do not authorize work, residence, entry after denial, or admission despite security, health, document, or border-control concerns.

The portal separately publishes group-tourist and urgent-tourist routes. Group tourism requires accredited agencies and at least ten people; urgent tourist visas are granted as stickers at border crossings only after Authority approval and an accredited Yemeni tourism-agency request. Neither establishes nationality-wide ordinary visa-free or visa-on-arrival access.

The separate 72-hour transit visa requires onward nationality/residence or an onward entry visa plus confirmed travel. Crew, diplomatic/official, family, work, exit/re-entry, residence, and special visas have their own terms and are not generalized here.

The MFA announcement says the system connects Authority branches, official land, sea, and air ports and missions. It does not prove that every port is operational or that a route is accepted in every territory or by every de facto authority; this policy is limited to the Republic of Yemen/IPNA official service and official-port framework.

application.label: Yemen eVisa application portal
steps: Select the applicable Visit Visa route in the official portal and submit the host, passport, health, travel, departure, and purpose evidence.
Obtain Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority approval and have the visa sticker issued by the relevant Yemeni embassy or consulate before travel.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports that do not require a visa
policies.summary: DGI expressly places these nationalities in its no-visa entry category.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality classification only. DGI's country list says these nationals do not require a visa to enter Zambia.

For air arrival, non-citizens/non-residents need a valid return air ticket; for land or water arrival, they need funds for their stay and departure. Admission remains subject to immigration examination.
This does not establish access for diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless or other special travel documents, residents, workers, students, crew, or case-specific travel.
Transit, including direct airside transit, and purpose-specific requirements are separate rules.

policies.title: Zambia: Zambian citizenship entry
policies.summary: Current Department of Immigration arrival guidance confines the visa requirement to qualifying non-citizens or non-residents; the same-country ordinary-passport relationship is normalized as citizenship, not a foreign visitor visa-free route.
conditions: DGI's arrival guidance distinguishes Zambian citizens from visa-requiring non-citizens; the no-visa schedule also expressly includes Zambia. This does not decide passport/document, dual-nationality, border, security or individual-admissibility formalities.
Direct-air-transit, resident, work, study, diplomatic, official, service and special-document rules are outside this nationality baseline.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports eligible for visa on arrival
policies.summary: DGI expressly allows these nationalities to get a visa at any Zambian port of entry.
conditions: DGI states these nationalities may receive a visa on arrival at any port of entry or from selected Zambian missions.
The same page says they may apply online, but that optional online route does not replace the expressly available arrival-visa route or make this a nationality-wide eVisa classification.

For arrival issuance, DGI requires host information and a physical Zambia address, a passport valid at least six months from entry with at least three full blank pages, and either a return air ticket or sufficient funds for land/water arrival.
Purpose, residence, employment, study, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document and individual admissibility rules remain separate.

policies.title: Zambia: listed ordinary passports requiring prior-clearance eVisa
policies.summary: DGI requires these nationalities to apply online and receive an approval letter before travelling to Zambia.
conditions: DGI says this category requires advance clearance, online application through eServices, and an approval letter before travel; it cannot use a visa-on-arrival route.
The electronic approval is an eVisa for the model's pre-travel-entry category; it does not guarantee admission, which remains subject to immigration examination.
Bring the approval letter and receipt to entry. DGI states eVisa approval-letter holders may enter through any port of entry.
DGI notes that applicants under 16 cannot make an eVisa application themselves and must be included in an adult's application when travelling with an adult.
Does not decide special documents, diplomatic/official treatment, residence, employment, study, crew, transit or case-specific purpose rules.

application.label: Zambia Department of Immigration eServices visa application
steps: Create or use an eServices account and select the visa application.
Complete Form 16, upload the required documents, review the application and pay online.
Receive and print the approval letter before travel; present the letter and receipt to the Immigration Officer.

policies.title: Category A ordinary passports: Zimbabwe visa-free visitors
policies.summary: The Department of Immigration Category A schedule and the live official eVisa nationality regime both expressly place this ordinary-passport cohort in the no-visa visitor category.
conditions: The schedules concern country nationals visiting Zimbabwe; this policy does not establish work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or other special-document treatment.
The online Zimbabwe Entry Declaration may be pre-filled before travel, but both official pages describe it as an entry declaration and it is not normalized as an ETA or visa.

Entry remains subject to ordinary documentary, health, security and immigration examination. The listed sources do not state a universal visitor stay period, proof-of-funds rule, accommodation rule or extension rule for this visa-free cohort.

policies.title: Zambian ordinary passport: Zimbabwe Category A visa-free visitor
policies.summary: Zimbabwe Immigration's current Category A schedule expressly names Zambia. The live eVisa FAQ omits it, so this narrow policy is retained separately with medium confidence rather than treated as a schedule complement.
conditions: This is a narrow ordinary-passport visitor finding from the Department of Immigration's Category A page. The official eVisa FAQ omission is a mutable-source discrepancy, not evidence of a different route.

The Entry Declaration is an optional/pre-fillable processing form, not an ETA or visa. Work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service and special-document routes are outside this policy.
Entry remains subject to documentary, health, security and immigration examination; the cited schedule does not state a universal stay, funds, accommodation or extension rule.

policies.title: Category B ordinary passports: Zimbabwe paid visa on arrival
policies.summary: The live official eVisa regime expressly allows this cohort to pay for and obtain a visa upon entering Zimbabwe. The optional online application does not displace that easier arrival route.
conditions: Category B requires a visa, but the official pages expressly permit payment and issuance at a Zimbabwe port of entry. This is therefore visa_on_arrival, even though an applicant may instead apply online before travel.

The current portal describes a standard arrival visa as valid for one month; double-entry and multiple-entry options have separate stated validity. Multiple-entry arrival availability is expressly limited to UK, US and Canadian travellers.

The Entry Declaration can be pre-filled online but is not an ETA. Visa type, fee and admission remain subject to Immigration's processing and discretion; no business-only, work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document route is included.

policies.title: Category C ordinary passports: Zimbabwe advance electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: The official Category C and eVisa regime require this cohort to apply, pay and obtain approval before travel. Immigration describes the approval as electronically issued and emailed, so it is normalized as evisa rather than visa required.
conditions: This policy covers only the named Category C ordinary-passport visitor cohort. The eVisa confirmation is issued electronically and emailed; passport stamping on arrival does not convert it into visa on arrival.

The official portal says to apply at least three weeks before travel and describes eVisa validity from issue as one month single-entry, three months double-entry, or six months multiple-entry. Processing or payment does not guarantee approval or admission.

The Entry Declaration is separate from the eVisa. Work, residence, business-only, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee and special-document rules remain outside this baseline; entry is subject to security and Immigration discretion.

application.label: Zimbabwe Department of Immigration eVisa service
application.processingTime: The FAQ states an average processing time of seven working days and advises applying at least three weeks before travel.
steps: Use the official Zimbabwe eVisa service to submit the visa application, required documents and payment before travel.
Wait for the electronic approval/confirmation sent to the applicant's email; an application fee does not guarantee approval.
Print the approved eVisa for travel and present it with the required travel documents for Immigration examination and passport stamping on arrival.

policies.title: Zimbabwean citizens: constitutional right to enter Zimbabwe
policies.summary: The Constitution grants every Zimbabwean citizen the right to enter Zimbabwe, so a Zimbabwean ordinary passport holder is not classified under the foreign-visitor visa regime.
conditions: This records the constitutional citizen-entry right only. It does not model nationality acquisition, dual-nationality disputes, passport issuance, document validity, criminal process, customs, health, security screening or other border controls.

policies.title: Peru: Peruvian-passport citizenship treatment
policies.summary: Migration guidance confirms that a person using a Peruvian passport has no limit on stay in Peru; this is citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa route.
conditions: The cited guidance concerns Peruvian nationals, including people with multiple nationalities, using a Peruvian passport for immigration control.
It does not determine dual-national documentation, departure requirements, identity-card use, nationality acquisition, loss, renunciation or individual border-admission circumstances.

policies.title: Peru: named ordinary passports visa-free for tourist entry
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry ordinary-passport table marks these nationalities as exempt (Sí) from the tourist visa requirement. This is visa-free entry, not an eVisa, visa on arrival, transit waiver or document-only route.
conditions: The policy is limited to the table's tourist column and ordinary passports; it does not classify transit, business, study, employment, residence, diplomatic, official, service, special, identity-card or other-document routes.
The table assigns nationality-specific stay limits and extension rules. No uniform duration, extension, entry count, fee, port, health, funds, onward-travel or admission condition is inferred.
Foreign visitors remain subject to migration control and the corresponding temporary immigration category; a visa exemption does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: Peru: named ordinary passports requiring a tourist visa
policies.summary: The current Foreign Ministry ordinary-passport table marks these nationalities as not exempt (No) from the tourist visa requirement. This is an advance visa requirement, not an eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The Ministry's legend states that No means the traveller is not exempt and requires a visa to enter Peru; the policy is limited to the ordinary-passport tourist column.

The current tourist-visa service directs affected travellers to apply through Peruvian consular offices at least 15 calendar days before travel. It does not directly establish an electronically issued eVisa, an ETA or a visa-on-arrival route for this cohort.

No duration, entries, fee, processing outcome, port, extension, health, funds, onward-travel or admission condition is inferred. Diplomatic, official, service, special, residence, transit, business, study, work and other non-tourist exceptions are outside this baseline.

policies.title: St Helena: named ordinary passports requiring advance eVisa
policies.summary: The current St Helena Immigration Service FAQ expressly lists these passport nationalities as requiring an eVisa applied for in advance. The authority says there is no visa-on-arrival facility for this cohort.
conditions: The Immigration Service’s current FAQ expressly names this closed passport-nationality cohort as requiring an eVisa applied for in advance; it says there is no visa-on-arrival facility at St Helena Airport.
The online eVisa route is limited to travel of up to 183 days. A decision remains subject to the authority’s application and admissibility checks and does not guarantee admission.

The passport used for travel ordinarily needs at least six months validity at entry. Temporary, emergency, diplomatic, official, service, special, refugee, stateless, former-state, St Helenian-status, residence, work, crew, transit and third-country-route treatment is excluded.

application.label: St Helena Immigration Service eVisa application
steps: Use the current official nationality guidance to determine whether the passport requires an advance eVisa.
Complete the Immigration Service eVisa application and provide the requested passport and supporting evidence before travel.
Travel only after a valid eVisa decision and present the same passport at St Helena border control.

policies.title: St Helena: Croatian and Slovenian ordinary passports under the former-Yugoslavia eVisa category
policies.summary: The current Immigration Service FAQ separately identifies territories formerly comprising the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as requiring an advance eVisa. This maps the remaining catalog ordinary passports in that direct category: Croatia and Slovenia.
conditions: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia are separately named in the authority’s country list; this narrow policy records the two remaining current catalog ordinary-passport codes covered by the FAQ’s separate former-Yugoslavia category.
The FAQ requires an eVisa applied for in advance and says there is no visa-on-arrival facility for visa nationals.
Former-state travel documents, residence, work, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special, St Helenian-status and other individual exceptions are excluded.

application.label: St Helena Immigration Service eVisa application
steps: Confirm use of a current Croatian or Slovenian ordinary passport within the authority’s former-Yugoslavia category.
Complete the eVisa application and provide requested evidence before travel.
Present the approved travel document at the St Helena border.

policies.title: St Helena: non-visa ordinary passports receive short-term entry permit at the border
policies.summary: St Helena Government says non-visa nationals may arrive without an advance short-term entry permit and that the permit is issued at the border. The arrival-issued permission is normalized as visa_on_arrival, while retaining the authority’s own non-visa terminology.
conditions: This is not a literal visa-on-arrival: it is the current arrival-issued Short Term Entry Permit normalized to visa_on_arrival because the applicable visitor permission is issued at the border.

The Government’s current policy expressly defines non-visa nationals against its Annex 3 visa-national schedule and says they can arrive without an advance short-term permit; this policy uses that stated complement rather than omission alone.

The permit may be granted for a visit not exceeding 183 days. It requires a valid passport, intended departure, pre-arranged accommodation, sufficient funds and medical-evacuation insurance; the current stated entry fee is GBP 20.

The immigration officer retains discretion. Criminal-conviction, passport-validity, health, admission, work, residence, long-term, landing-permission, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, St Helenian-status, and Ascension or Tristan da Cunha arrangements are excluded. British nationality or status categories other than the catalog’s ordinary GB passport are also outside this baseline.

policies.title: Solomon Islands: EU ordinary passports visa-free for short stays
policies.summary: The Immigration Division says the EU–Solomon Islands waiver applies to ordinary passports for visa-free short stays, excluding Ireland.
conditions: The source expressly covers ordinary passports, short stays for tourism, cultural visits, scientific activities or business, and excludes paid employment.
The page states a maximum 90 days in any 180-day period and excludes Ireland; it does not establish a route for other European nationalities or special travel documents.

The page also presents online-application and grant-letter text alongside its direct visa-free statement. This policy relies only on the express short-stay waiver and assigns no application, port, fee, entry-count or other operational condition.

policies.title: Solomon Islands: PRC ordinary passports visa-free for short stays
policies.summary: The Immigration Division states that the PRC mutual exemption permits ordinary-passport holders to travel to Solomon Islands without a visa.
conditions: The direct mutual-exemption statement covers ordinary PRC passports and says visa-free entry is up to 30 days per visit for tourism, business, family or transit purposes.

The same operational page also contains online-application, grant-letter and differing accumulated-stay text. No duration, eVisa route, fee, entry count or port is normalized beyond the expressly stated visa-free ordinary-passport status.
Work remains outside this short-visitor policy.

policies.title: Solomon Islands: UAE ordinary passports visa-free for short stays
policies.summary: The Immigration Division states that the UAE reciprocal agreement covers ordinary passports and permits visa-free entry.
conditions: The source expressly says the reciprocal agreement covers all passport classifications, including ordinary passports, for up to 90 days.

The same operational page contains online-application and grant-letter text. This policy relies only on the direct visa-free agreement statement and does not normalize an eVisa, entry count, fee or port.
Work is excluded.

policies.title: Solomon Islands: concessional ordinary passports receive a visitor visa on arrival
policies.summary: The current legal notice designates this nationality cohort for concessional entry, and government guidance says the cohort need not apply in advance and receives a visitor visa on arrival.
conditions: Legal Notice No. 128 names this exact concessional-country cohort and repeals earlier concessional notices. The government guidance says they do not apply in advance and are granted a visitor visa on arrival.
Arrival requires a passport valid for at least six months and a confirmed return or onward ticket; immigration retains ordinary entry and admission discretion.

This is visa_on_arrival, not visa-free admission. The current Immigration tourist page calls arrival issuance discretionary and gives inconsistent general tourist durations, so no uniform stay, extension, entry count, fee or port is assigned.

China and the covered EU ordinary passports are excluded because current, more specific mutual-exemption sources directly establish visa-free treatment; UAE is separately supported by its specific agreement.

policies.title: Papua New Guinea: current named ordinary-passport tourist Visa on Arrival cohort
policies.summary: ICA’s current Visa on Arrival schedule expressly makes these nationalities eligible; ICA’s visitor guidance confirms the holiday, sightseeing, social, recreational, friends-and-family visitor purpose.
conditions: The live schedule states that VOA is currently accessible to citizens of the named countries. The schedule expressly includes ordinary passports for the United Arab Emirates; Indonesia, Israel and Japan are stated to cover all passport types.
The Visitor Visa page limits this candidate to holiday, sightseeing, social or recreational visits and visits to friends or family; work and non-visitor categories are excluded.

The Visitor Visa page says that, in most circumstances, a visitor visa is single-entry for 60 days. This candidate does not generalize a duration, port, fee, entry count, medical, character, funds, return-travel, or admission condition beyond that source scope.

ICA provides an electronic application option to VOA-eligible travellers, but the directly available arrival route controls this normalized baseline. The PNG Digital Arrival Card is an online arrival declaration, not an ETA or visa.

The related non-VOA visa route is intentionally not classified here: ICA’s current Visitor Visa page directs that group to paper filing, while its linked 2025 handbook says visitor applications are online/eVisa. That unresolved processing conflict does not affect this named direct VOA cohort.

policies.title: Montserrat: current portal visa-free country list
policies.summary: The current Government of Montserrat immigration portal expressly lists these countries as not requiring a visa to travel to Montserrat. The list is used only for the exact mapped passport codes and is not treated as a residual rule.
conditions: The official portal directly labels the listed countries visa-free. The mapping uses only unambiguous country-name-to-ISO2 matches in the project passport manifest; territories and non-manifest entries are not normalized.

The source does not assign a stay period, visa-on-arrival route, ETA, electronic application, fee, port, entry count, special/diplomatic passport, residence, work, transit, third-country-document or citizenship exception. None is normalized.

The consolidated Act retains S.R.O. 46/2013 as the in-force visa-exemption Order, but this policy relies on the current portal list rather than inferring an unlisted complement from that older schedule.

policies.title: Montserrat: full British-citizen passports visa-free for short visits
policies.summary: Current UK government Montserrat guidance says travellers on a full British citizen passport from the UK can visit visa-free for up to 180 days.
conditions: The UK source expressly scopes this rule to travellers on a full British citizen passport from the UK and gives a limit of up to 180 days.
It does not establish treatment for other British-national statuses, British overseas-territory status, special documents, work, residence, transit or third-country entry requirements.
The mandatory online Immigration and Customs Form is a separate arrival declaration, not modeled as ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival.

policies.title: Montserrat: current portal eVisa-required country list
policies.summary: The current Government of Montserrat immigration portal expressly lists these countries as requiring a visa, and its FAQ identifies that required-visa route as an eVisa processed online.
conditions: The required-country list and FAQ directly state that nationals on the list require a visa; the FAQ describes the online eVisa as the available visitor/business visa route.

The portal says an eVisa authorizes travel but remains subject to normal immigration checks. No arrival-visa route, stay period, entry count, fee, port, work right, residence path, special/diplomatic passport treatment or third-country-document exception is normalized.
This is not inferred from the existence of an application form or from absence from the visa-free list: each passport code is explicitly present in the current required-country list.

policies.title: British Virgin Islands: full British citizen passport short visitor entry
policies.summary: Current UK Foreign Office travel advice says a visitor on a full British citizen passport can visit BVI without a visa for up to one month.
conditions: This mapping is limited to the ordinary full British citizen passport represented by GB in this catalog and to the one-month visitor scope stated by the UK Foreign Office.
It must not be generalized to British Overseas Territories citizenship, BVI belonger status, other British nationality classes, residence, work, transit, or special documents.
The online embarkation card mentioned by the advice is an arrival form; this source does not call it an ETA or visa.

policies.title: Cook Islands: ordinary short visitor permit granted on arrival
policies.summary: Cook Islands Immigration exempts short visitors without continuing rights from an advance visa, but requires an arrival report, arrival card and a visitor permit granted on arrival. The arrival-issued permit is normalized as visa_on_arrival.
conditions: This policy applies only to a person without Cook Islands continuing rights who travels as a short visitor for an allowed visitor purpose. It is not citizenship, permanent-residence, work, study, special-entry, transit, crew, cruise-only, or special-document treatment.

The Regulations exempt the visitor from obtaining a visa but make the exemption conditional on reporting on arrival, completing an arrival card, and being granted a visitor permit on arrival. The arrival-issued permission controls this project’s normalization as visa_on_arrival rather than visa_free.

New Zealand citizens travelling on New Zealand passports have visitor scope below 90 days; other international visitors have visitor scope below 31 days. No unstated duration or Australian-specific duration is inferred from amendment material.
Entry remains conditional on acceptable identity, character, health, sufficient funds or sponsorship, and onward travel. Arrival grant is not guaranteed.

No current official source establishes an ETA, eVisa, or advance-visa requirement for this initial ordinary short-visitor route. Online application links and emailed visa letters concern other, extended, or already approved visa-and-permit classes and are not reclassified here.

Cook Islander and permanent-resident continuing rights depend on status/document evidence, not a catalog passport code. The separate 72-hour crew and cruise permit waivers are outside ordinary short-tourist scope.

policies.title: Niue: named visitor-waiver passports receive 30-day visitor permit on arrival
policies.summary: Niue Tourism expressly says citizens in its named waiver list need not apply before travel and may receive a 30-day visitor permit on arrival. Because the admission document is issued on arrival, this is normalized as visa_on_arrival rather than visa_free.
conditions: The current tourism entry page explicitly identifies a waiver list, says no visa application is needed before travel, and expressly places issuance of a 30-day visitor permit on arrival. Only unambiguous project passport-code country matches are mapped; New Caledonia is not a project passport code.

The ordinary-passport abstraction does not establish diplomatic, official, emergency, temporary, refugee, stateless, crew, transit, work, study, residence, returnee, Niuean-origin or discretionary-admission treatment.

Visitors must have a passport valid at least three months after arrival, pre-booked accommodation, sufficient funds and a return/onward ticket. The source states admission may be refused; these are conditions, not a separate ETA/eVisa status.

policies.title: Niue: other directly modelled foreign visitors require advance visitor visa
policies.summary: The current Niue Tourism entry page expressly says all other travellers must apply for a visitor visa before travel. This is a prior-visa route, not an electronic visa or arrival permit.
conditions: This applies through the page’s explicit “all other travellers” instruction, not an inferred complement from an omitted nationality list. It is corroborated by the current Government of Niue Immigration form, which says travellers not from its named countries must apply for a visitor permit.

The current application form calls for passport information, itinerary, booked accommodation, fee and further material requested by the Chief Immigration Officer; its stated processing time is 7 to 14 days. It is not an electronic issuance route.
This does not establish work, study, residence, transit, crew, special/diplomatic passport, returnee, Niuean-origin, New Zealand status, discretionary-admission or third-country-document treatment.

application.label: Government of Niue Immigration visitor visa application form
application.processingTime: 7 to 14 days when the stated form and documents are complete.
steps: Complete the Government of Niue Immigration visitor visa form.
Submit the stated passport biodata, itinerary, booked accommodation, application fee and any material requested by the Chief Immigration Officer.
Receive the decision before travel; the form says the visa is sent after processing.

policies.title: Nauruan nationals: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: Nauru's visa requirement expressly applies to non-citizens, so an NR ordinary-passport holder is modelled as citizenship rather than a foreign visitor route.
conditions: This is a same-country citizenship normalization. It does not determine a dual national's treatment when presenting a different passport, nor passport, security, departure, residence, removal, or individual-admissibility decisions.
The cited provision establishes the foreign-national visa scope; it is not an inference from a visitor form or an arrival procedure.

policies.title: Russian and Spanish ordinary passports: visa waiver
policies.summary: The current statutory visa-waiver schedule names Russia and Spain without a passport-type limitation, unlike its expressly limited diplomatic, official, service, or public-affairs entries.
conditions: The Regulations exempt a national of a listed visa-waiver-agreement country only for the period and circumstances specified in the relevant agreement. Neither a duration nor agreement-specific eligibility conditions are reproduced here.

The schedule expressly limits Japan, China, India, and Cuba to specified diplomatic, official, service, or public-affairs passport categories. Those limitations are preserved and do not create ordinary-passport waivers for those codes.
This does not establish treatment of residence, employment, media, research, transit, crew, emergency, special-purpose, refugee, or other special-document routes.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: fee-exempt visitor visa on arrival
policies.summary: The named Schedule 3 nationalities may request the visitor visa on entry without completing an application form; this is a border-issued visitor visa, not visa-free admission.
conditions: Regulations 5(4) and 12(2)(a) allow a national covered by Regulation 16(4) to request a visitor visa on entry without any application form. Schedule 3 identifies these fee-exempt nationalities; Russia is excluded here because its separate waiver is the easier route.

Visitor visas are for holiday, visiting friends or relatives, listed meetings, cultural or sporting activities, or another purpose the Director considers appropriate; they are single-entry and may not exceed three months.

The applicant must hold an onward ticket and required destination documents, have no expected condition breach, and show support if requested. The visitor route excludes business-visa activities and non-normal religious activity.
China's Schedule 5 waiver is expressly limited to diplomatic, service, or public-affairs passports. It does not displace the ordinary Chinese passport's Schedule 3 arrival-visitor-visa route.
Cook Islands and Niue are named in Schedule 3 but are outside this repository's 199-passport manifest; no relationship is invented for either.

policies.title: Other ordinary foreign passports: advance visitor visa
policies.summary: Every remaining foreign ordinary passport requires a valid visa, and the visitor-visa regulation expressly requires the application before entry for every applicant outside the named arrival cohort.
conditions: This is the express statutory residual: the Act requires a visa for every non-citizen, while Regulation 12(2)(b) requires advance application for every visitor applicant outside the Regulation 16(4) arrival cohort. It is not inferred from omission from a list or application form.

A visitor visa is a pre-entry visa, not an eVisa. Form 7 permits online lodging, but the Regulations describe an application process and pre-arrival evidence of a granted visa; they do not state electronic visa issuance or create an eVisa category.
Australia and New Zealand applicants must provide a Nauruan-citizen sponsorship letter. That sponsorship condition is retained and does not create a separate status, exemption, or arrival route.

Japan, India, and Cuba have only passport-type-limited Schedule 5 waivers; Taiwan has no current Schedule 3 or Schedule 5 ordinary-passport entry route after the 2024 Schedule 3 substitution of the People's Republic of China. These special-document and historical entries do not alter this ordinary-passport policy.

Media, business, employment, research, residence, dependant, regional-processing-centre, long-term-stay, special-purpose, emergency, transit, crew, and citizenship routes are outside this short-tourist classification. Admission and visa grant remain discretionary under the Act and Regulations.

policies.title: Tongan subject: entry without a foreign visitor permit
policies.summary: The Immigration Act expressly entitles a Tongan subject to enter without first obtaining a permit. The same-country ordinary-passport catalog row is normalized as citizenship, not as a foreign visitor visa route.
conditions: The statutory entitlement is for a person who establishes Tongan-subject status; it does not determine treatment of a dual national travelling on a different passport, special travel document, work, residence, diplomatic or admission case.

policies.title: EU citizens: treaty short-stay visa-free travel
policies.summary: The in-force EU–Tonga agreement gives the named EU-nationality cohort visa-free short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. The treaty’s Member State definition excludes Ireland and the United Kingdom; Croatia is included.
conditions: The agreement applies to citizens travelling for a maximum 90 days in any 180-day period and excludes remunerated activity.
The treaty rule takes precedence over the Revenue and Embassy’s more general arrival-visitor wording for these mapped EU citizens.
This does not establish work, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document, security-screening or individual admission treatment.

policies.title: Consensus named foreign passports: visitor visa issued on arrival
policies.summary: Both live Tongan Government schedules name this ordinary-passport cohort for a visitor visa issued on arrival. This is normalized as visa_on_arrival; the sources’ 30-day and 31-day descriptions are not reconciled into a duration claim.
conditions: Revenue states issuance is conditional on a valid return ticket and sufficient funds; entry remains subject to immigration decision.
The Embassy says the visa is issued on arrival; its separate prior-authority pathway for unlisted travellers is not included in this consensus cohort.
This policy does not establish employment, business, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, official or special-document treatment.

policies.title: EU Member State ordinary passports: short-stay visa waiver
policies.summary: The operative EU–FSM agreement directly waives visas for citizens of the 26 listed EU Member States holding valid ordinary passports for short stays.
conditions: The agreement defines its Member-State scope as EU Member States other than the United Kingdom and Ireland; it directly covers ordinary passports and is not extended here to EFTA, United Kingdom, Irish or other passports.
The treaty waiver is for up to 90 days in any 180-day period and does not apply to travel for a paid activity.

The waiver preserves FSM entry and short-stay conditions and individual refusal of entry. It does not decide employment, residence, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or case-specific treatment.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: permit-free visits of up to 30 days
policies.summary: FSM Embassy entry guidance states a destination-wide rule: a permit is not required for a person visiting the FSM for 30 days or less. This policy records that direct universal short-visit rule outside the separately evidenced EU treaty cohort.
conditions: This is a direct universal rule for a person visiting for 30 days or less, not a nationality complement inferred from omission or an application form.
For a visit exceeding 30 days, the Embassy guidance requires an entry permit. The resulting longer-visit process is not normalized here as an eVisa, ETA or visa on arrival.

The Embassy guidance requires a passport valid for at least 120 days after entry and completion of the FSM Immigration Arrival and Departure Record on arrival where the visitor has no valid entry permit. The arrival record is a declaration, not an ETA or visa.

The separate longer-visit treatment stated for United States, Marshall Islands and Palau citizens/nationals does not change the direct permit-free classification for an ordinary short visit of 30 days or less.

This policy does not decide employment, residence, business or contract work beyond the ordinary short tourist visit; it also does not decide passport/document acceptance, diplomatic, official, service, special-passport, transit, crew, health or individual-admissibility cases.

policies.title: FSM citizens: national entry category
policies.summary: The official FSM entry material treats FSM citizens and nationals as their own travel-document category; its universal up-to-30-day no-permit rule also does not impose an entry permit on a person visiting the FSM.
conditions: This records the catalog's same-country citizenship relationship only. It is not a foreign visitor-visa classification.

policies.title: EU Member State ordinary passports: short-stay visa waiver
policies.summary: The operative EU–Tuvalu agreement directly waives visas for citizens of the 26 listed EU Member States holding valid ordinary passports for short stays.
conditions: The agreement defines its Member-State scope as EU Member States other than the United Kingdom and Ireland; it directly covers ordinary passports and is not extended here to EFTA, United Kingdom, Irish or other passports.
The visa waiver is for up to 90 days in any 180-day period and excludes travel for a paid activity.

The agreement leaves domestic entry and short-stay conditions, individual admissibility decisions and refusal of entry in place. It does not decide residence, employment, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or case-specific treatment.
A visa waiver does not erase a distinct domestic visitor-permit process; this normalized status only records that the agreement says no visa is required.

policies.title: New Zealand valid passports: temporary-visitor visa waiver
policies.summary: The current in-force New Zealand–Tuvalu agreement expressly allows New Zealand citizens holding valid New Zealand passports to enter Tuvalu as temporary visitors without a visa for stays not exceeding three months.
conditions: The agreement is modeled only for a New Zealand ordinary passport held by a New Zealand citizen; it does not extend to Cook Islands, Niue or Tokelau territorial treatment.
The rule is limited to temporary visitors for an intended stay not exceeding three months; it includes business visitors but excludes intended employment, profession or occupation.
The agreement preserves Tuvalu's entry, residence and other immigration requirements, individual refusal and temporary suspension for public order, health or security.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: visitor permit at entry
policies.summary: Tuvalu's current Immigration Act and Regulations directly establish a visitor-permit route for any visitor at entry. Excluding the directly waived EU and New Zealand cohorts, it is normalized as visa on arrival rather than visa-free.
conditions: This is an express destination-wide statutory visitor-permit route, not a complement inferred from a nationality list or an application form. Every overseas air or sea arrival must appear before an immigration officer; the Regulations' Conditions of Entry say that, absent an exempt category or already-obtained enter-and-reside permit, a visitor requires a Visitor's Permit and the officer permits entry for up to 30 days.

The immigration officer has discretion and must be satisfied about an onward ticket or other means of travel to a country the visitor can enter, and the visitor cannot exceed three months in the preceding 12 months. The permit is not automatic admission.

The visitor permit normally allows at most 30 days; ordinary visitors may not work, conduct business, study or proselytise. A separate special endorsement or permit-to-enter-and-reside process applies to employment, business, study, residence and other non-tourist purposes.

The Schedule 1 fee list distinguishes fee treatment only. It does not create an additional visa-free nationality cohort; likewise, arrival and departure cards are separate border declarations, not an ETA or visa route.

This policy does not decide section 7 individual exemptions (armed forces, diplomats, government employees, related families, specified Ministerial groups or seamen), citizenship, diplomatic, official, service, special passports, transit, crew, residency or third-country-document conditions.

policies.title: Tuvaluan citizens: entry without a permit
policies.summary: The Immigration Act expressly entitles a citizen of Tuvalu to enter without first obtaining a permit.
conditions: This records the catalog's same-country citizenship relationship only. It is not a visitor-visa classification for foreign passports.

policies.title: Marshall Islands citizens: outside foreign visitor-visa scope
policies.summary: The Immigration Act gives every citizen of the Republic a right to be in the Republic. The same-country ordinary-passport row is normalized as citizenship, rather than a foreign visitor route.
conditions: This same-country normalization does not decide a dual national's treatment when presenting a different passport, nor residence, work, special-document, clearance, or individual-admissibility treatment.
Citizens remain subject to border-recording procedures; that does not create a foreign visitor visa requirement.

policies.title: United States, Palau, and Federated States of Micronesia citizens: statutory visa exemption
policies.summary: The Immigration Act expressly exempts citizens of the United States, Palau, and the Federated States of Micronesia from the requirement to hold a visa. This ordinary-passport catalog normalization is visa_free, not an arrival-issued visa.
conditions: The Act's exemption applies to citizens, while ordinary passports are the catalog scope. It does not establish treatment for diplomatic, contractor, crew, work, residence, or other special routes.
The Act states that exempt persons remain subject to immigration clearance and may be refused an entry permit on the statutory eligibility grounds.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: 90-day visa exemption or waiver
policies.summary: The Division's linked summary expressly labels this named ordinary-passport cohort visa exempt/waived for 90 days from arrival. Its grouping label is not used to infer membership; only the directly enumerated passport codes are modeled.
conditions: The summary requires six months-plus passport validity after departure, confirmed onward travel, and necessary onward-country documents; it forbids extension, change of status, and employment.
The source's historical 'EU Member Countries' heading also expressly enumerates the United Kingdom. The direct enumeration, not that inaccurate heading, supports GB.
Taiwan is expressly written as Republic of China-Taiwan, ROC. The separately listed Guatemala row is not modeled because the same summary also puts Guatemala in its VOA table.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa on arrival
policies.summary: The Division's linked summary expressly labels this directly named ordinary-passport cohort VISA ON ARRIVAL, for a 90-day stay from arrival and a waived fee.
conditions: The summary specifies ordinary passports, six months-plus passport validity after departure, confirmed onward travel, and needed onward-travel visas; it excludes extension, change of status, employment, study, and research.

The list is modeled only for its directly named ordinary-passport codes. It does not prove a route for an omitted nationality, special passport, diplomatic mission, crew, transit, work, residence, or individual admission case.
Guatemala is deliberately excluded because the same official summary also places it in the visa-exempt table, creating a direct unresolved conflict.

policies.title: Kiribati citizen: right to enter
policies.summary: The official Immigration Procedures states that every Kiribati citizen has the right to enter and be in Kiribati. The same-country ordinary-passport catalog row is normalized as citizenship, not a foreign visitor visa route.
conditions: The statutory right requires proof of citizenship and identity and compliance with border requirements. It does not classify a dual national travelling on another passport or a foreign traveller’s visitor, work, transit, residence, special-document or admission case.

policies.title: Named foreign ordinary passports: visa waiver
policies.summary: The live Immigration Division page identifies the 2023 Order as current and expressly names this mapped foreign-nationality cohort among countries whose citizens may travel to Kiribati without a visa. The procedures call this mechanism a visa waiver; arrival entry processing is not normalized as a visa issued on arrival.
conditions: The current portal states a maximum 90 days in any 12-month period, a passport valid at least six months from departure, an ICAO-compliant passport, onward travel and sufficient funds.
The visa-waiver classification is limited to visitor travel. The portal directs travellers seeking work to obtain a work visa before travel.
This does not establish residence, employment, study, transit, diplomatic, official, special-document or individual admission treatment.
The portal names Greenland, Puerto Rico, Cook Islands and Niue as places but they are not independent ordinary-passport codes in this catalog; no catalog mapping is made for those place names.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Easy Visitor Permit electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: The current public ICA eVisa portal directly names this ordinary-passport cohort in its Easy Visitor Permit eligibility tables. The 2025 ICA handbook establishes that eVisas can be issued, so this is an electronic pre-travel visitor-visa route rather than mere online lodgement or VOA.
conditions: This policy concerns only national ordinary passports that were unresolved in the separate PNG ordinary-passport batch and are directly named in the portal's 30-day or 60-day Easy Visitor Permit tables. It does not duplicate that batch's direct VOA cohort.

The Easy Visitor Permit covers holiday, sightseeing, social or recreational visits and visits to relatives or friends. The 30-day table says online-only application, while the public service is ICA's eVisa portal and the 2025 ICA handbook states that an eVisa can be issued. This is not inferred from a form, payment page, or digital arrival declaration.

The portal describes a single entry, 30-day permit and says starred passports may also apply for a 60-day permit. The separate 60-day table directly names additional passports. Work is prohibited; media, organized travel, special passports, residence, business, employment, transit, individual admissibility and extension rules are not normalized here.

The portal's 60-day text calls its broader table countries on the VOA schedule, yet that table differs materially from ICA's current VOA page, which expressly excludes mainland France, New Zealand and the United States. The table is used only for its direct electronic-permit names, never to infer VOA; this discrepancy is a material freshness risk.
The PNG Digital Arrival Card is a separate arrival declaration and does not change this eVisa classification.

application.label: Papua New Guinea ICA eVisa portal
application.processingTime: The current 2025 ICA handbook says eVisa can be issued almost instantaneously when entry requirements are met, while also giving a general ten-working-day visa-processing time.
steps: Use the official ICA eVisa portal's Easy Visitor Permit option for the directly named ordinary passport, holiday, sightseeing, social, recreational, friends or family purpose.
Provide the requested passport and travel information, pay the portal charge where applicable, and wait for the pre-travel visa decision before departure.
Complete the separate PNG Digital Arrival Card when required and present the approved visa and travel documents for ICA examination on arrival.

policies.title: EU, EEA, Swiss and French ordinary passports: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Current France-Visas guidance expressly exempts EU, EEA and Swiss nationals from overseas-territory visas. FR is represented as visa_free rather than citizenship because the destinations are territorial catalog codes PF and NC.
conditions: Ordinary passport held as a citizen of the listed EU, EEA or Swiss state; up to 90 days.
This records only the short visitor visa result, not residence, employment, family-member residence cards, identity-document alternatives, transit, special passports or final admission.
French Polynesia and New Caledonia are outside Schengen and remain separately scoped destinations.

policies.title: Named Annex II ordinary passports: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: The current French Polynesia and New Caledonia Annex II schedules expressly exempt these passport nationalities without a biometric, residence, visa, cruise, work or special-document qualifier.
conditions: For a short visitor stay of up to three months in each six-month period.
GB records the ordinary United Kingdom baseline; separate named British non-British-Citizen document statuses are not mapped to the catalog.
The schedules separately mention New Zealand passport holders from Cook Islands, Niue and Tokelau; that document condition is not mapped to CK or NU catalog codes.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visitor visa-free treatment with work exception
policies.summary: The current schedules expressly waive visas for ordinary visitor travel by these nationalities, with a narrow listed exception for certain paid activities lacking the required work authorisation.
conditions: Short tourism or other non-remunerated visitor entry up to three months per six-month period.
Excludes the schedule's paid-activity/work-authorisation exception, residence, transit, diplomatic, service and special-document routes.
The U.S. extension for American Samoa and Guam applies only when the traveler holds a U.S. passport; it is not mapped to AS or GU catalog codes.

policies.title: Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passports: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Both current schedules separately name the Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport documents; they do not grant the same rule to a PRC ordinary passport.
conditions: Only a Hong Kong SAR or Macao SAR passport respectively; up to three months in each six-month period.
Excludes PRC passport, Taiwan identity-number, residence-permit, cruise, transit, work, diplomatic, service and special-document routes.

policies.title: Other ordinary passports: territory-specific advance visa required
policies.summary: For the remaining catalog ordinary passports, the two current orders require a valid territory-specific visa unless the traveler qualifies for a separately specified exemption. The required visa is a physical vignette, so it is normalized as advance visa rather than eVisa.
conditions: Short visitor baseline only. A Schengen visa alone is insufficient; the visa must be valid for the requested overseas territory.

Residence permits, long-stay visas, French multi-entry visas, cruise conditions, transit, diplomatic, service, official and other special-document exemptions remain conditional and are not normalized as nationality-wide visitor access.

For Vanuatu, the listed ordinary-passport waiver is limited to passports issued before 25 May 2015; the current entry order also requires a travel document issued less than ten years earlier, so it cannot support a current ordinary-passport waiver.
No eVisa or ETA is inferred from France-Visas' online application workflow.

policies.title: U.S. passport holder: American Samoa, Guam and CNMI domestic/citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A U.S. citizen or national travelling on a U.S. ordinary passport does not use a foreign visitor visa, ESTA, G-CNMI ETA or territorial visitor-permit route. The project has no separate U.S.-citizenship status for AS, GU and MP, so this no-visa treatment is normalized as visa_free.
conditions: For American Samoa, this covers the official U.S. citizen/national document route: a valid U.S. passport or equivalent specified citizenship/identity documents, confirmed return or onward travel, and the entry page's proof-of-employment or official-assignment requirement. Travellers meeting the valid-document route do not need an OK Board; its waiver process covers lost, expired or substitute documents.

For Guam and CNMI, federal documentary rules regulate nonimmigrant aliens. This is not a foreign visitor category, does not establish entry for a dual national travelling on another passport, and does not cover residence, work, parole, military, transit, diplomatic, special-document or final-admission cases.

policies.title: American Samoa: named current waiver-country online 30-day permit
policies.summary: The current American Samoa Government list names this 46-code ordinary-passport cohort, including Qatar. Its current U.S. Visa/Waiver visitor service requires online application and an emailed permit before arrival; that mandatory electronic pre-travel authorization is normalized as eta.
conditions: Apply and obtain the emailed American Samoa visitor permit before travel; the portal states applications must be submitted online within three business days before travel.

The route is limited to a 30-day visitor permit, requires a qualifying passport/document, return ticket within 30 days, lodging/local-contact evidence, fee and admissibility. It is not a visa-free entry.

The program’s precise statutory EPWP label and country-list update mechanism, work, residence, credit study, transit, crew/commercial-vessel, diplomatic, official, special-document, third-country-document and final-admission treatment are outside this ordinary visitor mapping.

application.label: American Samoa U.S. Visa / Waiver 30-Day Visitor Permit
steps: Use the official visitor-permit service before travel.
Provide identity, return-ticket, lodging/local-contact and payment information.
Receive the emailed permit and present it to American Samoa Immigration on arrival.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: Canadian citizen visitor no-visa route
policies.summary: The U.S. State Department states that Canadian citizens travelling to the United States do not require a nonimmigrant visa, subject to its listed non-visitor and inadmissibility exceptions. This applies to ordinary Canadian visitor passports for Guam and CNMI and is normalized as visa_free.
conditions: This is not ESTA, VWP or G-CNMI VWP. It is limited to ordinary short visitor travel and remains subject to U.S. immigration law, inspection and admissibility.
Canadian official, treaty-trader/investor, K, S and other specifically listed non-visitor purposes require visas; permanent residents of Canada are not Canadian citizens for this rule.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: eligible Freely Associated State citizen Compact no-visa route
policies.summary: Current U.S. State Department Compact guidance establishes visa-free U.S. entry for eligible FSM, Marshall Islands and Palau citizens. The ordinary-passport visitor route for Guam and CNMI is normalized as visa_free.
conditions: This policy is for citizens eligible under the respective Compact, travelling on a valid national ordinary passport; CBP inspection, I-94 documentation, admissibility and the territorial scope remain material.

FSM alien spouses or children do not share the privilege. RMI eligibility varies with citizenship/acquisition, relationship and purpose; adoption and citizenship/passports acquired through investment/passport-sale programs are excluded. Palau’s privilege generally does not extend to alien spouses/children and official-passport official travel can require a visa.
These Compact residence, study and employment privileges do not make a third-country holder, a resident/document route, a special passport or a parole/crew/transit case passport-wide visitor access.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: G-CNMI Visa Waiver Program electronic travel authorization
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1(q) names these ten countries plus the qualifying Hong Kong and Taiwan routes and requires a CBP electronic travel authorization before embarkation. It is therefore normalized as eta, not visa_free.
conditions: For travel on or after 29 November 2024, receive CBP G-CNMI travel authorization before embarking, then request admission for business or pleasure in Guam or CNMI for no more than 45 days.

A valid ICAO-compliant machine-readable passport, I-94, qualifying carrier and round-trip ticket are required. Hong Kong requires an HKSAR or BN(O) passport plus Hong Kong ID; Taiwan requires Taiwan residence, prescribed itinerary, Taiwan ID and passport/re-entry permit.

The authorization is neither a visa nor a determination of admissibility. It does not permit travel beyond Guam/CNMI, extension or change of status; work, residence, credit study, transit, crew, parole, diplomatic, official and special-document cases remain separate.

The State Department's general VWP page still mentions paper Form I-736, while current 8 CFR and the live CBP service require electronic authorization; this mapping follows the controlling regulation and operational portal.

application.label: CBP G-CNMI ETA
steps: Apply for a CBP G-CNMI electronic travel authorization before embarkation.
Provide passport, eligibility and travel information.
Travel only after authorization and request CBP admission in Guam or CNMI.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: other federal VWP ordinary passports require ESTA
policies.summary: For these federal VWP passport codes not covered by the separate G-CNMI program, the State Department requires approved ESTA before U.S. visitor travel. The Guam/CNMI route is normalized as eta.
conditions: This covers tourism or business stays of 90 days or less, with an e-passport and approved ESTA before travel; it is distinct from the G-CNMI 45-day program.

VWP Improvement Act prior-travel, dual-nationality, carrier, passport, admissibility and purpose limitations can require a visitor visa. Work, credit study, residence, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document, transit and final-admission cases are excluded.

application.label: U.S. ESTA
steps: Submit ESTA before travel.
Use an eligible e-passport for a permitted visitor purpose.
Request CBP admission at Guam or CNMI.

policies.title: Guam: PRC ordinary passport requires advance visa
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1(r) expressly confines PRC visa-free EVS-TAP to CNMI and states that a PRC national seeking admission to Guam still requires a visa.
conditions: This is a Guam-only ordinary PRC passport rule. CNMI EVS-TAP is not a Guam route.
A valid U.S. visa, other federal status, residence document, parole, transit, crew, diplomatic/official or special-document route is outside this passport-only visitor baseline.

policies.title: Northern Mariana Islands: PRC CNMI EVS-TAP
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1(r) establishes CNMI EVS-TAP as a restricted pre-travel electronic authorization sub-program for PRC nationals, so the short-visitor route is normalized as eta.
conditions: Before embarking, the PRC national must receive CBP electronic authorization, be a business/pleasure visitor, use an ICAO-compliant PRC machine-readable passport and hold the required round-trip ticket and I-94.

Entry and stay are CNMI-only for no more than 14 days; it is neither admission to Guam nor ordinary U.S. entry. No extension or change of status is available; residence, work, transit, crew, parole, diplomatic, official, special-document and final-admission routes are outside this policy.

application.label: CBP CNMI EVS-TAP
steps: Submit the CNMI EVS-TAP electronic authorization before embarkation.
Provide PRC passport, eligibility and travel information.
Travel only after authorization and request CBP admission in the CNMI.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: qualifying Bahamian preclearance no-visa route
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1 provides a narrow no-visa exception for a qualifying Bahamian traveller examined by U.S. immigration officers in the Bahamas before direct travel. The project normalizes that conditional ordinary-passport route as visa_free, consistently with its existing U.S. destination evidence.
conditions: The exception is not general visa-free travel: it depends on Bahamian residence/citizenship documentation, prior U.S. immigration examination in the Bahamas and travel on the qualifying inspected route.
A traveller outside those conditions can require a U.S. visitor visa. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document and final-admission cases remain separate.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: remaining foreign ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: For every remaining catalog foreign ordinary passport not affected by the current proclamation and after the separate Bahamian, Canadian, Compact, federal VWP, G-CNMI and PRC-CNMI exceptions are removed, current 8 CFR 212.1 applies its general requirement to present a valid visa.
conditions: This is the ordinary short business/pleasure nationality baseline, not a finding that every person holding the passport lacks a valid U.S. visa or other immigration status.

Valid U.S. visas, lawful permanent residence, advance parole, humanitarian or individual documentary waivers, visas for transit/crew/work/study/residence, diplomatic/official/special passports and inadmissibility remain distinct conditional cases.
The rule never treats a residual passport as eligible for G-CNMI, federal VWP/ESTA, Compact or CNMI EVS-TAP merely by omission.

The catalog passports affected by Presidential Proclamation 10998 are deliberately unresolved because current entry and visitor-visa restrictions and their historic-visa, dual-national and other exceptions cannot be represented by one passport-wide access category.

policies.title: EU, EEA, Swiss and French ordinary passports: visa-free short visits
policies.summary: France-Visas and the Interior Ministry directly exempt EU, EEA and Swiss citizens from overseas visas. FR is visa_free, not citizenship: GF, FW, YT and RE are territorial destination codes rather than France itself.
conditions: Ordinary passport held as a citizen of the listed EU, EEA or Swiss state, for a visitor stay up to 90 days.
This does not normalize residence, work, family-member residence cards, identity-document alternatives, transit, special passports or final admission.
All four catalog destinations are outside Schengen; the classification follows free-movement rights rather than a Schengen visa.

policies.title: Named French Guiana ordinary passports: visa-free visitor stays
policies.summary: The current DROM Annex II schedule directly waives the French Guiana visitor visa for this ordinary-passport cohort. Geographic exceptions, document-qualified waivers and paid activity remain separate.
conditions: Short visitor stay up to 90 days in 180 days. The work-authorisation exceptions for Australia, Japan, Republic of Korea, Mexico, Singapore, the United States and Venezuela do not apply to ordinary tourism or family visits.
Hong Kong and Macao are SAR passport entries only, not a PRC ordinary-passport rule.
The schedule's passport-specific, French multi-entry-visa, residence-permit, cruise, transit, diplomatic, service, special-document and final-admission rules remain separate.

policies.title: Ecuadorian ordinary passports: visa-free French Guiana visitor stays
policies.summary: The DROM Annex II expressly grants Ecuador all-passport visa exemption for French Guiana, while treating Réunion differently.
conditions: Short visitor stay up to 90 days in 180 days; excludes work, residence, transit, diplomatic/service and final-admission conditions.
This is not generalized to Réunion, Mayotte, or the aggregate French West Indies destination.

policies.title: Dominican and Saint Lucian ordinary passports: limited French Guiana visa-free visits
policies.summary: The DROM Annex II directly grants Dominica and Saint Lucia a French Guiana ordinary-passport waiver only for the specified short duration.
conditions: Only stays of 15 days or less, within 120 cumulative days in 12 months.
Does not establish a waiver for a longer stay, work, residence, transit, cruise, special passport or other document condition.

policies.title: Named Réunion ordinary passports: visa-free visitor stays
