policies.summary: The current DROM Annex II schedule directly waives the Réunion visitor visa for this ordinary-passport cohort. The listed work exceptions and document-qualified routes are retained as conditions.
conditions: Short visitor stay up to 90 days in 180 days. The work-authorisation exceptions for Australia, Japan, Republic of Korea, Mexico, Singapore, the United States and Venezuela do not apply to ordinary tourism or family visits.
Hong Kong and Macao are SAR passport entries only, not a PRC ordinary-passport rule.
The schedule's passport-specific, French multi-entry-visa, residence-permit, cruise, transit, diplomatic, service, special-document and final-admission rules remain separate.

policies.title: Brazilian, South African, Mozambican, Dominican and Saint Lucian ordinary passports: visa-free Réunion visitor stays
policies.summary: The DROM Annex II directly distinguishes Réunion from French Guiana and grants the listed ordinary-passport visitor waivers.
conditions: Short visitor stay up to 90 days in 180 days. The ordinary visitor classification excludes the schedule's paid-activity/work-authorisation exception for Brazil.
For Dominica and Saint Lucia, Réunion has the full short-stay waiver; French Guiana has only the separate 15-day waiver.
No result is inferred for Mayotte or the French West Indies aggregate from this Réunion-specific material.

policies.title: Named Mayotte ordinary passports: visa-free visitor stays
policies.summary: The current Mayotte Annex II directly waives the visitor visa for this ordinary-passport cohort. The schedule differs from the DROM order in destination-specific rows, which are recorded separately.
conditions: Short visitor stay up to 90 days in 180 days. The work-authorisation exceptions for Australia, Japan, Republic of Korea, Mexico, Singapore, the United States and Venezuela do not apply to ordinary tourism or family visits.
Hong Kong and Macao are SAR passport entries only, not a PRC ordinary-passport rule.
The schedule's passport-specific, French multi-entry-visa, residence-permit, cruise, transit, diplomatic, service, special-document and final-admission rules remain separate.

policies.title: Brazilian, Mozambican, Dominican and Saint Lucian ordinary passports: visa-free Mayotte visitor stays
policies.summary: The current Mayotte Annex II directly grants ordinary-passport visitor waivers for these destination-specific rows.
conditions: Short visitor stay up to 90 days in 180 days; the ordinary visitor classification excludes the paid-activity/work-authorisation exception for Brazil.
No result is inferred for French Guiana, Réunion or the French West Indies aggregate from this Mayotte-specific material.

policies.title: Other French Guiana ordinary passports: advance territory visa required
policies.summary: The current DROM order requires a valid territory-specific visa unless an Annex II nationality exemption applies. This covers the ordinary-passport baseline after direct waivers and genuinely unresolved biometric rows are removed.
conditions: A valid visa must cover French Guiana; a Schengen visa alone does not authorize the territory. France-Visas' online workflow is application filing, not eVisa issuance.

French multi-entry-visa, residence-permit, long-stay visa, cruise, transit, crew, special/diplomatic/service passport and individual-admission exceptions remain conditional and do not change this ordinary-passport baseline.

Georgia's former Annex II exemption was removed effective June 2025. Vanuatu's waiver is restricted to pre-25-May-2015 ordinary passports, so it cannot establish a current unqualified ordinary-passport exemption.
Brazil's listed French Guiana exceptions are organized/brief/transit/frontier/emergency routes rather than a nationality-wide visitor waiver.

policies.title: Other Réunion ordinary passports: advance territory visa required
policies.summary: The current DROM order requires a valid territory-specific visa unless an Annex II nationality exemption applies. This covers the ordinary-passport baseline after direct waivers and genuinely unresolved biometric rows are removed.
conditions: A valid visa must cover Réunion; a Schengen visa alone does not authorize the territory. France-Visas' online workflow is application filing, not eVisa issuance.

French multi-entry-visa, residence-permit, long-stay visa, agency package, cruise, transit, crew, special/diplomatic/service passport and individual-admission exceptions remain conditional and do not change this ordinary-passport baseline.

Georgia's former Annex II exemption was removed effective June 2025. Vanuatu's waiver is restricted to pre-25-May-2015 ordinary passports, so it cannot establish a current unqualified ordinary-passport exemption.

policies.title: Other Mayotte ordinary passports: advance territory visa required
policies.summary: The current Mayotte order requires a valid territory-specific visa unless an Annex II nationality exemption applies. This covers the ordinary-passport baseline after direct waivers and genuinely unresolved biometric rows are removed.
conditions: A valid visa must cover Mayotte; a Schengen visa alone does not authorize the territory. France-Visas' online workflow is application filing, not eVisa issuance.

French multi-entry-visa, residence-permit, long-stay visa, cruise, transit, crew, special/diplomatic/service passport and individual-admission exceptions remain conditional and do not change this ordinary-passport baseline.

Georgia's former Annex II exemption was removed effective June 2025. Vanuatu's waiver is restricted to pre-25-May-2015 ordinary passports, so it cannot establish a current unqualified ordinary-passport exemption.

policies.title: Norwegian ordinary passports: visitor visa issued on arrival
policies.summary: Tonga Revenue’s current schedule names Norway for a visitor visa on arrival, and Norway’s current Foreign Ministry advice independently states that Norwegian citizens receive a visa on arrival. This is normalized as visa_on_arrival; the sources’ stated durations are not combined.
conditions: Revenue qualifies arrival issuance with a valid return ticket, sufficient funds, and immigration decision; the Norwegian advice states a stay up to 90 days, while Revenue describes 30 days.
This is an ordinary-passport short-visitor mapping only; it establishes no work, residence, transit, special-document, biometric, or individual-admission entitlement.
The older Embassy page’s Schengen visa-free wording conflicts with the two current government guidance sources and is not used to normalize this code as visa_free.

policies.title: Bahrain: named online-eligible ordinary passports with eVisa route
policies.summary: For these previously unsupported passport rows whose snapshot already records eVisa, NPRA's live country list names the country as online-eligible and its process page confirms an NPRA-reviewed online visa issuance workflow.
conditions: This policy is confined to ordinary-passport rows that were previously unsupported and already normalized as eVisa in the snapshot. The live online list names the corresponding countries, but says terms and conditions apply and directs a traveller to country-specific eligibility; it does not establish an unconditional exemption or a special-passport rule.

The portal describes a genuine pre-travel electronic-visa workflow: the traveller completes the online eligibility and application flow, uploads documents, pays, undergoes NPRA processing, and receives approval notification. It is not merely an arrival-registration form.

Passport validity, funds, accommodation, return/onward travel, sponsor, prior-document, residence, GCC-status, profession, purpose, fee, duration, entry-count, security, sanctions, and final-admission conditions remain traveller- and visa-type-specific. They were not exposed as a reproducible code-level crosswalk in this review.

The separately promoted GCC-citizenship exemption, Bahrain citizenship, GCC-resident eVisa, family, work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, emergency, refugee, and other special-document routes are not classified by this policy. Border officers retain final admission authority.

application.label: Bahrain NPRA eVisa service
steps: Use the official service's eligibility flow and select the applicable visa type and conditions.
Complete the online application, upload the required documents, and pay the required application fee.
Await NPRA review and approval before travel; present the issued visa and any required entry documents for border examination.

policies.title: Bahrain: Iran, North Korea, and Kosovo ordinary passports requiring advance visa
policies.summary: Iran, North Korea, and Kosovo are not named in either live NPRA online or on-arrival country schedule. Bahrain's National Portal expressly gives the residual rule that a non-on-arrival country needs an entry visa issued in advance through an embassy, sponsor, or travel agency.
conditions: This is the National Portal's explicit advance-issuance residual for nationalities outside the on-arrival schedule, read with the current online and on-arrival country schedules. It is not inferred from a commercial passport index or from a failed application.

The cited schedules do not name these three catalog passport codes. The National Portal describes advance issuance through a Bahrain embassy in the country of residence, a Bahraini sponsor, or a travel agency; it does not establish a nationality-wide self-service eVisa route for them.

This policy does not decide any resident-, GCC-status-, third-country-document-, invitation-, work-, residence-, transit-, diplomatic-, official-, service-, refugee-, emergency-, or special-document exception. Visa issuance, security screening, sanctions, carrier checks, and final admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Chilean citizens: citizenship entry status
policies.summary: Chile's Foreign Ministry provides Chileans abroad without valid identity documents a safe-conduct document to travel to Chile. An ordinary Chilean passport therefore represents citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa route.
conditions: This is supported by the Foreign Ministry's direct Chilean return-document route, rather than inferred solely from matching catalog codes.
It does not determine treatment of a dual national presenting a different passport, an individual document-validity issue, departure controls, or any foreign visitor status.

policies.title: Uruguayan citizens: citizenship entry status
policies.summary: Uruguay's Foreign Ministry supplies a one-way return travel document to Uruguayan nationals or legal citizens whose travel document is unavailable. An ordinary Uruguayan passport therefore represents citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa route.
conditions: This is supported by the Foreign Ministry's direct return-document route, rather than inferred solely from matching catalog codes.
It does not determine treatment of a dual national presenting a different passport, individual document-validity issues, departure controls, residence, or any foreign visitor status.

policies.title: Hong Kong SAR ordinary passport: Category A visa exemption
policies.summary: El Salvador's current Foreign Ministry ordinary-passport table expressly includes Hong Kong among the Special Administrative Regions of the PRC and assigns Category A, exempt from visa.
conditions: The table distinguishes ordinary from diplomatic, official and service passports; this policy is only for the ordinary Hong Kong SAR passport row.
The table separately describes treatment of British passports held by Hong Kong-origin travellers. It does not change this direct Hong Kong SAR ordinary-passport classification.
Purpose, CA-4 stay limits, passport validity, carrier, security and final admission conditions remain outside this visa-category classification.

policies.title: Albanian ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: An Albanian national travelling on an ordinary Albanian passport is classified as citizenship, not as a foreign visitor visa category.
conditions: This is a citizenship classification only; it does not characterize the rules for foreign passport holders or non-national travel documents.

policies.title: Albania: named ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: MEFA's current interactive country table marks the listed national-passport Type C entries WITHOUT VISA. Saudi Arabia and Qatar are excluded because MEFA states their separate temporary tourism-only waiver.
conditions: This is the ordinary national-passport short Type C baseline as displayed in MEFA's selector. It does not generalize the selector's diplomatic, service, residence, work, airport-transit or long-stay fields.
Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan are mapped only to the respective passport entries named by MEFA's table; this does not infer citizenship from a territory code.
Passport validity, maximum permitted stay, purpose, funds, health, security and final border-admission requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Albania: Saudi and Qatari ordinary passports temporarily visa-free for tourism
policies.summary: MEFA expressly waives visas for Saudi Arabian and Qatari citizens travelling with a passport only for tourism from 15 April through 31 December 2026. This current temporary exemption is narrower than a general nationality baseline.
conditions: Only tourism and a passport are expressly covered; work, residence, transit, diplomatic, service, special-document and other purposes remain outside this policy.
The temporary period must be rechecked after 31 December 2026, together with ordinary passport-validity and final-admission requirements.

policies.title: Albania: named ordinary passports requiring a Type C visa, available as an electronic visa
policies.summary: MEFA's current selector marks this named ordinary-national-passport cohort WITH VISA for Type C and links the official eVisa service. The official service permits selection of an electronic visa and, when approved, generates and emails it before travel; this is an eVisa rather than an ETA, visa on arrival or mere online authorization.
conditions: The applicant must be outside Albania, use the travel document registered in the application, complete the online process and obtain approval before travel. If approved, the electronic visa is generated and emailed; it must be held at the border crossing point.

The official service also offers a stamped-visa option. This policy records the available electronically issued visa as the normalized, easier ordinary-passport route, not an assertion that every applicant must choose it.

A used multiple-entry Schengen, EU, US or UK visa/residence permit, UAE ten-year residence permit, Schengen visa-free status and named EU travel documents can create conditional visa-free entry; those document/residence routes do not change this nationality baseline.

Visitor Type C is up to 90 days in 180 days. Work, residence, transit, diplomatic/service, special passport, sanctions, passport-validity and discretionary admission rules are outside this baseline; visa approval does not guarantee admission.

application.label: Albania official eVisa application
application.processingTime: The official portal says assessment normally takes up to 15 working days and may take up to 30 days in exceptional cases.
steps: Select Electronic Visa in the official eVisa service while outside Albania and submit the required Type C visitor application and documents.
After approval, download the digitally signed electronic visa sent by email and carry it with the registered travel document at the border.

policies.title: Albania: ordinary passports not named in MEFA's table, electronic-visa baseline
policies.summary: MEFA expressly says foreign citizens from countries not included in its table must have a visa before travel and directs applicants to its official eVisa service. That service offers an electronic visa, generated and sent by email after approval, establishing the residual advance eVisa route without using table omission alone as the rule.
conditions: This residual follows MEFA's express all-unlisted advance-visa rule and official eVisa route, not an inference from a portal nationality selector or unverified territorial citizenship equivalence.
Conditional visa-free treatment based on used third-country visas, residence permits, Schengen status, UAE residence or specified EU travel documents remains separate and is not generalized here.

The policy is ordinary passport, short visitor Type C only. Work, residence, airport transit, crew, diplomatic/service/special passports, sanctions, travel-document recognition, passport validity and final admission remain separate conditions.

application.label: Albania official eVisa application
application.processingTime: The official portal says assessment normally takes up to 15 working days and may take up to 30 days in exceptional cases.
steps: Select Electronic Visa in the official eVisa service while outside Albania and submit the required Type C visitor application and documents.
After approval, download the digitally signed electronic visa sent by email and carry it with the registered travel document at the border.

policies.title: Current MFA nationality schedule: visa-free short visitors
policies.summary: The current MFA diplomatic-post schedule expressly lists these nationalities as visa-exempt. China is added separately only because a current mutual ordinary-passport agreement expressly establishes its exemption.
conditions: The MFA page says the listed nationalities may stay visa-free for one year. China is limited by its mutual ordinary-passport agreement to a single stay of up to 30 days and an aggregate 90 days in 180 days.

This is only the ordinary short-visitor nationality baseline. It does not establish work, residence, study, journalism, diplomatic, official, service, crew, transit, refugee, stateless, special travel-document, dual-nationality, or purpose-specific treatment.
A valid third-country visa or residence permit can create a separate 90-in-180 visa-free route under Ordinance No. 256; that document/status exception is not a passport-wide classification.
The Law permits refusal for missing documents, bans, false data, lack of insurance or funds, security, public-order or foreign-policy grounds. Border admission remains case-specific.
Foreign citizens and stateless persons may enter Abkhazia only via Zugdidi and the Tskhinvali region only via Gori; other directions are prohibited. This territorial rule is not nationality-specific.

policies.title: Named eVisa countries: supporting-document cohort
policies.summary: The live official eVisa country page explicitly assigns these passport/country entries to the cohort that is eligible only with a valid Schengen or OECD visa or residence-permit supporting document.
conditions: The portal requires a valid supporting document: a Schengen visa, a valid visa from an OECD member, or a valid Schengen/OECD residence permit.

For tourist eVisa applications it lists biometric photo, passport/travel-document copy, supporting document, accommodation proof, return ticket unless using other transport, travel insurance and proof of funds.

The electronic-visa statute requires an application through the MFA's special webpage while abroad; the portal describes eVisa as short-stay only and its FAQ says issuance follows email delivery and printing.

The current application page requires the travel document to remain valid at least three months after the requested Georgian visa. Where an Israeli visa is relied on at the border, it says a physical Israeli visa stamp is mandatory and an Israeli electronic visa is not accepted.

This does not treat a third-country visa/residence permit as passport-wide visa-free entry; it is an eVisa eligibility/document condition. Other purpose, special-document, admission, security and occupied-territory rules remain outside the classification.

application.label: Georgia eVisa application
application.processingTime: The statutory maximum for a short-term electronic visa is five working days after a complete webpage application.
steps: Apply from outside Georgia through the eVisa portal using the passport/travel document selected for travel.
Upload the cohort-specific supporting document and the tourist documents required by the portal, then complete payment.
Complete the mandatory DuVerify step sent by email within 24 hours, then receive and print the electronic visa for border examination.

policies.title: Named eVisa countries: standard-document cohort
policies.summary: The live official eVisa country page explicitly names these passport/country entries in its standard document cohort for tourist or business eVisa applications.
conditions: For tourists the portal lists biometric photo, passport/travel-document copy, accommodation proof, return ticket unless using other transport, travel insurance and proof of funds.
For business visitors it lists biometric photo, passport/travel-document copy, accommodation proof, return ticket unless using other transport, travel insurance and proof of travel purpose.

The electronic-visa statute requires an application through the MFA's special webpage while abroad; the portal describes eVisa as short-stay only and its FAQ says issuance follows email delivery and printing.

The current application page requires the travel document to remain valid at least three months after the requested Georgian visa. Where an Israeli visa is relied on at the border, it says a physical Israeli visa stamp is mandatory and an Israeli electronic visa is not accepted.

This does not treat a third-country visa/residence permit as passport-wide visa-free entry; it is an eVisa eligibility/document condition. Other purpose, special-document, admission, security and occupied-territory rules remain outside the classification.

application.label: Georgia eVisa application
application.processingTime: The statutory maximum for a short-term electronic visa is five working days after a complete webpage application.
steps: Apply from outside Georgia through the eVisa portal using the passport/travel document selected for travel.
Upload the tourist or business documents stated for the cohort, then complete payment.
Complete the mandatory DuVerify step sent by email within 24 hours, then receive and print the electronic visa for border examination.

policies.title: Named eVisa countries: minimal-document cohort
policies.summary: The live official eVisa country page explicitly names these passport/country entries in its third document cohort, which lists a biometric photo and travel-document copy.
conditions: The portal's third cohort lists a biometric photo and copy of a valid travel document/passport. It does not state that these are the only documents a case or border examination may require.

The electronic-visa statute requires an application through the MFA's special webpage while abroad; the portal describes eVisa as short-stay only and its FAQ says issuance follows email delivery and printing.

The current application page requires the travel document to remain valid at least three months after the requested Georgian visa. Where an Israeli visa is relied on at the border, it says a physical Israeli visa stamp is mandatory and an Israeli electronic visa is not accepted.
This does not establish visa-free entry or a visa-on-arrival route. Other purpose, special-document, admission, security and occupied-territory rules remain outside the classification.

application.label: Georgia eVisa application
application.processingTime: The statutory maximum for a short-term electronic visa is five working days after a complete webpage application.
steps: Apply from outside Georgia through the eVisa portal using the passport/travel document selected for travel.
Upload the documents stated by the portal and complete payment.
Complete the mandatory DuVerify step sent by email within 24 hours, then receive and print the electronic visa for border examination.

policies.title: Georgian citizens: entry without permit
policies.summary: Georgia's entry law expressly allows a Georgian citizen to enter Georgia at any time without a permit; this is citizenship, not a foreign visitor-visa category.
conditions: The law says a Georgian citizen enters temporarily with a Georgian passport, a return certificate, or another treaty-recognised substitute. This policy records citizenship only and does not decide passport issuance, dual citizenship, departure limits, identity checks or other formalities.

policies.title: Azerbaijani citizens’ entry right
policies.summary: The Migration Code implements an Azerbaijani citizen's entry right through that citizen's Azerbaijani passport.
conditions: This citizenship policy does not determine treatment of a foreign passport held by a dual national.
General individual border restrictions or document issues are not represented by passport-nationality status.

policies.title: Temporary visa-free admission for Gulf ordinary passports
policies.summary: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Saudi Arabia have a temporary ordinary-passport visitor waiver from 15 February 2026 through 15 February 2027.
conditions: Visa-free entry is limited to three entries in one year and up to 30 days per entry.
The waiver is for ordinary-passport visitors for tourism; other purposes or longer stays require the relevant visa.
The separate visa-at-airport route for holders of specified third-country residence permits is conditional and is not classified here.
Individual entry restrictions and document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Temporary visa-free admission for Japanese and Korean ordinary passports
policies.summary: Japan and the Republic of Korea have a temporary ordinary-passport visitor waiver from 1 July 2026 through 1 July 2027.
conditions: Visa-free entry is limited to three entries in one year and up to 30 days per entry.
A valid visa is required at a fourth entry within the stated one-year period.
Individual entry restrictions and document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Temporary visa-free admission for Bosnian and Singaporean ordinary passports
policies.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina and Singapore have a temporary ordinary-passport visitor waiver from 1 August 2026 through 1 August 2027.
conditions: Visa-free entry is limited to three entries in one year and up to 30 days per entry.
A valid visa is required at a fourth entry within the stated one-year period.
Individual entry restrictions and document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: ASAN Visa eligible ordinary-passport nationalities
policies.summary: The live ASAN Visa eligibility schedule identifies these nationalities for electronically issued single-entry visitor eVisas.
conditions: The eVisa is electronically issued after ASAN Visa processing; the MFA online application-form portal for consular visas is not itself eVisa issuance.
A standard eVisa is issued within three working days and an urgent eVisa within three hours; it is single-entry, valid for 90 days, and permits a stay of up to 30 days.
The travel document must remain valid for at least three months after eVisa expiry; the approved eVisa must be printed and presented at the border.
The eVisa does not authorize paid work; media activity needs MFA accreditation. Stays over 15 days require registration.
The ASAN schedule's temporary visa-free markings take precedence for the separately dated waiver policies, so those nationalities are excluded here.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: A Serbian national travelling on an ordinary Serbian passport is classified as citizenship, not under Serbia's foreign-visitor visa regime.
conditions: This is a citizenship classification only. The cited law requires entry to be allowed when the person is established as a Serbian citizen, even without a travel document.
It does not establish foreign-passport, dual-national documentation, residence, work, transit, or final border-control treatment.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free up to 90 days in six months, with stated identity-card route
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for these ordinary passports for up to 90 days in six months and separately state that an identity card can be used to travel to Serbia.
conditions: The policy records the ordinary-passport visitor baseline. The separate identity-card statement is not an ordinary-passport expansion and depends on the stated bilateral agreement or Government decision.
It does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
A valid document, purpose and financial proof may be required; border admission remains discretionary under the published entry requirements.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for these ordinary passports for visits of up to 90 days in a six-month period from first entry.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport visitor baseline only. It does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
A valid document, purpose and financial proof may be required; border admission remains subject to the MFA's published refusal conditions.

policies.title: Argentina ordinary passport: tourism visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA's Argentina page specifically waives a visa for tourist visits up to 90 days in a six-month period from first entry.
conditions: The published waiver is expressly for tourist visits; it does not establish work, residence, airport transit, business, diplomatic, official/service, or special-document treatment.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free up to 90 days in 180 days
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for these ordinary passports for up to 90 days within the stated 180-day period.
conditions: This is limited to the named ordinary-passport visitor baseline and does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free up to 30 days in one year
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for these ordinary passports for up to 30 days within one year.
conditions: This is limited to the named ordinary-passport visitor baseline and does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free up to 30 days
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for these ordinary passports for visits of up to 30 days.
conditions: This is limited to the named ordinary-passport visitor baseline and does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Holy See and South Korean ordinary passports: visa-free up to 90 days
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for Holy See and South Korean ordinary passports for visits of up to 90 days.
conditions: This is limited to the named ordinary-passport visitor baseline and does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Moldovan biometric ordinary passport: visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA limits Moldova's 90-day-in-six-month visa exemption to biometric passports.
conditions: Only a biometric ordinary passport is established. Non-biometric, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service and other special travel documents are not covered by this policy.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Montenegrin ordinary passport: visa-free up to 90 days
policies.summary: The MFA waives visas for Montenegrin ordinary passports for up to 90 days and separately notes a stated identity-and-citizenship document route.
conditions: The identity-and-citizenship document statement is a separate document route, not an expansion of this ordinary-passport policy.

This policy does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access; final admission remains subject to published border requirements.

policies.title: Hong Kong SAR passport: visa-free up to 14 days
policies.summary: The Serbian MFA's China page waives visas for Chinese citizens holding an SAR Hong Kong passport for visits up to 14 days.
conditions: The exemption is document-specific: it applies to a Chinese citizen holding an SAR Hong Kong passport and must not be generalized to other Chinese travel documents.
The live MFA country page displays a 3 April 2018 update date, so the result is retained with medium confidence pending a newer official restatement.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Macao SAR passport: visa-free up to 90 days
policies.summary: The Serbian MFA's China page waives visas for Chinese citizens holding an SAR Macao passport for visits up to 90 days.
conditions: The exemption is document-specific: it applies to a Chinese citizen holding an SAR Macao passport and must not be generalized to other Chinese travel documents.
The live MFA country page displays a 3 April 2018 update date, so the result is retained with medium confidence pending a newer official restatement.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visitor visa required
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages mark these ordinary passports as requiring a Serbian visa. The policy records the short-visitor baseline, not an electronic-visa cohort.
conditions: This is the ordinary national-passport short-visitor baseline. The short-stay C visa may cover tourism, business and other travel up to 90 days in 180; employment, education and family residence are separate long-stay D or residence matters.

Serbia has genuinely issued Digital Travel Authorizations since 23 April 2025, but the MFA only makes them available to countries enabled on the Government portal. It publishes no exhaustive current nationality mapping, so online filing or issuance is not normalized as a nationality-wide eVisa entitlement here.

A holder of a valid Schengen, UK, EU-member-state or United States visa, or a Schengen/EU/US residence permit, has a separately stated up-to-90-day document-conditioned visa-free route. That route is not inferred from passport nationality and does not alter this baseline.

Visa issuance and entry remain subject to passport validity, purpose, invitation or travel proof, funds, insurance, security, sanctions, health, transit and final border-admission requirements. This policy establishes no diplomatic, official/service, emergency, refugee or other special-document result.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: short visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry's current country schedule expressly exempts these ordinary passports for the stated short tourist, business, transit, or general-visit period.
conditions: The Ministry gives country-specific periods: most are 90 days in 180 days, while Belarus, Brunei, Costa Rica, Indonesia, Mongolia, Russia, Thailand, Venezuela, and Macao have expressly different limits. China is expressly effective from 2026-01-02.

Where the schedule says tourism, business, transit, or tourist purpose, that stated purpose limitation remains. Work, study, residence, documentary filming, research, excavation, truck-driver, crew, diplomatic, official, and special-document regimes are not flattened into this policy.

The Law's general maximum is 90 days in 180 days unless the applicable exemption states otherwise. A passport or travel document normally must remain valid 60 days beyond the authorised stay, and a visa exemption does not remove admissibility or entry-ban checks.

policies.title: Antigua and Barbuda, Dominican Republic, and Saint Vincent: visa obtainable at entry
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry expressly permits these ordinary passport holders to obtain a visa at Turkish ports of entry; the easier arrival-issued route controls over their parallel e-Visa option.
conditions: The current Ministry schedule says Antigua and Barbuda, the Dominican Republic, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines may obtain three-month multiple-entry visas at ports of entry, as well as by e-Visa or Turkish missions.

This policy is a genuine border-issued visa, not an inference from an online form. Article 13 permits border visas only in exceptional cases and subjects them to applicable documents, insurance, funds, purpose, admissibility, and border-officer requirements.
Work, study, residence, official, service, diplomatic, crew, and special-travel-document rules are outside this ordinary short-visitor policy.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance visa required baseline
policies.summary: For these ordinary passports, the current Foreign Ministry schedule expressly says a visa is required and does not itself establish a reproducible ordinary-passport e-Visa or arrival-visa route.
conditions: This is the current ordinary-passport baseline from the Ministry's country-by-country schedule. The Law normally directs a foreigner without a visa exemption to obtain the purpose-specific visa at a Turkish consulate in the citizenship or legal-residence country.

It does not erase country-specific diplomatic, official, service, special, crew, residence, work, study, transit, or other exceptional arrangements. Visas do not confer an absolute right of entry and remain subject to statutory document, insurance, funds, security, health, purpose, and entry-ban controls.

policies.title: Turkish ordinary passport: citizen admission
policies.summary: A person claiming Turkish citizenship is statutorily admitted at Türkiye's border once the prescribed citizenship evidence is established.
conditions: Passport Law No. 5682 requires normal passport or valid substitute-document presentation at entry and specifies admission even where a claimant arrives without one once Turkish citizenship is proved.
This is a citizen-entry rule, not a foreign visitor visa or passport-waiver classification.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: A Russian national using an ordinary Russian passport is classified as citizenship rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: Article 27(2) establishes a Russian citizen's right to return freely. This classification is limited to Russian citizenship and does not establish a rule for dual nationals travelling as foreign citizens or for non-national travel documents.

policies.title: Russia: ordinary passports visa-free up to 90 days
policies.summary: The current MFA country table gives these ordinary-passport nationalities a visa-free short-visitor baseline of up to 90 days.
conditions: The country table's stated 90-day ordinary-passport or all-passport waiver controls; passport validity, migration registration, purpose, admission and any shorter treaty condition remain applicable.
This is not a work, residence, diplomatic, service, crew, APEC-card, local-border or special-document classification.

policies.title: Russia: ordinary passports visa-free where the current MFA table states no duration
policies.summary: The current MFA country table expressly says these nationalities are visa-free for all passport types but does not state a nationality-specific duration in the displayed entry.
conditions: Do not infer an unlimited visitor stay from the table's silence on duration; immigration, registration, document and final-admission rules remain applicable.
The stated all-passport waivers may also permit specified internal identity documents, but this policy covers the ordinary passport relationship only.

policies.title: Russia: ordinary passports visa-free up to 30 days
policies.summary: The current MFA table gives these ordinary passports a short visa-free baseline of up to 30 days.
conditions: Bosnia and Herzegovina is limited to 30 days in 60; the other displayed ordinary-passport waivers state up to 30 days.
This excludes diplomatic, service, crew, APEC-card, invitation, organized-tour and other special routes.

policies.title: Russia: ordinary passports visa-free up to 60 days
policies.summary: The current MFA table gives Dominican Republic, Republic of Korea, Mauritius, Samoa and Cabo Verde ordinary passports a visa-free stay of up to 60 days.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport visitor baseline only; it excludes the separately listed diplomatic, service, accredited-staff and other document routes.

policies.title: Russia: Brunei and Nauru ordinary passports visa-free up to 14 days
policies.summary: The current MFA table records a 14-day visa-free short-stay rule for Brunei and Nauru.
conditions: This is a short visitor baseline; purpose, passport, registration and final border-admission rules remain separate.

policies.title: Russia: Chinese ordinary passports temporarily visa-free
policies.summary: The MFA table grants Chinese ordinary passports visa-free entry for up to 30 days only through 14 September 2026.
conditions: This is a temporary ordinary-passport waiver. The table separately lists diplomatic/service treatment, organized-tour groups, crews and APEC-card routes.
Recheck after 14 September 2026; the unified e-visa route is separately available.

policies.title: Russia: Hong Kong and Macao permanent residents with the stated SAR passports visa-free
policies.summary: The MFA table limits the Hong Kong and Macao passport waivers to permanent residents holding the respective valid SAR passport.
conditions: Hong Kong is up to 14 days and Macao up to 30 days, each only for a permanent resident holding the matching valid SAR passport.
This does not infer eligibility for another Chinese, British, Portuguese, residence or travel-document category.

policies.title: Russia: Serbian biometric ordinary passports visa-free up to 30 days
policies.summary: The MFA table makes the Serbian ordinary-passport waiver conditional on a biometric passport and limits it to 30 days.
conditions: Only an ordinary biometric Serbian passport is covered, for up to 30 days; diplomatic and service rules are separate.

policies.title: Russia: Omani ordinary passports visa-free with annual cap
policies.summary: The MFA table gives Omani ordinary passports visa-free entry up to 30 days per visit, capped at 90 days in a calendar year.
conditions: The 30-day-per-visit and 90-day-per-calendar-year limits apply. The e-visa is an alternative route, not an extension of the visa-free allowance.

policies.title: Russia: Saudi ordinary passports visa-free with annual cap
policies.summary: The MFA table grants Saudi Arabian ordinary passports visa-free entry for up to 90 days in a calendar year.
conditions: The 90-days-per-calendar-year cap applies. The unified e-visa remains an alternative, more restrictive route.

policies.title: Russia: Myanmar ordinary passports visa-free with annual cap
policies.summary: The current MFA country table grants Myanmar ordinary passports visa-free entry up to 30 days per visit, with a 90-day calendar-year cap.
conditions: The 30-day-per-visit and 90-day-per-calendar-year limits apply. The live unified-eVisa portal still lists Myanmar, so this current table-controlled visa-free baseline needs monitoring.

policies.title: Russia: named ordinary passports eligible for the unified electronic visa
policies.summary: The current MFA country table identifies this cohort as eligible for a unified e-visa. The portal confirms an issued unified e-visa is an actual single-entry electronic visa, not merely an online application or authorization.
conditions: Apply no earlier than 86 and no later than 4 days before entry using a machine-readable national passport issued by the nationality state and valid at least six months from application; each child needs a separate e-visa.
It is single entry, valid 120 days from issue, with a stay of no more than 30 calendar days, through only approved border crossing points. Arrival and departure days both count.
Visitor purposes are private/business visits, tourism, and the stated scientific, cultural, socio-political, economic or sporting events. Other purposes require a regular visa.

Movement is barred to territories, organisations and facilities requiring a special permit. Insurance is required unless reciprocity exempts the nationality; approval and admission remain discretionary.

application.label: Russian MFA unified e-visa application
application.processingTime: No more than 4 calendar days from submission.
steps: Create a personal account on the official MFA e-visa website or use its mobile application.
Submit the application between 86 and 4 days before entry, pay the required fee and respond to any correction request.
Download or save the positive e-visa notification and show it to the carrier and border officer at an approved crossing point.

policies.title: Russia: other modelled ordinary foreign passports require a regular visa
policies.summary: For these nationalities, the current MFA country table states either visas for all passports or only a non-ordinary waiver and does not provide the unified e-visa. The MFA's general rule therefore requires a regular visa.
conditions: This is the ordinary foreign-passport short-visitor baseline. Diplomatic, official, service, special, crew, accredited-staff, APEC-card, group-tour, invitation, local-border and other stated exceptions are not passport-wide access.

A regular visa is obtained through a Russian diplomatic mission or consular post at the person's place of permanent residence. Visa type, invitation, validity, document recognition, purpose, registration and admission requirements remain case-specific.

policies.title: Moldovan ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: A person travelling on a Moldovan ordinary passport is classified as a Moldovan citizen, not under the foreign-visitor visa regime.
conditions: The Border Police states that Moldovan citizens have the right to leave and enter Moldova on a passport issued by the competent authorities.
This citizenship classification does not establish foreign-passport, dual-national document choice, residence, work, transit, or final border-control treatment.

policies.title: Named foreign ordinary passports: visa-free visitor baseline
policies.summary: Moldova's current MFA schedule expressly exempts these foreign nationalities from the visa requirement; Hong Kong and Macao are included only on the stated SAR-passport basis and Qatar is listed under bilateral accords.
conditions: This is the ordinary foreign-passport visitor baseline inferred from the MFA's nationality exemption list. Hong Kong and Macao are expressly limited to holders of their respective SAR passports; Qatar is a separate bilateral-accord exemption.
The cited live schedule does not provide a single duration for this full group, so this candidate does not normalize a length of stay from older embassy pages or country-specific agreements.
It does not establish work, residence, airport transit, refugee, emergency, diplomatic, service, special, identity-card, or other travel-document treatment.

Foreign entrants must hold an accepted valid travel document, meet purpose/means and onward-travel requirements where applicable, and remain subject to refusal, security, public-health, document-validity and final-admission checks.

policies.title: Named foreign ordinary passports: electronic visitor visa available before travel
policies.summary: The MFA's current schedule requires these nationalities to hold a visa, and Moldova's official eVisa portal says all foreigners may request a PDF eVisa for eligible transit or short-stay purposes. This is a genuine electronic-issuance route, not merely online filing.
conditions: The official portal says the eVisa is issued in PDF form and has the same entry right as a sticker visa. Only transit B and short-stay C visas can be obtained online; airport-transit A and long-stay D require a diplomatic mission or consular office.

The portal says all foreigners may request eVisa for listed purposes including business, tourism, visits, mission, sports, transport, culture, humanitarian and scientific activities. It does not establish work, study/residence, airport-transit, diplomatic, service, emergency, refugee or other special-document access.

On 21 August 2026, normal TLS verification of the official portal failed because its server omitted a trusted issuer chain. This transport defect is an operational warning, not evidence that electronic issuance ended; users must not bypass browser certificate warnings.

MFA's required-visa list makes a separate invitation procedure applicable to named nationalities and retains exceptions from that procedure. Its [2] nationalities can instead travel while holding a valid non-transit EU/Schengen, UK, US or Canadian visa or residence permit; that document-conditioned alternative does not change this nationality baseline.

For Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Turkmenistan and Vietnam, MFA footnote [1] preserves treaty-based diplomatic, service and special-passport exceptions; those documents are outside this ordinary-passport policy.
Foreign entrants remain subject to accepted-document, purpose, means, onward-travel, refusal, security, public-health, passport-validity and final border-admission requirements.

application.label: Moldova Government eVisa portal
application.processingTime: The official eVisa guidance says a request is processed in up to 10 days.
steps: Use the Government eVisa portal to select an eligible transit B or short-stay C purpose and complete the application.
Supply the portal's required passport, purpose and any invitation-related materials, then pay the applicable fee.
Receive the PDF eVisa before travel and carry the relevant documents for Border Police admission checks.

policies.title: Montenegro: Article 1 named passport issuers visa-free for 90 days
policies.summary: The current consolidated Regulation's Article 1 grants the listed passport issuers up to 90 days visa-free entry, transit and stay with a valid travel document. This list reflects the consolidated text through Gazette 108/2026, rather than the superseded 2025 web list.
conditions: Valid ordinary travel document issued by the competent authority of the named issuer is required; maximum stay is 90 days.
Hong Kong and Macao are included only because Article 1 expressly names valid travel documents issued by those Special Administrative Regions; this does not infer citizenship from a territory code.

Identity-card, refugee/stateless-document, diplomatic/service-document, third-country visa, residence-permit and APEC-card routes are separate conditional rules and are not generalized by this ordinary-passport policy.
Passport validity, purpose, funds, security checks and final border-admission requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Montenegro: Peruvian ordinary passport visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Article 3 of the current consolidated Regulation allows Peruvian nationals to enter, transit and stay for up to 30 days with a valid travel document under the reciprocal-travel agreement.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid travel document issued by the competent Peruvian authority, under the reciprocal-travel agreement named in Article 3.
This does not extend to diplomatic/service documents, residence, work or other purposes outside the ordinary short-visitor baseline.

policies.title: Montenegro: Belarusian and Russian ordinary passports temporarily visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Article 3a preserves a 30-day visa-free ordinary-travel-document route for Belarus and Russia only through 31 October 2026; the MFA announces visa requirement from 1 November 2026.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid travel document issued by the competent authority, pursuant to the reciprocal-travel agreements named in Article 3a.
This time-limited policy must not be used for travel on or after 1 November 2026; the MFA says a visa then becomes required.

policies.title: Montenegro: Saudi and Turkish ordinary passports temporarily visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Article 1a allows Saudi Arabian and Turkish nationals a 30-day visa-free ordinary-travel-document route only through 31 October 2026; the MFA announces visa requirement from 1 November 2026.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid travel document issued by the competent authority of Saudi Arabia or Türkiye.
This time-limited policy must not be used for travel on or after 1 November 2026; the MFA says a visa then becomes required.

policies.title: Montenegro: Kazakh ordinary passports temporarily visa-free for 30 days
policies.summary: Montenegro MFA's Kazakhstan-specific page states that the ordinary visa baseline is temporarily waived from 1 May to 1 October 2026 for stays up to 30 days.
conditions: Up to 30 days with a valid Kazakh travel document only during the official 1 May to 1 October 2026 seasonal period.
The MFA page states the normal Kazakhstan baseline is visa required; recheck the exact end-of-period treatment before travel after 1 October 2026.

policies.title: Montenegro: Article 4 ordinary-passport visa baseline
policies.summary: For every remaining catalog issuer, Article 4 expressly requires a valid foreign travel document containing a visa. Montenegro's published issuance guidance describes consular issuance, so this is not promoted as an eVisa merely because application support may be arranged online or through a service centre.
conditions: Article 4 is an express residual rule, not an inference from omission: a valid foreign travel document containing a Montenegro visa is required.

No eVisa policy is proposed. The MFA guidance describes visa issuance through diplomatic and consular missions; online filing or a VFS application centre would not itself establish electronic issuance.

For China, Article 6 separately preserves, only through 31 October 2026, 30-day visa-free entry for organized tourist groups with paid-arrangement and return proof, or business-passport holders with an invitation. Those condition-bound routes do not convert the ordinary baseline to visa-free.

Articles 7, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 12a contain separate third-country-visa, residence, special-document, refugee/stateless, diplomatic/service and accreditation exceptions; none changes this ordinary nationality baseline.
Passport validity, stated purpose, documentation, security checks, visa approval and final border admission remain separate requirements.

policies.title: Montenegro: Kazakh ordinary passports require a visa after the 2026 seasonal waiver
policies.summary: After the official seasonal waiver ends on 1 October 2026, Kazakhstan returns to Montenegro's explicit Article 4 advance-visa baseline.
conditions: This future-dated policy must not displace the current seasonal visa-free route on or before 1 October 2026.
The MFA's Kazakhstan page identifies visa-required as the normal baseline; the Article 4 rule requires an advance Montenegro visa and does not establish eVisa issuance.

policies.title: Montenegro: four temporary ordinary-passport waivers end on 1 November 2026
policies.summary: The MFA expressly says Belarusian, Russian, Saudi and Turkish nationals require a visa from 1 November 2026, returning these ordinary passports to the Article 4 baseline.
conditions: This future-dated policy must not displace the current 30-day visa-free route through 31 October 2026.

The announcement also names China, whose ordinary-passport baseline is already visa-required; China's temporary organized-group and business-document exceptions remain separately conditioned through 31 October.
The Article 4 advance visa is issued through a diplomatic or consular mission; no current electronic-issuance route is established.

policies.title: North Macedonian ordinary passport: citizenship and constitutional return
policies.summary: A North Macedonian citizen has a constitutional right to return and is classified as citizenship rather than under the foreign-visitor visa regime.
conditions: This is a citizenship classification supported by the constitutional right to return; it does not determine document formalities for a dual national presenting another passport.
Residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency-document and final border-control treatment remain outside this classification.

policies.title: EU and Schengen ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: The current MFA entry page directly exempts nationals of EU Member States and Schengen signatories from an entry visa.
conditions: The MFA additionally permits these nationals to enter with a valid national identity card; this policy records the ordinary-passport relationship only.

A qualifying EU/Schengen residence permit or multiple-entry Schengen C visa can create a separate 15-day route for other travellers. A temporary 2026 decision creates a similar document-conditioned route for qualifying multiple-entry US, UK or Canadian visas. Neither route expands this nationality cohort.
Document validity, purpose, funds, registration, public-order and final-admission requirements remain applicable; work, residence and special travel documents are outside this policy.

policies.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A traveller using an ordinary Bosnia and Herzegovina passport is classified as a BiH citizen, not as a foreign visitor under the visa regime.
conditions: The Border Police says that a BiH citizen who holds another citizenship is not considered a foreigner in the territory of BiH.
This classification does not establish entry treatment for a dual national presenting another state's passport, nor work, residence, transit or final border-control treatment.

policies.title: Bahrain, Oman and Saudi Arabia ordinary passports: temporary visa-free entry through 30 September 2026
policies.summary: Official Gazette 37/26 exempts ordinary passport holders of Bahrain, Oman and Saudi Arabia from a visa for entry, exit, transit and stay from 1 June through 30 September 2026.
conditions: The waiver is limited to holders of ordinary passports of Bahrain, Oman and Saudi Arabia.
Within the stated temporary period, the aggregate stay permitted is no more than 60 days.
This policy does not establish a rule after 30 September 2026, work, residence, special-passport, document, security or final border-admission treatment.

policies.title: Kosovo ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Kosovo national travelling on a Kosovo ordinary passport is classified as citizenship rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: Article 35 says a Kosovo citizen may not be denied entry. This does not classify a dual national presenting another country's travel document.
Residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency-document and final border-admission treatment are outside this classification.

policies.title: Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Russia ordinary passports: visa required
policies.summary: A signed Government decision and the Official Gazette directly place Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Russia under Kosovo's visa regime.
conditions: Decision No. 21/216 directly subjects Botswana, Namibia and South Africa to the visa regime.
For Russia, the Gazette decision requires a Kosovo visa even for ordinary, official and diplomatic passport holders and holders of listed Schengen documents.
This does not establish eVisa, ETA or nationality-wide visa-on-arrival access. The current Interior guidance retains travel-document, purpose, means, registration and final-admission conditions.

policies.title: Ukraine ordinary passport: temporary visa waiver
policies.summary: Government Decision No. 14/67 temporarily suspends Kosovo's entry-visa regime for Ukrainian citizens until a later Government decision.
conditions: The Gazette says the suspension remains effective until a subsequent Government decision; recheck it before any publication because it has no stated end date.
This establishes no eVisa, ETA, arrival-visa, work, residence or special-document entitlement. Ordinary admission requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Andorran ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: An Andorran national travelling on an Andorran ordinary passport is classified as citizenship, not as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: This is a citizenship classification, not a foreign visitor-visa relationship. The official passport guidance identifies the passport as proof of identity and nationality, and the Government publishes the nationality-by-origin rules.
It does not define travel by a dual national presenting another passport, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free route to Andorra through Spain or France
policies.summary: Andorra issues no visitor visa. Union citizens do not need an entry visa for the Spanish or French access leg, so these ordinary passports have a visa-free visitor route to Andorra.
conditions: Andorra has no airport and is outside Schengen; access is through France or Spain. This status means no visa is needed for the access leg, not that Andorra is a Schengen Member State.
Use a valid passport or national identity card as applicable. Normal document validity, admission and route checks remain.
No Andorran eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival is established.

policies.title: Visa-exempt Schengen-access ordinary passports: visa-free route to Andorra
policies.summary: Andorra issues no visitor visa. These passports are visa-exempt for the needed Schengen access leg under Annex II or equivalent free-movement arrangements, and therefore have a visa-free route to Andorra.
conditions: Andorra is outside Schengen and has no airport; access is through France or Spain. Annex II exempts applicable third-country passports for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
Biometric passport is required for AL, BA, GE, MD, ME, MK, RS, UA and XK. Taiwan requires the identity-card number in the passport; HK and MO require their named SAR passports.
CH, IS, LI and NO follow equivalent free-movement treatment for the access leg; this does not make Andorra part of Schengen.

For non-EU minors, the Andorran guidance expressly requires a two- or multiple-entry Schengen visa. This age-specific requirement is retained and does not convert the adult Annex II ordinary-passport baseline into a visa requirement.
ETIAS is not operating on the research date. Do not normalize its planned future operation as a current ETA requirement.
No Andorran eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established. Passport validity, purpose, funds, return/onward travel and final admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Annex I ordinary passports: Schengen visa required to reach Andorra
policies.summary: Andorra itself issues no visitor visa, but these passports require a Schengen visa to cross the French or Spanish external border needed to reach Andorra. The Andorran Government requires a double-entry or multiple-entry Schengen visa according to planned exits and returns.
conditions: This is a Schengen advance-visa requirement for the actual France/Spain access leg, not a separate Andorran visa: Andorra requires no type of visa.

Obtain a double-entry Schengen visa for one exit from Andorra and return to Schengen; obtain a multiple-entry Schengen visa for several exits and returns. A single-entry visa does not preserve the return leg.
Apply through the competent French or Spanish consular route. A short-stay visa normally concerns up to 90 days in any 180-day period; issuance and final entry are separate.

No Andorran eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival is established. Residence permits, long-stay visas, family-member rights, diplomatic/official/service documents, local-border permits and other exceptions are not flattened into this baseline.

application.label: European Commission: applying for a Schengen visa
application.processingTime: Apply at least 15 days before travel and no earlier than six months before the journey; individual cases can take longer.
steps: Choose the French or Spanish consular route corresponding to the intended Schengen access itinerary and lodging rules.
Apply for a Schengen short-stay visa with enough double or multiple entries for every planned exit from Andorra and return to Schengen.
Receive the visa before travel and present the valid travel document, visa and supporting documents for border control.

policies.title: Nauru ordinary passport: Schengen visa required pending EU waiver agreement
policies.summary: Although Nauru appears in Annex II, its footnote makes exemption conditional on entry into force of an EU waiver agreement. The current Council register says the regime applies only once Nauru and the EU have concluded that agreement; the ordinary-passport route to Andorra therefore remains Schengen visa required.
conditions: Andorra has no separate visitor visa; this is the Schengen visa required for travel through France or Spain to reach Andorra.
The Annex II Nauru footnote is conditional. Do not classify Nauru as visa-free until an official source confirms the EU–Nauru waiver agreement is concluded and in force.
If a visa is required, use double entry for one exit from Andorra and return to Schengen, or multiple entry for several exits and returns.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free short visit to Monaco
policies.summary: For a short visit, Monaco applies the same foreigner entry and circulation regime as France. Union citizens need no French entry visa, therefore have a visa-free visitor route to Monaco.
conditions: This is an ordinary visit of under three months under Monaco's France-aligned entry regime; Monaco is not a Schengen Member State.
Use a valid passport or national identity card as applicable. Admission, document validity, purpose, funds, public-order and route checks remain applicable.
No separate Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources.

policies.title: Visa-exempt French-access ordinary passports: visa-free short visit to Monaco
policies.summary: For a short visit, Monaco applies the same foreigner entry and circulation regime as France. These ordinary passports are visa-exempt for the French access leg under Annex II or equivalent free-movement arrangements and therefore have a visa-free visitor route to Monaco.
conditions: This is a Monaco visit of under three months; the French/Schengen access leg is limited to no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
Biometric passports are required for AL, BA, GE, MD, ME, MK, RS, UA and XK. Taiwan requires an identity-card number in the passport; HK and MO require their named SAR passports.

CH, IS, LI and NO follow equivalent free-movement treatment for the French access leg. Residence permits, refugee/stateless documents, border permits, school groups, paid activity, crew and special passports are not normalized into this ordinary-passport baseline.
No current source establishes a separate nationality-wide Monaco visitor visa rule for minors. A Monaco circulation document for a minor resident is a residence document, not a visitor-access rule.
ETIAS is not operating on the research date. No separate Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources.

policies.title: Nauru ordinary passport: advance visa required pending EU waiver agreement
policies.summary: Nauru remains subject to the French short-stay visa requirement because its Annex-II exemption is conditional on an EU–Nauru waiver agreement that is not concluded.
conditions: This is a French/Schengen advance-visa requirement applied in Monaco under the France–Monaco short-stay convention, not a separately issued Monegasque visitor visa.
Nauru's Annex-II listing does not currently create a waiver: the Regulation's footnote makes it conditional, and the Council says the agreement remains unconcluded.
No Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources. Final French and Monaco admission decisions remain separate.

policies.title: Annex I ordinary passports: advance visa required for Monaco short visit
policies.summary: For a short visit, Monaco applies the French foreigner-entry regime. These passports require the applicable French/Schengen advance visa; a visa valid for France is valid in Monaco.
conditions: This is the French/Schengen advance-visa requirement carried into Monaco's short-stay foreigner regime, not a separately issued Monegasque visitor visa. Visas valid for France are valid in Monaco.
The Monaco visit is under three months. The French/Schengen access leg follows its short-stay rules; residence permits, long-stay visas and special documents are not flattened into this baseline.

The source law provides distinct rules for stays over three months and Monegasque residence permits; those are not visitor-visa waivers. ETIAS is not operating and no Monegasque eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established by the reviewed official sources.

policies.title: Sammarinese ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Sammarinese national travelling on a Sammarinese ordinary passport is classified as citizenship rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: The current passport-service charter limits the holder to a Sammarinese citizen. This is a citizenship classification, not a foreign-visitor visa rule.
It does not define entry by a dual national presenting another passport, residence, work, transit, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: San Marino has no separate entry visa for a visitor who is compliant with Schengen access through Italy. Union citizens do not need an entry visa for that access leg.
conditions: This records the ordinary-passport short-visitor route via Italy, not membership of San Marino in Schengen.
San Marino Foreign Affairs says a stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence. Carry a valid passport or equivalent identity document.
No San Marino eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival is established.

policies.title: Visa-exempt Schengen-access ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access
policies.summary: A visitor with these qualifying passports is compliant with the Italian Schengen access rule and may visit San Marino without a separate San Marino entry visa.
conditions: San Marino requires the necessary Schengen entry and transit authorisations before departure; a stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence.

Biometric passport is required for AL, BA, GE, MK, MD, ME, RS, UA and XK. The Italian MFA schedule excludes Serbian Coordination Directorate passports; Taiwan requires the identity-card number; HK and MO require their named SAR passports.
CH, IS, LI and NO follow equivalent free-movement treatment for the Italian access leg; this does not make San Marino part of Schengen.

ETIAS is not operating on the research date. Schengen residence-permit and family-status routes are document-conditioned exceptions outside this passport-code baseline, as are special passport and refugee-document rules.
Minor-specific identity, parental-authorisation and carrier or Italian controls are outside this adult ordinary-passport classification.

policies.title: Schengen-visa-required ordinary passports: visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: These ordinary passports require the Italian/Schengen visa needed for access through Italy; San Marino does not issue a separate entry visa.
conditions: This is the advance Schengen visa required for entry through Italy, not a separate San Marino visa. The Italian MFA describes a visa sticker affixed to the passport or other travel document; no eVisa status is established.
San Marino requires the necessary Schengen authorisation before departure; a local stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence.

Italian entry conditions separately require a valid travel document, purpose and means evidence, a visa where prescribed, and no refusal/security ground. A Schengen residence permit holder has a separately stated 90-in-180 visa exemption; that document-conditioned route does not change this ordinary-passport nationality baseline.
Minor, diplomatic/official/service, refugee/stateless, residence, work, transit and other special-document exceptions are not flattened into this policy.

application.label: Italian MFA entry-visa information
application.processingTime: The cited page does not publish a universal decision-time promise; consult the competent Italian consular post for the itinerary and residence location.
steps: Apply through the competent Italian consular channel for the Schengen access itinerary.
Obtain the Schengen visa sticker in the valid travel document before travelling to Italy and onward to San Marino.
Present the visa, passport and supporting entry documents for Italian border control; carry identity documentation in San Marino.

policies.title: Nauru ordinary passport: Schengen visa required pending EU waiver
policies.summary: Nauru's Annex II exemption is conditional on entry into force of an EU waiver agreement. The current Council register says visa-free travel applies only once Nauru and the EU conclude that agreement, so the route through Italy remains visa required.
conditions: This is the Schengen visa needed for Italian entry before visiting San Marino; a local stay exceeding 30 days requires a stay permit or residence.
Do not classify Nauru as visa-free until an official source confirms the EU–Nauru waiver agreement is concluded and in force.
No San Marino eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established.

policies.title: Belarusian ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: A person travelling on a Belarusian ordinary passport is classified as a Belarusian citizen, not under the foreign-visitor visa regime.
conditions: The Constitution gives Belarusian citizens a right to return without hindrance. This citizenship classification does not determine treatment where a dual national presents another passport.
It does not establish foreign-passport, residence, work, transit or final border-control treatment.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: bilateral visitor visa-free baseline
policies.summary: The MFA's current bilateral table expressly names these ordinary passport holders as visa-free, with the stated country-specific duration limits.
conditions: The MFA table gives the particular limits: Albania 30 days per entry and 90 per year; Argentina 90 per year; Brazil, Colombia, Mongolia, Qatar, UAE and Venezuela 90 days; Cuba, Laos, Montenegro, Myanmar, Oman, Serbia, Türkiye and Vietnam 30 days; Israel 90 in 180 days.

China is 30 days per entry and 90 days in a calendar year. Hong Kong and Macao are limited to their respective SAR passports as stated in the MFA table; this must not be generalized to other Chinese documents.

The source does not give one pooled duration for Armenia, Azerbaijan, Ecuador, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Russia, Ukraine or Uzbekistan; this candidate does not import durations from secondary materials.

Work, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, service, special, emergency and other-document rules are not established by this ordinary-passport visitor policy. Final admission and entry-document checks remain applicable.

policies.title: Named European ordinary passports: temporary visa-free entry through 31 December 2026
policies.summary: The State Border Committee's current temporary programme waives visas for these named ordinary passports; this policy excludes North Macedonia because its bilateral MFA waiver already establishes its baseline.
conditions: Lithuanian and Latvian ordinary passport holders have the programme from 15 April 2022 and Poland from 1 July 2022: up to 90 days per visit and 90 days in a calendar year.
The remaining named passports have the programme from 19 July 2024: up to 30 days per entry and 90 days in a calendar year.
Entry and exit may use any Belarus international border checkpoint. Work, study or residence requires the appropriate Belarusian visa; transit to a third country is permitted except via Russia.

A valid document, medical insurance, stay funds, migration-card and final border-admission requirements continue to apply; diplomatic, service and special passports are outside this ordinary-passport policy.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: airport-route visa-free entry up to 30 days
policies.summary: The MFA's current 76-country airport programme provides a route-limited, ordinary-passport visa-free visitor option for this non-overlapping subset; it is not a general land-border waiver.
conditions: Entry and exit are only through Minsk National Airport, Airport Brest, Airport Gomel, Airport Grodno, Airport Mogilev or Airport Vitebsk. Arrival from, or planned flight to, Russia is excluded.
Stay is at most 30 calendar days and cannot be extended. The traveller needs an ordinary passport valid 90 days after departure, funds and Belarus-valid EUR 10,000 medical insurance.

For the airport programme, Egypt, Gambia, Haiti, India, Iran, Jordan, Lebanon, Namibia, Pakistan, Samoa, South Africa and Vietnam require a used multiple-entry EU/Schengen visa and an air ticket confirming departure from one of the stated Belarus airports within 30 days. Vietnam's separate bilateral waiver is prioritized in the preceding policy.
Diplomatic, service, special and equivalent passports are excluded. Registration and final border-admission checks continue to apply.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: electronic visitor visa issued before travel
policies.summary: The official E-Pasluga eligibility list and MFA guidance establish a genuine pre-travel electronic visa for these named ordinary passports after all visa-free priority routes are removed.
conditions: This is a single-entry individual electronic visa, issued for no more than 30 days, for business, specified events, private affairs or tourism. It is not merely an online filing system: the official service sends a PDF visa or a refusal decision.
Apply through E-Pasluga service 3.04.01 at least seven calendar days before entry, then print and carry the electronic visa. It is valid through all international Belarus checkpoints.
