It does not establish work, study, residence, airport transit, diplomatic, service, special, emergency, refugee or other-document treatment. Entry from Russia on Belarus e-visas remains technically barred according to the MFA.

The all-nationality Brest-Grodno 15-day tourist-zone route and the Belarus-Russia visa/residence-document agreement are separate document- and route-conditioned alternatives; they do not change this nationality baseline.

application.label: Belarus E-Pasluga e-visa issuance service 3.04.01
application.processingTime: The official service says applications must be submitted at least seven calendar days before requested entry.
steps: Register and authenticate with the E-Pasluga portal.
Use service 3.04.01 to submit the electronic visa application and pay the stated fees.
Receive the decision/PDF electronic visa before travel, then carry it at entry and during the stay.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance visitor visa required baseline
policies.summary: Belarus's MFA explicitly requires a visa unless a treaty or Presidential decision provides otherwise. After the current official bilateral, temporary-European, airport and exact e-visa exception lists are applied, this is the ordinary-passport short-visitor complement.
conditions: This is a short-visitor ordinary-passport baseline, established by the MFA's express visa-unless-exception rule and the closed nationality scopes of the current official exception lists; it is not inferred merely from an online portal omission.

The all-nationality Brest-Grodno programme is a separate up-to-15-day tourist-zone route that requires an advance Belarusian travel-agency document, booked tourist service and insurance; it does not create a general passport-wide visa-free baseline.

A valid Belarus or Russian visa may be mutually recognized under the Union State Agreement when paired with a document recognized by both states. A Belarus or Russian residence permit or qualifying event document also has a separate document-conditioned no-visa route; e-visas cannot be used to enter Belarus from Russia.
Minsk airport can issue a visa only after advance visa-support processing (normally at least two business days), so it is not normalized as an unconditioned visa-on-arrival entitlement.

This policy establishes no work, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, service, special, emergency, refugee or other-document result. Visa issuance, sanctions/restrictions, health, security, document and final border-admission checks remain applicable.

policies.title: Nordic nationals: permit-free entry, residence and work
policies.summary: Danish, Finnish, Icelandic, Norwegian and Swedish nationals may enter, reside and work in the Faroe Islands without a permit; this records their ordinary-passport short-visitor outcome as visa-free.
conditions: The territory-specific source states that Nordic nationals can enter, reside and work without a permit. This does not classify any pair as citizenship because the catalog has no Faroe Islands passport issuer code.
Final identity, security, sanctions and border-control checks remain applicable.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: These listed passport holders may enter Denmark visa-free and therefore, under the current Danish territorial rule, may enter the Faroe Islands visa-free for a short visit.
conditions: Visa-free travel is limited to a maximum combined 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen region, Greenland and the Faroe Islands, subject to the stated special Danish calculations for specified nationalities.
A valid travel document, documented purpose and sufficient means are required; refusal, SIS, expulsion, UN/EU sanctions and final border-admission checks apply.
This policy does not establish work, residence, diplomatic, service, special, emergency, refugee, crew or other-document treatment.

policies.title: Named biometric ordinary passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: The Danish official register exempts these named nationalities only when the stated biometric-passport condition is met; the current territorial rule carries that visa-free result to the Faroe Islands.
conditions: A biometric ordinary passport is required. The register gives issue-date information for Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine; Georgia's ordinary passports issued from 28 July 2014 are biometric.
The same combined 90-days-in-180 visa-free maximum, travel-document, purpose, means, sanctions and final-admission conditions apply.

policies.title: Hong Kong, Macao and qualifying Taiwan passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: The Danish register's passport-specific exemptions carry to the Faroe Islands under the current territorial entry rule.
conditions: Hong Kong requires an HKSAR passport and Macao requires a Macao SAR passport. Taiwan requires the stated identity-card number, and older Republic of China passports also require stated Taiwan birthplace and identity-card number.
The policy is visa-free only under the stated document qualifications and ordinary short-visitor conditions; it does not infer a nationality or citizenship classification from a catalog code.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Faroe Islands visitor visa required
policies.summary: These passports are in Denmark's current visa-required nationality schedule without an applicable ordinary-passport exemption and need a visa valid for the Faroe Islands before a short visit.
conditions: The visa sticker must expressly be valid for the Faroe Islands. A Danish/Schengen visa alone does not authorize entry to the Faroe Islands; the standard application and issue route is through a Danish diplomatic mission or Danish representation abroad.
A territorial Faroe Islands visa can authorize a stay of up to 90 days. That territorial-visa maximum is distinct from the combined visa-free 90-days-in-180 calculation.
Online filing does not itself establish an eVisa. An individual border visa may exceptionally be issued under the applicable rules; it does not establish a passport-wide visa-on-arrival route.

A physical residence permit or EU free-movement residence card issued by Denmark, another EU country or another Schengen country is a separate document-conditioned no-visa route. A C or D visa from another Schengen country alone is insufficient unless territorially endorsed; exceptional entry-permit routes do not alter this passport baseline.

Diplomatic, service, official, special, residence, work, transit, refugee and other travel-document exceptions are outside this ordinary-passport policy; visa issuance and final admission remain discretionary.

policies.title: Nordic nationals: permit-free entry, residence and work
policies.summary: Danish, Finnish, Icelandic, Norwegian and Swedish nationals may enter, reside and work in Greenland without a permit; this records their ordinary-passport short-visitor outcome as visa-free.
conditions: The territory-specific source states that Nordic nationals can enter, reside and work without a permit. This does not classify any pair as citizenship because the catalog has no Greenland passport issuer code.
Final identity, security, sanctions and border-control checks remain applicable.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: These listed passport holders may enter Denmark visa-free and therefore, under the current Danish territorial rule, may enter Greenland visa-free for a short visit.
conditions: Visa-free travel is limited to a maximum combined 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen region, Greenland and the Faroe Islands, subject to the stated special Danish calculations for specified nationalities.
A valid travel document, documented purpose and sufficient means are required; refusal, SIS, expulsion, UN/EU sanctions and final border-admission checks apply.
This policy does not establish work, residence, diplomatic, service, special, emergency, refugee, crew or other-document treatment.

policies.title: Named biometric ordinary passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: The Danish official register exempts these named nationalities only when the stated biometric-passport condition is met; the current territorial rule carries that visa-free result to Greenland.
conditions: A biometric ordinary passport is required. The register gives issue-date information for Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine; Georgia's ordinary passports issued from 28 July 2014 are biometric.
The same combined 90-days-in-180 visa-free maximum, travel-document, purpose, means, sanctions and final-admission conditions apply.

policies.title: Hong Kong, Macao and qualifying Taiwan passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: The Danish register's passport-specific exemptions carry to Greenland under the current territorial entry rule.
conditions: Hong Kong requires an HKSAR passport and Macao requires a Macao SAR passport. Taiwan requires the stated identity-card number, and older Republic of China passports also require stated Taiwan birthplace and identity-card number.
The policy is visa-free only under the stated document qualifications and ordinary short-visitor conditions; it does not infer a nationality or citizenship classification from a catalog code.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Greenland visitor visa required
policies.summary: These passports are in Denmark's current visa-required nationality schedule without an applicable ordinary-passport exemption and need a visa valid for Greenland before a short visit.
conditions: The visa sticker must expressly be valid for Greenland. A Danish/Schengen visa alone does not authorize entry to Greenland; the standard application and issue route is through a Danish diplomatic mission or Danish representation abroad.
A territorial Greenland visa can authorize a stay of up to 90 days. That territorial-visa maximum is distinct from the combined visa-free 90-days-in-180 calculation.
Online filing does not itself establish an eVisa. An individual border visa may exceptionally be issued under the applicable rules; it does not establish a passport-wide visa-on-arrival route.

A physical residence permit or EU free-movement residence card issued by Denmark, another EU country or another Schengen country is a separate document-conditioned no-visa route. A C or D visa from another Schengen country alone is insufficient unless territorially endorsed; exceptional entry-permit routes do not alter this passport baseline.

Diplomatic, service, official, special, residence, work, transit, refugee and other travel-document exceptions are outside this ordinary-passport policy; visa issuance and final admission remain discretionary.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: Gibraltar's current treaty-entry guidance applies the EU free-movement regime to Union citizens. These ordinary passports have a visa-free short-visitor route through Gibraltar's dual Gibraltar/Schengen controls.
conditions: Use a valid passport or national identity card as applicable; this is not a Gibraltar or UK citizenship classification.

The Gibraltar airport route has dual Gibraltar and Schengen immigration checks. Residence, family-member, work, study, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document and individual-admission rules are not normalized into this ordinary-passport visitor baseline.
ETIAS is not operating on the research date. No separate nationality-wide Gibraltar eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established for this cohort.

policies.title: EEA/Swiss ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: Icelandic, Liechtenstein, Norwegian and Swiss ordinary passports have the equivalent-free-movement visitor route applied at Gibraltar's Schengen-aligned external border.
conditions: Carry the valid passport or identity document required for the applicable free-movement route. Gibraltar remains a separate jurisdiction and operates dual Gibraltar/Schengen controls at the airport.
This does not normalize residence, family-member, paid-activity, special-document or individual-admission treatment. ETIAS is not operating on the research date.

policies.title: Named visa-exempt third-country ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: These ordinary-passport jurisdictions are named in Gibraltar's 15 July 2026 visa-exempt appendix and have a visa-free short-visitor route, subject to the simultaneous Schengen entry conditions at Gibraltar's external border.
conditions: The short stay is no more than 90 days in any 180 days, calculated with time in Gibraltar and the Schengen Area. A valid travel document, purpose/conditions of stay, means and other admission checks remain required.

Biometric passports are required for AL, BA, GE, MD, ME, MK, RS, UA and XK. Taiwan requires a passport with an identity-card number; HK and MO require their named SAR passports. Serbian Coordination Directorate passports remain subject to the current Regulation's biometric condition.

A Gibraltar or Schengen residence document, a UK visa or UK immigration status, minor/parental arrangements, crew/seafarer identity documents, refugee/stateless documents, diplomatic/official/service passports and paid activity are separate document- or purpose-conditioned routes, not this ordinary-passport nationality rule.
ETIAS is not operating on the research date. No separate nationality-wide Gibraltar eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is established.

policies.title: Full British-citizen ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: Current UK government Gibraltar guidance states that British nationals on a full British-citizen passport do not need a visa for a short visit.
conditions: This is limited to a full British-citizen passport, as expressly scoped by the UK source; it does not establish treatment for every other British nationality or Gibraltar identity-card holder.
The limit is 90 days in any 180 days, including time in Gibraltar and the Schengen Area. Passport validity, dual controls, EES where applicable and ordinary admission checks remain relevant.
This source establishes visa-free entry only; it does not establish a Gibraltar electronic-issuance or ETA route for this visitor cohort.

policies.title: Schengen advance-visa-required ordinary passports: visitor entry
policies.summary: These ordinary passports require a Schengen short-stay visa before Gibraltar entry. This includes Annex I passports and Nauru, whose Annex II waiver remains conditional. Gibraltar accepts a Schengen short-stay visa; if Gibraltar is the main destination, Spain is the competent issuing Schengen State.
conditions: This is an advance Schengen short-stay visa requirement, not a UK visitor visa. The reviewed primary sources do not establish a general Gibraltar electronic-issuance, UK-ETA or ordinary visa-on-arrival alternative for this cohort; Gibraltar's prior UK visa application platforms ceased operating on 8 July 2026.
Gibraltar recognises Schengen short-stay visas. Where Gibraltar is the main destination, Spain issues the Schengen visa; otherwise competence follows the applicable Schengen rules.

The ordinary visitor stay is no more than 90 days in any 180 days including time in Gibraltar and the Schengen Area. Passport validity, purpose, means, security and other admission conditions remain applicable.

A Schengen residence document, Gibraltar residence/identity card, UK status, civilian sea-crew identity document, family status, paid activity, minor, refugee/stateless or special passport arrangement is not flattened into this nationality baseline.

policies.title: Vatican ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A traveller presenting the current Vatican City State ordinary passport is classified as citizenship rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: Law CXXXI directly identifies citizens of the Vatican City State, and the State directly publishes its current ordinary VA passport. This is a narrow catalogue citizenship classification, not a claim that citizenship automatically grants public access to every controlled Vatican area.

Citizenship, residence and access are governed by Vatican-specific provisions. Dual nationality, residence, work, diplomatic, service, temporary-service and special-document treatment is outside this ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: For a short public visit, these travellers need no entry visa for the controlling Italian/Schengen access leg; this route finding does not say that a Vatican instrument imports Italian rules.
conditions: Vatican City is an enclave with an open border adjoining Italy. This records the necessary Italian/Schengen route, not Vatican membership of Schengen or an adoption of Italian law by Vatican City.
A Union citizen needs a valid identity card or passport for Italian entry; no Italian entry visa or equivalent formality applies.

The Lateran Treaty normally leaves St Peter's Square open to the public and reserves public-access regulation to the Holy See. No ordinary public-visitor maximum duration is established by the directly reviewed Vatican sources.
No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources. ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date.

policies.title: EEA and Swiss ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: For a short public visit, these EEA and Swiss travellers use the visa-free Italian/Schengen access leg; this is a route finding, not a claim that Vatican City imports Schengen law.
conditions: The current Schengen Borders Code directly recognises persons exercising free movement under Union law and distinguishes the EU, EEA and CH border lane. This policy records the necessary Italy/Schengen route only.
Vatican City is not a Schengen member. The Lateran Treaty preserves Holy See control of Vatican public access and does not itself enact Italian nationality-visa rules.
No ordinary public-visitor maximum duration is established by the directly reviewed Vatican sources. No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources.
ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date. Residence, family-member, diplomatic, service and special-document rules are outside this ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: Visa-exempt Schengen-access ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access
policies.summary: With the required qualifying document, these visitors are exempt from the Italian/Schengen short-stay visa needed to reach Vatican City; this route finding does not establish a separate Vatican visitor visa.
conditions: The controlled Italian/Schengen short-stay allowance is up to 90 days in any 180-day period; it is not evidence of a separate Vatican visitor-stay maximum.
Biometric ICAO-compliant passports are required for AL, BA, GE, MK, MD, ME, UA and XK. Taiwan requires an identity-card number; HK and MO require the respective named SAR passport.

A valid travel document and the ordinary Italian external-entry conditions remain required. Residence-permit, family-member, refugee/stateless, diplomatic/official/service, minor and other document-specific rules are not flattened into this nationality baseline.
No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources. ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date.

policies.title: Schengen-visa-required ordinary passports: visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: These ordinary passports need the advance Italian/Schengen visa required for the access route through Italy; the route finding neither calls it a Vatican visa nor says Vatican law imports Italian rules.
conditions: This is the advance Italian/Schengen visa for the access route through Italy, not a Vatican visa. Vatican public access remains subject to Holy See controls.
For the Italian access leg, the ordinary travel document must normally remain valid three months after planned Schengen departure, have been issued within ten years and have two free pages.

The Schengen short-stay limit is up to 90 days in any 180-day period. It does not establish a Vatican local visitor-stay maximum; no such ordinary visitor duration was found in the reviewed direct Vatican material.

No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources. ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date. Residence, family-member, minor, diplomatic/official/service, refugee/stateless and other special-document exceptions remain outside this ordinary-passport nationality baseline.

policies.title: Ukrainian ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Ukrainian ordinary-passport traveller is classified as citizenship, not as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: This is a narrow catalogue home classification. Martial-law restrictions, military records, dual nationality, residence, work and special-document rules are outside the ordinary foreign-visitor baseline.

policies.title: Djiboutian ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A traveller using a Djiboutian ordinary passport is classified as citizenship rather than under the foreign-visitor visa rules.
conditions: The published Nationality Code distinguishes Djiboutian nationals from foreigners. This is a narrow citizenship classification, not a finding about any particular passport, residence, diplomatic, service or special-document procedure.

policies.title: Comorian ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A traveller using a Comorian ordinary passport is classified as a Comorian citizen rather than as a foreign visitor under the foreigner-entry visa regime.
conditions: This is a narrow catalogue home-country classification: the foreigner-entry law applies to people of foreign nationality, while the Nationality Code determines Comorian nationality.
It does not establish treatment for a dual national presenting another passport, or for work, residence, transit, special passports, document validity, public-order controls or final admission.

policies.title: Chinese ordinary passports: visa-free tourist entry
policies.summary: Cuba Travel expressly exempts Chinese nationals using regular passports from the tourist-visa requirement.
conditions: This is limited to Chinese nationals using regular passports for the ordinary short-tourist baseline. Cuba Travel states a tourist may stay up to 90 days, extendable once for 90 more days.

A valid passport, D’VIAJEROS QR code, medical insurance, transport and final admission requirements remain applicable. Work, residence, transit, special passports and individual restrictions are outside this policy.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: visa-free stays up to 90 days
policies.summary: Russia’s current Foreign Ministry consular guidance says Russian citizens may enter Cuba without a visa for a stay not exceeding 90 days using a foreign passport.
conditions: The cited bilateral-consular guidance limits visa-free travel to stays not exceeding 90 days. Longer stays, residence, employment and commercial activity require a Cuban Embassy visa.

This treats the Russian foreign passport as the ordinary-passport baseline; it does not establish special documents, dual-citizenship treatment, entry conditions, public-order controls or final admission.

policies.title: Serbian ordinary passports: electronic tourist visa required
policies.summary: Serbia’s current Foreign Ministry advisory says national passports require a Cuban visa through eVisaCuba; Cuba’s official tourism portal confirms the electronic tourist visa is issued by internet and sent as a visa code.
conditions: The Serbian MFA expressly distinguishes national passports, which require a visa, from diplomatic and official passports, which have a separate waiver.

Cuba Travel describes the issued eVisa code and states the tourist visa is single-entry for up to 90 days, extendable once for 90 more days. A valid passport, return ticket, D’VIAJEROS QR code, insurance and final admission remain required.
This is a tourist route only and does not cover work, residence, transit, emergency, diplomatic, official, service or special-document treatment.

application.label: eVisa-Cuba tourist visa portal
application.processingTime: Cuba Travel describes issuance of a visa code by email; the Serbian MFA directs national-passport applicants to the web route.
steps: Confirm that the journey is an ordinary tourist visit and that all passport and travel conditions are met.
Apply through the eVisa-Cuba route identified by Cuban and Serbian official guidance.
Use the issued visa code with the required D’VIAJEROS entry form and travel documents when seeking entry.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: Haiti visa-free tourist entry
policies.summary: The Embassy’s live tourist-visa page says tourists generally do not need a visa, then directly names nine nationality exceptions. This policy covers every other foreign ordinary passport in the catalog. The stated USD 10 airport fee is not visa-on-arrival or electronic issuance.
conditions: Applies only to tourist visits on an ordinary passport, excluding the nine nationalities named in the Embassy’s advance-visa exception list. The Embassy says the passport must be valid for at least six months.
The Embassy says a USD 10 fee is payable on arrival at the airport, while expressly saying no visa is needed. This fee is not normalized as visa-on-arrival.
DIE’s 2026 IKAT is a digital embarkation/debarkation declaration, not electronic visa issuance, an ETA, or evidence of a visa requirement. The source does not state one uniform visa-free duration.

Final admission and rules for work, residence, transit, diplomatic or official passports, special documents, public health, security, and any nationality-specific prohibitions are outside this tourist ordinary-passport classification.

policies.title: Nine named foreign ordinary passports: Haiti tourist advance visa
policies.summary: The Embassy directly names these nine nationalities as requiring a visa to enter Haiti and says they must apply at least one month before departure. The cited process is consular advance processing, not an eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: Applies to tourist travel on an ordinary passport. The Embassy says applicants must apply for a visa at least one month before departure and that the passport must be valid for at least six months.

The direct three-language exception list includes Yemen. A later parenthetical sentence calls the cohort nine countries but inadvertently omits Yemen; the direct repeated named exception list controls, and this should be rechecked when Haiti publishes a dated schedule.
This classification does not establish a uniform stay duration or address work, residence, transit, diplomatic or official passports, special documents, public health, security, or final admission.

policies.title: Haitian citizen ordinary passport: home entry
policies.summary: DIE states that the Government issues a Haitian passport to its nationals after proof of Haitian citizenship. This supports the catalog’s Haitian-citizenship home-entry classification, not a foreign-visitor visa rule.
conditions: Applies only to a Haitian national travelling on a Haitian ordinary passport. Citizenship, identity-document, carrier and border-admission requirements remain governed by Haitian law and practice.

policies.title: Saint Kitts and Nevis ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A Saint Kitts and Nevis citizen is classified as citizenship rather than a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: Immigration Act section 4 grants a citizen a right to enter at any time. This is not a finding about residence, work, diplomatic, emergency, or special-document processing.

policies.title: OECS Protocol Member ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: The five other catalog OECS Protocol Member State citizens have the statutory indefinite-entry permit; the eTA release confirms they need not apply for an eTA.
conditions: Immigration Act section 4(3), subject to statutory prohibited-person procedures, requires an immigration officer to grant an indefinite-entry permit to a Protocol Member State citizen.

The 2025 eTA release says OECS citizens need not apply for eTA, but they must complete the electronic Immigration and Customs declaration. This does not establish ordinary tourist treatment for non-Protocol CARICOM citizens, residents, diplomats, crew, transit, work, or special documents.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Saint-Martin Annex II directly lists these ordinary passports as visa-exempt for an ordinary short visit; all have the normal 90-days-in-180-days ceiling unless the schedule states a narrower rule.
conditions: For a visitor stay not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period, except where the current Annex II gives a more favourable or narrower passport-specific limit. The listed 15-day Saint Lucia rule is separated below.

For AU, BR, JP, KR, MX, SG and US, the Annex II waiver does not cover a remunerated activity where French law requires a work authorisation and it is not produced. This candidate is limited to the ordinary short-visitor purpose.

For GB, this reflects the ordinary British Citizen passport baseline. The Annex II separately limits certain other British-nationality labels; special passports, residence/long-stay-visa waivers, crew and cruise exceptions, transit, public-order restrictions and final admission are not normalized here.

MF denotes Saint Martin (French part), a French overseas collectivity. This is not a Schengen-visa classification, and the table does not establish any electronic visa or routine visa-on-arrival issuance.

policies.title: Biometric ordinary passports: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Saint-Martin Annex II limits the ordinary-passport waiver for these states to biometric passports.
conditions: Only an ordinary biometric passport qualifies. The current Annex II also excludes Serbian passports issued by the Serbian Coordination Directorate from the Serbian waiver.

The ordinary short-visitor waiver is up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Work, residence, transit, special passports, residence-document waivers, entry prohibitions and final admission remain outside this policy.

policies.title: Taiwan ordinary passports with identity-card number: visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Annex II limits Taiwan's ordinary-passport waiver to passports that contain an identity-card number.
conditions: The passport must have been issued by Taiwan and contain an identity-card number. The waiver is for an ordinary visitor stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
This does not normalize other Taiwan travel documents, work, residence, transit, special passports, entry prohibitions or final admission.

policies.title: Saint Lucia ordinary passports: limited visa-free short visitor entry
policies.summary: The current Annex II gives Saint Lucia ordinary passports a specific shorter visa-free allowance.
conditions: Visa-free visits are limited to 15 days or less, with no more than 120 cumulative days in a 12-month period; this overrides the general 90-days-in-180-days framing.
Work, residence, transit, special passports, entry prohibitions and final admission remain outside this ordinary-passport visitor policy.

policies.title: Unlisted ordinary passports: advance territorial visa required
policies.summary: For the listed ordinary passports, the current order requires a valid French visa because they are neither free-movement beneficiaries nor ordinary-passport entries in the exhaustive Saint-Martin Annex II waiver list.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport, short-visitor baseline: the order requires a valid French visa where the Annex II waiver does not apply. The territorial visa is a French visa sticker bearing the collectivity for which it is valid, not an eVisa or standard visa on arrival.

A qualifying current French or fully Schengen-applying-state residence permit or long-stay visa can independently waive the Saint-Martin visa for up to 90 days in 180; that document-conditioned route is deliberately not normalized into these passport rows.

The Annex II has narrow pre-existing-French-visa, old-Vanuatu-passport, cruise, crew, transit, exceptional border-visa and special/diplomatic-passport exceptions. These do not change the unconditioned ordinary short-visitor baseline. A border visa is exceptional, requires unforeseeable imperative entry and may be valid no more than 15 days. Final admission remains for border authorities.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: pre-entry visa required
policies.summary: The Ministry of National Security's live notice expressly identifies twelve passport nationalities for which a visa is required for entry, including Bangladesh and Nepal, and directs use of its new visa-application platform.
conditions: Applies to the listed nationalities' ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline; the notice does not establish treatment for diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency, stateless, residence or other special documents.

The Ministry requires a pre-entry visa application and identifies supporting evidence, including passport bio page, photograph, sponsor letter, police certificate, financial evidence and, where applicable, accommodation, charter and itinerary evidence.

The online Ministry service accepts an application, documents and payment. The reviewed official sources do not say that the entry visa itself is issued electronically, so this is not normalized as eVisa.
Final admission, visitor-permit duration, extension, onward travel, funds, purpose, security and other immigration controls remain separate from the pre-entry visa requirement.

application.label: Ministry of National Security Entry Visa Applications
steps: Open the Ministry's Entry Visa Applications service.
Provide an accessible email address to begin the application.
Upload the stated supporting documents and pay the stated application fee online.

policies.title: American Samoa: Samoa ordinary passports, 10-day visitor permit
policies.summary: The current territorial code and official portal create a Samoa-passport Entry Permit Waiver Program route requiring a pre-travel visitor permit.
conditions: The specific Samoa route is limited to 10 days, has a $10 fee and a monthly maximum of 400 citizens. The candidate concerns ordinary passports, not the alternative identity-document route.

The official portal requires online application/payment. The EPWP requires pre-travel documents and OK-to-Board authorization; work, residence, transit, special documents and final admission are excluded.

application.label: American Samoa Samoa 10-day visitor permit
steps: Apply and pay online before travel.
Obtain the territorial authorization required for the EPWP route.
Present required documents to Immigration when seeking entry.

policies.title: U.S. ordinary passports: no foreign-visitor visa for the U.S. territories
policies.summary: A U.S. citizen or national is not an alien for federal immigration law; American Samoa also gives U.S. citizens a document route rather than a foreign visitor permit.
conditions: This is normalized as visa_free because the destinations are territorial codes, not the sovereign United States. American Samoa’s current page specifies documentary requirements for non-resident U.S. citizens.
Residence, identity-document alternatives, military orders, emergency waivers, inspection and final admission are not normalized.

policies.title: Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands: Canadian, Compact and U.S. ordinary passports
policies.summary: Federal law explicitly removes the visitor visa requirement for Canadian citizens and eligible FSM/RMI/Palau Compact citizens; U.S. passport holders are not aliens.
conditions: For Canada, the exemption is for Canadian citizens, not Canadian permanent residents; E, K, S and V classifications are excluded.

For FM, MH and PW, this is an eligible Compact-citizen route, not one for every country-issued document. RMI citizenship/acquisition, passport-sale and adoption exclusions; FSM spouse/child exclusions; and Palau official-passport conditions remain material.
Inspection, admissibility, work, residence, crew, transit, official/special documents and final admission remain outside these visitor baseline policies.

policies.title: Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands: explicit residual visitor-visa baseline
policies.summary: The federal documentary regulation expressly requires a valid visa of each arriving nonimmigrant alien except its stated classes; this cohort is outside the U.S., Canadian, Compact and VWP cohorts.
conditions: This ordinary short-visitor baseline requires a valid unexpired U.S. nonimmigrant visa and passport. A qualifying residence, special document, crew, transit, emergency waiver or individual immigration classification is not normalized into passport-wide access.
No eVisa, routine visa-on-arrival or universal electronic authorization is established. Consular issuance and final CBP admission remain required.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: Canadian, Compact and U.S. ordinary passports
policies.summary: Federal law explicitly gives Canadian citizens and eligible FSM/RMI/Palau Compact citizens no-visa treatment; a U.S. passport holder is not an alien.
conditions: For Canada, the exemption is for Canadian citizens, not Canadian permanent residents; E, K, S and V classifications are excluded.

For FM, MH and PW, this is an eligible Compact-citizen route, not one for every country-issued document. RMI citizenship/acquisition, passport-sale and adoption exclusions; FSM spouse/child exclusions; and Palau official-passport conditions remain material.
Inspection, admissibility, work, residence, crew, transit, official/special documents and final admission remain outside these visitor baseline policies.

policies.title: Federal territories: Bahamian preclearance visitor no-visa route
policies.summary: The federal regulation creates a route-conditioned visitor no-visa exception for Bahamian nationals inspected by a U.S. immigration officer in the Bahamas before or at embarkation.
conditions: A passport is required. Before or at embarkation on a vessel or aircraft, the traveller must satisfy the examining U.S. immigration officer in the Bahamas that they are clearly and beyond doubt otherwise admissible.
This is not an unqualified waiver: other origins, travel modes, work, residence, transit and final admission remain outside the policy.

policies.title: Guam: explicit residual visitor-visa baseline
policies.summary: The current federal documentary regulation expressly requires a valid visa unless a named exception applies; this cohort is outside Guam’s federal no-visa, VWP/ESTA and G-CNMI passport cohorts.
conditions: This ordinary short-visitor baseline requires a valid unexpired U.S. nonimmigrant visa and passport. Qualifying residence, special-document, crew, transit, emergency-waiver and individual immigration routes are not normalized.
No eVisa, routine visa-on-arrival or universal electronic authorization is established. Consular issuance and final CBP admission remain required.

policies.title: Northern Mariana Islands: explicit residual visitor-visa baseline
policies.summary: The current federal documentary regulation expressly requires a valid visa unless a named exception applies; this cohort is outside CNMI’s federal no-visa, VWP/ESTA, G-CNMI and EVS-TAP passport cohorts.
conditions: This ordinary short-visitor baseline requires a valid unexpired U.S. nonimmigrant visa and passport. Qualifying residence, special-document, crew, transit, emergency-waiver and individual immigration routes are not normalized.
No eVisa, routine visa-on-arrival or universal electronic authorization is established. Consular issuance and final CBP admission remain required.

policies.title: CA-4 Category A ordinary passports: visa-free Honduras entry
policies.summary: The current COCESNA CA-4 eAIP defines Category A as visa-exempt for ordinary passports travelling to Honduras. This policy includes the current listed Category A passports after applying directly stated Honduras-specific changes for Bolivia, Ecuador, Latvia, Taiwan and the United Kingdom.
conditions: Applies only to ordinary passports in the stated CA-4 Category A baseline; it does not flatten diplomatic, official, service, residence, refugee, stateless, provisional or special-document treatment.

The category schedule's Honduras observations control the mapped deviations: Bolivia and Ecuador are Category A; Latvia is Category B. Taiwan is included in Category A by the current common CA-4 schedule.

A tourist normally receives up to 90 days at entry and may seek a 30-day extension. A valid passport, onward or continuing ticket, migration form, funds, purpose, lodging, health and individual-admissibility requirements apply.
CA-4 resident, qualifying third-country visa/residence and other special exceptions are conditional and not a nationality-wide substitute for this baseline.

policies.title: CA-4 Category B/C ordinary passports: advance Honduran visa required
policies.summary: The current CA-4 eAIP places these ordinary passports in Category B (consular) or C (consulted). Both require advance visa processing for the unconditional ordinary-passport baseline, so both normalize to visa_required rather than eVisa, ETA or visa on arrival.
conditions: Category B is an advance consular visa: INM says it is affixed to the passport and delivered at the personal, in-person appointment. Category C requires prior written INM validation before the applicant proceeds at a Honduran consulate.
The Category B/C grouping is only a normalized outcome; it does not erase the consulted-visa authorization, sponsor, documentary, fee, purpose or consular requirements that vary by category.

The current schedule's Honduras observations place Latvia and the Dominican Republic in Category B. SRE's current index separately records the United Kingdom ordinary-passport consular-visa rule and the Jordanian and Palestinian ordinary-passport Category B rules.

A Category B visitor with a qualifying United States, Canadian or Exchange visa, or qualifying Category-A-country residence, may receive Category A treatment; a Category C visitor with stated qualifying documents may be reduced only to Category B. These are conditional document exceptions, not nationality baselines.

CA-4 residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless and special-document cases remain outside this ordinary-passport visitor classification. Final admission remains with migration authorities.

policies.title: Benin: ordinary foreign visitor eVisa residual
policies.summary: Foreign ordinary-passport visitors outside ECOWAS and without an MFA-listed ordinary/national-passport waiver must obtain Benin’s tourist/visit eVisa online before arrival. This exact residual excludes the 39 current waiver rows and Beninese citizenship.
conditions: DEI states that the tourist/visit eVisa is for family, professional, health or tourist stays not exceeding 90 days; it is renewable for the same duration.
DEI states that it is issued to foreign nationals outside ECOWAS or without a Benin visa-exemption agreement, obtained online via evisa.bj, and held before arrival.

The three current MFA agreement-register endpoints supply the exact ordinary/national-passport exemption roster excluded from this residual. The API is intermittently slow; its successful 2026-08-21 responses should be independently rechecked before promotion.

This does not establish work, study, business, transit, residence, cruise, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, special-document, health, passport-validity, public-order, security, prior-history or final-admission treatment.

application.label: Benin official eVisa application workflow
application.processingTime: The official sources reviewed do not publish a universal decision-time commitment.
steps: Initiate the eVisa request online with email address and passport-document details.
Confirm the emailed link, complete personal, eVisa, travel and passport forms, then pay online.
Check the request status using the issued application number and hold the eVisa before travel.

policies.title: Suriname: ordinary passports outside the named 21-country exception visa-free for tourism or family visits
policies.summary: The Government established unilateral visa abolition for all foreign nationalities for tourist or family visits, while current Ministry guidance names an exhaustive 21-country exception from 1 May 2023. The remaining catalog foreign ordinary-passport rows are therefore visa-free under that stated general rule and closed exception.
conditions: This policy applies only to foreign ordinary passports outside the current named 21-country exception and only to tourism or family visits, for a maximum stay of 90 days.

The 2022 general rule expressly covered all foreign nationalities; the current Ministry page identifies the precise nationalities for which it ceased to apply from 1 May 2023. No rule is inferred merely from omission.

The Entry Fee is a separate fee/voucher mechanism, not an ETA, eVisa, visa on arrival or visa-free exception. The Ministry says its PDF voucher is electronically sent after online payment; that issuance concerns the fee only.

Business, internship, work, residence, PSA, transit, diplomatic, service, special, official, international-organization and third-country-document routes are outside this ordinary tourist/family baseline. Final admission and other travel-document requirements are not established here.

policies.title: Suriname: 21 named ordinary-passport nationalities subject to visa requirement
policies.summary: Current Government guidance identifies these 21 nationalities as excluded from unilateral visa abolition from 1 May 2023, and BIBIS confirms their visa requirement was reinstated. This is a visa-required baseline, not a visa-on-arrival policy or a finding of electronically issued visas.
conditions: The Government directly names this closed 21-nationality cohort as excluded from unilateral visa abolition from 1 May 2023; BIBIS confirms the visa requirement was reinstated for the 21 countries.

The Government’s E-Visa directory and BIBIS explanation establish an authorized online application service, but the opened official workflow does not state that a final ordinary visitor visa for this whole cohort is issued electronically. It is consequently normalized as visa_required, not evisa.
No visa-on-arrival route is stated. The separate Government Entry Fee voucher is not treated as a visa, ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival status, and does not displace the visa requirement.

For Cuba, Dominican Republic and Venezuela, BIBIS says a tourist card was reintroduced alongside the visa for tourist, business and short-stay travel. This alternate document is retained as a condition, not a separate normalized status.

No visa duration, entries, extension, port, admission result, health, funds or onward-travel condition is inferred. Residence, PSA, transit, CARICOM, diplomatic, service, special, official, international-organization, business, work and third-country-document exceptions are outside this ordinary visitor baseline.

policies.title: Suriname nationals entering Suriname
policies.summary: The Surinamese civil-registration authority identifies the national passport and expressly ties emergency-passport eligibility to Surinamese nationality. This records the catalog home-nationality relationship, not a foreign visitor permission.
conditions: This is the citizenship/home relationship for a Surinamese national ordinary passport, not a finding about visa-free visitor admission or a substitute for travel-document, exit, criminal, health or final-entry rules.

policies.title: Bermuda: unlisted nationals visa-free for bona fide short visits
policies.summary: Section 28 of the Bermuda Immigration and Protection Act removes the need for specific permission for a bona fide visitor who fulfils its conditions. Order No. 2 of 2025 supplies the exhaustive nationality exception by prohibiting only the named Schedule nationals. The resulting unlisted ordinary-passport baseline is visa-free, not an ETA, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: This is limited to a bona fide ordinary-passport short visitor whose nationality is not in the current Order No. 2 Schedule; it does not cover special passports, residence, work, study, crew, transit, or individual permission routes.

Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport rows follow the Order's express asterisk incorporation: the current UK Immigration Rules exempt PRC nationals holding those specific passports from the visa-national rule.
At landing and throughout the visit, the visitor must not be an exceptionable person and must hold a passenger ticket for departure to a country where the visitor has a right of entry.
The unrestricted period is six months or 180 days, whichever is greater, within a 12-month period, but the Minister may shorten or end it by written notice.
This statutory exemption from specific permission does not guarantee admission; other Immigration Act requirements and final border assessment remain applicable.

policies.title: Bermuda: Schedule nationals require qualifying third-country travel authorization
policies.summary: Order No. 2 of 2025 prohibits the named Schedule nationals from entering Bermuda unless they have qualifying current Canadian, UK or US travel authorization or a narrow Bermuda Government spouse/belongs letter. For the ordinary-passport baseline without either condition, this is normalized as visa-required; it is not a Bermuda eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: This visa-required classification is the passport-only baseline: the Order requires advance qualifying travel authorization to enter and re-enter Canada, the United Kingdom, or the United States, valid for 45 days after intended Bermuda departure.

The official Immigration guidance describes that document as a UK, US, or Canadian multi-re-entry visa; the binding Order uses the broader term travel authorization. Neither source establishes a Bermuda-issued eVisa or visa-on-arrival for this cohort.

The Department's corroborative guidance additionally requires both the MRV and passport to remain valid for 45 days after the visitor stay expires. This enforcement wording is retained separately from the controlling Order's intended-departure language.

The asterisk incorporates current UK exceptions. Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports are mapped separately as visa-free; a Taiwan passport qualifies only when it contains the competent authority's identity-card number, so the broader TW issuer row retains the passport-only visa-required baseline.
A current Bermuda Government letter attesting that the person is a Bermudian spouse or belongs to Bermuda is a separate narrow exception and is excluded from this nationality-only visitor policy.
The double-asterisk Cuba, Haiti, Ukraine and Venezuela standard-work-permit landing exception and all work, residence, special-document, transit and individual-permission routes are excluded.
Even after the Order condition is met, the bona fide visitor requirements, duration limit, exceptionable-person rule and final admission assessment under the Immigration Act remain applicable.

policies.title: Bolivian ordinary passport: citizenship/home entry
policies.summary: Article 21 of the current Constitution gives Bolivians freedom of residence, permanence and movement in Bolivian territory, expressly including entry into the country. This supports the home/citizenship normalization.
conditions: This is a Bolivian ordinary-passport citizenship/home-entry normalization, not a visitor-visa, residence, dual-nationality, emergency-document, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless or other special-document rule.
Migration registration/control and lawful identity or travel-document requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Group I ordinary passports: visa-free tourism or visit
policies.summary: The live Ministry country API assigns 54 mapped catalog nationalities to Group I. Later official measures override stale API rows for Honduras, Israel, El Salvador, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; the resulting 58 named ordinary passports are visa-free for tourism or visits.
conditions: The scope is tourism or visit only, without a residence purpose. The source does not establish a nationality-wide ETA, eVisa, or visa-on-arrival requirement for this group.

Honduras follows the bilateral tourist/visit visa suppression effective 17 March 2024; El Salvador the ordinary-passport agreement effective 21 June 2024; the Dominican Republic its waiver effective 2 September 2024; and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines its agreement effective 11 November 2021.

The 1 December 2025 announcement controls South Korea, South Africa, Bulgaria, Malta, Romania, United Arab Emirates, Israel and United States. The API has not updated Israel and is not followed for that older Group III value.

Passport/document validity, identity, admission screening, health evidence where applicable, stay, purpose, extension and other migration conditions remain outside this nationality baseline. Diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless and other special documents are excluded.

policies.title: Group II ordinary passports: tourist/visit visa or qualifying entry authorization
policies.summary: The current Ministry country API assigns these 100 unambiguously mapped catalog nationalities to Group II. Current law requires a tourism/visit visa or a DIGEMIG tourist/visit entry authorization. Neither route is an electronically issued visa or an unconditional passport-wide visa on arrival.
conditions: Current law requires a Group II tourism/visit visa or a DIGEMIG tourist/visit entry authorization. The official portal is an application system, while the Ministry describes the visa itself as issued by consulates and embassies; neither source establishes electronic visa issuance.

DIGEMIG may issue the alternate authorization at a land or airport border, or exceptionally at an office, when the traveller could not access a Bolivian mission. It requires the same evidence and procedures as a visa and is not an unconditional nationality-wide visa-on-arrival route.

Applicants must meet the Ministry’s stated requirements, including ordinarily a valid passport, application declaration, itinerary/return travel, invitation or accommodation, means, photograph and yellow-fever evidence where applicable. Admission remains subject to control.
No residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, special-document or third-country-document route is normalized.

policies.title: Group III ordinary passports: tourist/visit visa with prior DIGEMIG verification
policies.summary: The current Ministry country API assigns these 18 unambiguously mapped catalog nationalities to Group III. The current framework requires a tourism/visit visa after verification and authorization by DIGEMIG; the duplicate contradictory Libya records are left unresolved.
conditions: This is a visa requirement with prior Group III verification and authorization by DIGEMIG. A border-issued authorization is possible only exceptionally after reasoned DIGEMIG authorization, so it is not a nationality-wide visa-on-arrival route and is not normalized as eVisa or ETA.
The Ministry’s electronic service accepts visa applications, but reviewed sources establish consular issuance and do not establish electronic issuance of the visa or electronic permission to board.

The general tourism/visit application requirements and final border-admission control apply. Residence, work, study, transit, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless, special-document and third-country-document rules are excluded.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa waiver plus eTA
policies.summary: The in-force bilateral agreement waives visas for ordinary passports of all current EU Member States except Ireland; the current eTA remains mandatory.
conditions: The bilateral agreement applies to a valid ordinary passport and a non-paid visit of at most three months in a six-month period.
It defines Member State as every EU Member State except Ireland; this current scope includes Croatia and excludes no other current member.
An approved eTA is required before travel under the operational eTA system; admission remains discretionary and the eTA is not an eVisa.

policies.title: Russian and Ukrainian ordinary passports: visa waiver plus eTA
policies.summary: Current official foreign-ministry records establish visa-free entry for Russian and Ukrainian ordinary passports; the operational eTA remains mandatory.
conditions: Russia: the current Russian MFA table gives Russian citizens visa-free travel for 90 days in each 180 days.
Ukraine: the current Ukrainian MFA country profile identifies the reciprocal waiver agreement and its 27 January 2017 entry into force.
Both remain subject to approved eTA before travel, the ED declaration, document validity, prohibited-person rules, and immigration-officer admission.

policies.title: Ordinary passports outside the statutory visa-national schedule
policies.summary: The 2025 Ordinance replaces the visa schedule and subjects passports issued by its listed countries and territories to a visa requirement. For the ordinary-passport nationalities omitted from that exhaustive passport-nationality schedule, no visitor visa is required; a separate visitor permit remains mandatory for admission.
conditions: This is a visa exemption only: every ordinary short visitor remains subject to a visitor permit and the Immigration Officer's admission decision.
A visitor permit is normally stamped and applied for on arrival; it is not a visa on arrival or an electronic travel authorisation.
A permit issued without referral is normally valid for up to one month; longer stays require the published advance/referral process.
Visitors must show onward travel or funds, booked accommodation, sufficient funds, and medical-evacuation insurance; visitor-permit holders may not take employment.
This nationality baseline does not displace the statute's separate transit, emergency, UN travel-document, permit-holder, right-of-abode, watch-list, document, purpose, or individual-admission rules.

policies.title: Kazakhstan ordinary passport: Turkmenistan visa required
policies.summary: Kazakhstan MFA’s current passport-type table marks Turkmenistan as “visa” for an ordinary Kazakhstan passport, consistent with Turkmenistan’s statutory foreign-visitor visa baseline.
conditions: This normalization does not cover work, transit, diplomatic/service passports, residence-based entry or any local border arrangement.
Visa issuance and final admission remain subject to the competent Turkmen authorities and required documents.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passport: Turkmenistan visa required
policies.summary: Russia MFA’s current passport-type table records that a Russian ordinary passport requires a visa for Turkmenistan; the cited bilateral agreement is limited to the listed visa-free passport class.
conditions: This maps only ordinary passports for a short visitor purpose. It excludes diplomatic/service passports, residence/document exemptions, work, transit and individual admission decisions.

Turkmenistan’s current law provides that visa/eVisa is unnecessary where its international treaties provide a waiver; the Russian MFA table identifies the ordinary Russian passport as requiring a visa.
Visa issuance and final admission remain subject to the competent Turkmen authorities and required documents.

policies.title: Türkiye ordinary passport: visa required for Turkmenistan
policies.summary: Türkiye's current Foreign Ministry country notice directly states that ordinary Turkish passport holders are subject to a Turkmenistan visa requirement. The Turkmen Migration Law supplies the destination's visa baseline while preserving treaty exceptions.
conditions: This policy concerns a Turkish ordinary passport travelling for a short visitor purpose. It does not establish a visa-free, eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route.
The separately described 30-day waiver is for service, special and diplomatic passports and requires the stated approval or invitation; it does not alter the ordinary-passport baseline.

Turkmenistan's law provides that foreign entry is visa-based unless an international treaty provides otherwise. Visa issuance, invitation, passport, purpose, registration and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Cuban ordinary passport: Panama stamped visa required
policies.summary: Panama first placed Cuba in the stamped-visa category in 2015. The subsequent Tourist Card route was removed in 2021, and SNM’s 2024 notice still describes the Cuban stamped-visa process.
conditions: This is an advance stamped consular visa, not an eVisa, ETA, visa on arrival, online appointment or Tourist Card. The 2024 notice says the online appointment request was disabled while the process was being addressed; it does not announce a nationality exemption.

The 2017 amendment modifies Article 2 of the 2015 decree. The 2018 Tourist Card and the 2019 stamped-visa procedure form part of the later history; Executive Decree 88 removed use of the Tourist Card in 2021.

The official sources do not provide an accessible consolidated in-force nationality register. The legal chain and the 2024 operational notice support this policy at medium confidence; recheck for later repeal or amendment before promotion.
Third-country visa/residence routes, transit, work, residence, diplomatic/service/special documents and individual admission are outside this ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: Dominican Republic ordinary passport: Panama stamped visa required
policies.summary: Panama’s 2015 stamped-visa classification remains the direct baseline after the later Dominican Tourist Card was removed by Executive Decree 88 in 2021.
conditions: This is an advance stamped consular visa baseline, not an eVisa, ETA, visa on arrival, online appointment or Tourist Card.
The 2017 amendment modifies Article 2 of the 2015 decree. The 2019 Tourist Card was an intervening document route, and Executive Decree 88 removed its use in 2021.

The official sources do not provide an accessible consolidated in-force nationality register or a later Dominican-specific operational notice. This legal sequence supports a medium-confidence correction, with mandatory recheck for later repeal or amendment before promotion.
Third-country visa/residence routes, transit, work, residence, diplomatic/service/special documents and individual admission are outside this ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: Venezuelan ordinary passport: Panama stamped visa required
policies.summary: Executive Decree 77 of 2022 directly requires Venezuelan nationals entering Panama to request a stamped visa at a Panamanian consular office.
conditions: This is an advance stamped consular visa requirement, not an eVisa, ETA, visa on arrival or online filing classification.
The decree directs application at the Panamanian consular office where the traveller is located, under the stated migration procedures.

The official sources do not provide an accessible consolidated in-force nationality register. No later repeal or amendment was identified in the reviewed official sources; recheck remains required before promotion.
Third-country visa/residence routes, transit, work, residence, diplomatic/service/special documents and individual admission are outside this ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: Kazakhstan ordinary passport: Tunisia visa-free up to 90 days
policies.summary: Kazakhstan MFA's current N (ordinary-passport) column expressly records Tunisia as visa-free up to 90 days.
conditions: The cited ordinary-passport table gives a maximum visa-free stay of 90 days; it does not establish residence, employment, study, transit, crew or special-document rights.
The table does not displace destination documentary, health, security, carrier or final-admission requirements.

policies.title: Kazakhstan ordinary passport: Ukraine visa-free up to 90 days
policies.summary: Kazakhstan MFA's current N (ordinary-passport) column expressly records Ukraine as visa-free up to 90 days.
conditions: The cited ordinary-passport table gives a maximum visa-free stay of 90 days; it does not state a rolling-period calculation.
This candidate maps only the ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline. It does not establish treatment for study, work, residence, transit, diplomatic/service or special documents.
Border accessibility, martial-law measures, documentary, security and individual final-admission rules remain outside this nationality visa classification.

policies.title: Turkish ordinary passports: visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Türkiye's current MFA table explicitly records the listed ordinary Turkish passports as visa-free for the stated short visitor scope.
conditions: Syria is visa-free according to the MFA table, but ordinary-passport holders pay a border fee on arrival; the fee is not a visa-on-arrival classification.
Tunisia and Ukraine are visa-free up to 90 days; Bosnia and Herzegovina is visa-free for no more than 90 days in 180; Panama is visa-free for three months.
This does not establish residence, work, special-document, route, security or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: Türkiye ordinary passports: Djibouti eVisa
policies.summary: Türkiye's MFA says ordinary Turkish passport holders are visa-subject and may travel to Djibouti with an eVisa obtained through the named official service.
conditions: The policy is limited to the MFA-described ordinary-passport tourist route; it does not establish visa on arrival, work, residence, transit, or special-document access.
The MFA separately lists service, special and diplomatic passport holders as visa-free for up to 90 days.

application.label: Djibouti official eVisa service
steps: Apply for the eVisa before travel through the official service named by Türkiye's MFA.

policies.title: Türkiye ordinary passports: Comoros and Sudan visa on arrival
policies.summary: Türkiye's current MFA table expressly says that ordinary Turkish passport holders may obtain visas at the border in Comoros and Sudan.
conditions: Comoros: the MFA says ordinary passports are visa-subject and visas can be obtained at border posts.
Sudan: the MFA says ordinary, service and special passport holders are visa-subject and visitors may obtain visas at all Sudanese border posts.
This establishes only the stated short-visitor border-visa route, not eVisa, residence, work, transit, special-document or final-admission treatment.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: Bosnia and Herzegovina visa-free short visit
policies.summary: The current Russian MFA passport-type table records visa-free travel for an ordinary Russian passport to Bosnia and Herzegovina for up to 30 days in 60 days.
conditions: The ordinary-passport table states 'без визы до 30 дней в течение 60 дней' (visa-free up to 30 days in 60 days).
This does not normalize residence, work, transit, special passports, document requirements, individual admission decisions or any separate Bosnia and Herzegovina entry conditions.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: Cuba visa-free short visit
policies.summary: The current Russian MFA passport-type table records visa-free travel for an ordinary Russian passport to Cuba for up to 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The ordinary-passport table states 'без визы до 90 суток в течение 180 дней' (visa-free up to 90 days in 180 days).
This does not alter the existing canonical Cuba-to-Russia policy; it records the outbound Russian-passport relation only and excludes longer stays, work, residence, documents and final admission.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: Panama visa-free short visit
policies.summary: The current Russian MFA passport-type table records visa-free travel for an ordinary Russian passport to Panama for up to 90 days in 180 days.
conditions: The ordinary-passport table states 'без визы до 90 дней в течение 180 дней' (visa-free up to 90 days in 180 days).
This does not normalize residence, work, transit, special passports, document requirements, individual admission decisions or Panama's separate entry conditions.

policies.title: Russian ordinary passports: Tunisia visa-free short visit
policies.summary: The current Russian MFA passport-type table records unilateral visa-free travel for an ordinary Russian passport to Tunisia for up to 90 days.
conditions: The ordinary-passport table states 'без визы до 90 дней' (visa-free up to 90 days) and notes that this is unilateral.
This does not establish treatment for tour-package, residence, work, transit, special-document, document, carrier or final-admission conditions.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: specified visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Current State Department entry guidance establishes visa-free visitor access for the listed destination-specific ordinary U.S. passport scopes.
conditions: Visitor/tourism scope only; work, residence, transit, special-document, dual-nationality and final-admission rules remain outside this classification.
TN: up to 90 days; UA: up to 90 days in 180, with health-insurance and funds requirements; VG: 30 days or less; PA: 180 days; BA: 90 days in six months.
For UA, visa status does not establish border accessibility or override martial-law, carrier, registration, document and security conditions.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: explicitly pre-travel electronic visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance explicitly requires electronic visa approval before arrival for the listed destinations.
conditions: IQ: obtain an e-Visa through the Iraq e-Visa Portal before arrival; distinct KRG entry alternatives do not widen this nationwide classification.
GQ: complete the e-visa application, receive approval before arrival, and carry the printed approval.
Visitor purpose, passport validity, entry-point, special-document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: expressly available arrival visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance expressly describes an arrival-issuance route for the listed destinations, subject to each stated limitation.
conditions: SY: tourist visa may be issued on arrival at Damascus International Airport or at land entry from Lebanon or Jordan; 30-day stay, fee and Israeli-document restrictions apply.
DJ: visitors may apply on arrival; the stated fee is USD 23.
KM: visa is available on arrival and payment is in cash USD or euros.
TM: obtain the required letter of invitation first; then an airport visa route is available at Ashgabat. Registration, purpose, document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: expressly pre-travel visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance expressly requires a visa to be obtained before travel for the listed destinations.
conditions: LY: applications are made at the Libyan embassy in the applicant's country of residence, require MFA approval, and visas are unavailable at the port of entry.
SD: obtain the visa from a Sudanese embassy before arrival; SS and CF: obtain the visa before arrival/travel.
CG: obtain the visa before travel; invitation or hotel-reservation conditions apply.
Visitor purpose, passport validity, invitation, transit, special-document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Tunisia visa-free short visit
policies.summary: FCDO records visa-free Tunisian visits up to 90 days for full British citizen passport holders.
conditions: Limited to a full British citizen passport from the UK and up to 90 days.
Crown Dependency passport holders may need a visa on arrival and are excluded; document, onward-travel, accommodation and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Djibouti tourist visa on arrival
policies.summary: FCDO says full British citizen passport holders can buy a tourist visa on arrival in Djibouti.
conditions: Limited to a full British citizen passport from the UK and the stated tourist route.
Cash payment in US dollars and evidence of onward travel are stated conditions. An online application is also available but is not needed to establish this arrival-issued route.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Iraq electronic visa
policies.summary: FCDO says a full British citizen passport holder must apply before travel through the Government of Iraq e-visa portal.
conditions: The ordinary visitor visa must be applied for through the stated Iraqi government e-visa portal at least 24 hours before travel; FCDO says visit visas on arrival are no longer available for Iraq.
The KRI has a separate e-visa and arrival route that is valid only in the Kurdistan Region and is not this Iraq-wide baseline. Return/onward ticket and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Comoros visa on arrival
policies.summary: FCDO says full British citizen passport holders can buy a Comoros visa on arrival at Hahaya airport or other entry points.
conditions: Limited to a full British citizen passport from the UK and the stated arrival issuance at Hahaya airport or other entry points.
The stated price is 30 euros; transit, document, health, special-passport and final-admission rules are not normalized.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Sudan advance visa
policies.summary: FCDO directs full British citizen passport holders to apply for a Sudanese visa through the Sudanese Embassy.
conditions: The page applies to a full British citizen passport from the UK.
The source identifies an embassy application route. Exit-visa, sponsor, travel-permit, Israeli-travel-document, health, purpose and final-admission conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Ukraine visa-free short visit
policies.summary: FCDO says full British citizen passport holders may enter Ukraine visa-free for up to 90 days in 180 days, continuing until 30 January 2027.
conditions: Limited to a full British citizen passport from the UK and visits of up to 90 days in 180 days; FCDO says Ukraine confirmed continuation until 30 January 2027.
Martial-law border accessibility, non-government-controlled-area permits, residence, work, document, security and final-admission rules remain separate.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: British Virgin Islands visa-free short visit
policies.summary: FCDO says a full British citizen passport holder from the UK may visit BVI visa-free for up to one month.
conditions: This is confined to the catalog's GB full British citizen passport from the UK; it is not a rule for every British nationality, Crown Dependency passport or BVI belonger status.
The one-month arrival entry stamp is not a visa on arrival. Extensions, work, residence, online embarkation card, document and final-admission conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Cuba tourist electronic visa
policies.summary: FCDO says a full British citizen passport holder may obtain Cuba's tourist electronic visa, which is linked to the applicant's passport.
conditions: A tourist visa is required before travel. FCDO says the electronic-visa is linked to the passport after approval and a code is entered in the D'Viajeros process.
A paper tourist visa route also exists. Onward/return travel, the D'Viajeros arrival form, tourism purpose, document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Panama visa-free land or air short visit
policies.summary: FCDO says a full British citizen passport holder can visit Panama visa-free for up to three months when arriving by land or air.
conditions: Limited to a full British citizen passport from the UK, land or air arrival, and a visit of up to three months.
Sea arrivals other than cruise ships require a visa; cruise/Panama Canal and over-three-month rules are separately qualified. Immigration discretion and final admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Bosnia and Herzegovina visa-free short visit
policies.summary: FCDO records visa-free travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina for a full British citizen passport for up to 90 days in six months.
conditions: Limited to tourist, family/friends, business-meeting, cultural/sport, short-study or training visits and up to 90 days in six months.
Residence, other travel purposes, entry/exit stamp, document and final-admission requirements remain separate.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Turkmenistan sponsored visa on arrival
policies.summary: FCDO says a full British citizen passport holder may purchase a Turkmenistan visa on arrival after obtaining a letter of invitation.
conditions: A letter of invitation is mandatory before travel; for tourist visits, authorised travel agents can provide it.

The stated arrival route is at Ashgabat International Airport and some land borders, with current land-border details to be checked with the sponsor. It does not normalize transit visas, work, purpose, sponsor, entry point or final-admission conditions.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Central African Republic advance visa
policies.summary: FCDO directs full British citizen passport holders to apply through the Central African Republic Embassy in Paris.
conditions: The page applies to a full British citizen passport from the UK.
This is an embassy application route; requirements may change and health, transport, purpose, document and final-admission conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Gabon advance visa
policies.summary: FCDO says a full British citizen passport holder must apply for a Gabon visa before travelling.
conditions: The page applies to a full British citizen passport from the UK and explicitly requires application before travel.
Business invitation, tourist accommodation, yellow-fever, document and final-admission conditions remain separate.

policies.title: Full British citizen passport: Equatorial Guinea online pre-approval and arrival-issued visa
policies.summary: FCDO describes an online application whose e-visa letter is presented on arrival and the visa is issued by border officials.
conditions: This is not classified as an electronically issued visa: FCDO says the applicant prints the online e-visa letter and border officials issue the visa on arrival.
A physical embassy route is also available. Processing, passport-stamp, yellow-fever, purpose, document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Canadian ordinary passports: named visa-free visitor routes
